articles.title: El Niño takes toll on Bukidnon rice farms
articles.summary: VALENCIA CITY, Bukidnon — Hundreds of hectares of rice fields in this major agricultural hub have been affected by below-normal rainfall, prompting the National Irrigation Administration (NIA) to…

blocks.text: VALENCIA CITY, Bukidnon — Hundreds of hectares of rice fields in this major agricultural hub have been affected by below-normal rainfall, prompting the National Irrigation Administration (NIA) to implement scheduled water deliveries.

Valencia City spans a total physical agricultural area of over 10,000 hectares, consisting of 9,862 hectares of irrigated land, 990 hectares of rainfed farms, and 19 hectares of upland fields dedicated to local consumption located in Pantaron, Barangay Banlag.

Adonis Torres, monitoring personnel of the City Agriculture Office, told the Inquirer on Thursday, September 3, that the dry spell has severely impacted both rainfed and downstream agricultural areas.

In Sitio Bantal, Barangay Banlag—which covers over 300 hectares of rainfed rice fields—about 80 percent of the crops have struggled to transition from the vegetative to the reproductive stage due to a severe lack of water.
Torres noted that farmers have exhausted all options, including water pumps, as local water sources have dried up.
While NIA has installed solar-powered pumps in areas like Barangay Laligan, Lumbayao, Lumbo, and upper Kabolooan and Boyog in Barangay Banlag, officials said the supply remains insufficient.
In Lumbayao and Lumbio, solar pumps are still being monitored as farms heavily rely on rainfall.

Meanwhile, areas near rivers like Banlag still have some water supply and remain in the vegetative stage at 70 to 80 percent, but officials warn these crops are not guaranteed to survive if the rivers dry up amid continuous below-normal rainfall.
Conversely, areas with sufficient NIA irrigation, particularly in Laligan, have largely completed harvesting with minimal worries, while downstream areas bear the brunt of the shortage.

For corn crops, Torres reported that while most have already been harvested, ears were notably smaller due to extreme heat and below-normal rains experienced as early as mid-April, affecting around 50 to 100 hectares.
Additionally, about thee hectares of four-month ginger gardens have been affected by the dry conditions.

The agricultural strain comes in the wake of an advisory issued by the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) on September 1, warning of unusually high temperatures and a moderate-to-strong El Niño across Mindanao.

Climate models indicate the phenomenon could strengthen toward late 2026 and persist into the first half of 2027, prompting local authorities to initiate water conservation and drought-mitigation measures.
The City Government of Valencia and relevant local departments are continuing monitoring efforts to assist affected farmers as dry conditions persist. /mr

articles.title: NU-MOA: Bomb threat in Pasay campus was a ‘hoax’
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The National University–Mall of Asia (NU-MOA) in Pasay City said authorities have determined that the alleged bomb threat in its campus early Thursday was a hoax. According to…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The National University–Mall of Asia (NU-MOA) in Pasay City said authorities have determined that the alleged bomb threat in its campus early Thursday was a hoax.
According to the NU-MOA, its premises have been “cleared and deemed safe,” and no explosive or hazardous materials were found after an inspection by the Pasay City authorities.

Personnel from the PNP MOA Substation K9 unit, Pasay Investigation Division, and the Pasay Bureau of Fire Protection swept the area following the security threat at around 7:50 a.m., the university said.
Meanwhile, afternoon classes resumed. Its morning classes were temporarily held through remote learning modes due to the incident.

“While afternoon classes are expected to resume, we assure our students, faculty, employees, parents and the entire NU community that your safety and security remain our highest priority,” the NU-MOA said earlier.
The NU-MOA urged the public to refrain from spreading unverified information regarding the incident.
It added that announcements or advisories will be posted in its official pages.
“A cyber investigation is underway in coordination with the appropriate offices to trace and verify the source of the threat,” it added. /apl

articles.title: Tarlac lawmaker says she sought funds for collapsed bridges
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Tarlac Rep. Maria Cristina Angeles said Thursday that she had long sought government funding to strengthen two bridges that recently collapsed due to heavy rains and strong…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Tarlac Rep. Maria Cristina Angeles said Thursday that she had long sought government funding to strengthen two bridges that recently collapsed due to heavy rains and strong river currents.
Angeles said she had asked the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) to address concerns over the foundations of the two bridges even when she was still a mayor.
She was referring to the 136-meter-long Agana Bridge, which collapsed over the weekend, and the 720-meter-long Aquino Bridge, which collapsed on Aug. 28.

“Through the years that I was mayor, I had long asked the DPWH to give sufficient attention to finding a solution to strengthen the foundations of these two bridges, but this was not prioritized by previous officials,” Angeles said in Filipino.
“As a newly seated congresswoman, I personally appealed to Secretary Vince Dizon during the recent budget hearing to provide sufficient funding for the bridges,” she added.
Angeles also thanked President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon for visiting the area to inspect the damage.
“I am deeply grateful to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and Secretary Vince for their personal visit, concern, solutions and immediate response,” she said in Filipino.
Angeles also appealed for unity among Tarlac residents and urged them to refrain from politicizing the issue or pointing fingers.
“Instead, let us unite and help one another, and respect the DPWH as it provides the correct information about what happened,” she said in Filipino.
On Wednesday, Marcos and Dizon inspected the ongoing construction of a Bailey bridge intended to restore access following the collapse of Agana Bridge.
The President directed the DPWH to fast-track the construction of the alternate bridge and said the national government would provide P300 million in assistance to the Tarlac City government.
Angeles joined Tarlac City Mayor Susan Yap, Tarlac Gov. Christian Yap and other local officials during the inspection.
Marcos also said Wednesday that widespread flooding in Central Luzon and Metro Manila resulted from the failure to implement a flood control master plan that had existed for decades.
“We already have a master plan; it’s just never been executed,” Marcos said when asked whether the public could expect such a plan.
“We’re only executing it now. We have had a master plan for decades, but nothing was done. Only now. We’re only starting it now,” he added, without specifying which master plan he was referring to.
The remarks came as 9.4 million people, or 2.7 million families, across Luzon were displaced by flooding caused by three storms and the prevailing southwest monsoon, or habagat, since Aug. 1.
On Aug. 29, a sport utility vehicle fell into the Tarlac River as Agana Bridge collapsed. Only one of its five passengers survived.
The remains of two passengers were recovered in Pangasinan, while two others remained missing.
Tarlac was placed under a state of calamity on Aug. 30 following widespread damage caused by the southwest monsoon.

articles.title: Palace says 'no laws violated' amid acting capacity of some Cabinet officials
articles.summary: Malacañang on Thursday stood firm that President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. is not violating any law even as some of his appointed Cabinet officials still serve in an acting capacity.

blocks.text: Published September 3, 2026 5:51pm
Malacañang on Thursday stood firm that President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. is not violating any law even as some of his appointed Cabinet officials still serve in an acting capacity.

Palace Press Officer Usec. Claire Castro said this in a press briefing, responding to the statement of Senator Imee Marcos that over a dozen Cabinet officials still have not undergone scrutiny and confirmation by the Commission on Appointments (CA).
“Hindi nagtatalaga ng permanenteng mga opisyal na dadaan sa Commission on Appointments; bakit? Kalapastanganan na naman sa Saligang Batas!” Senator Imee, sister of the President, said.
(They aren’t appointing permanent officials who would undergo the process of the Commission on Appointments; why? This is another violation of the Constitution!)
“Dalawang taon na lang ang administrasyong ito, puro ‘acting’ lang lahat, mga overacting na,” she added.
(This administration has only two years left, yet everyone is just in ‘acting’ capacity. They are now over-acting!)
The CA is mandated to approve or disapprove appointments made by the President of the Philippines, the confirmation of which is required under the 1987 Constitution.
But Castro said that she cannot question the decisions of the President. She said that Marcos has not given any explanation as to why some acting secretaries are not yet being called to the CA.
“Unang unang, prerogative ng Pangulo ‘yan at tumutupad ang Pangulo sa batas,” the Palace official said.
(First of all, that is the prerogative of the President, and the President is following the law.)

“Sa ngayon po ay naaayon pa rin ang pag-a-appoint sa mga acting secretary katulad ni Sec. Dave Gomez, siya po ay interim appointee as of July 10. So wala po nilalabag na anumang proseso, batas ang ating Pangulo,” she added.

(For now, the appointment of acting secretaries like Sec. Dave Gomez is still in accordance with the law. He is an interim appointee as of July 10. So there is no violation of any process, and our President is following the law.)
Based on the art card posted by Imee Marcos on her Facebook page, the following Cabinet officials are still serving in an acting capacity:

items: Executive Secretary Ralph Recto
Presidential Communications Office (PCO) Secretary Dave Gomez
Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Secretary Vince Dizon
Department of Transportation (DOTr) Secretary Giovanni Lopez
Department of Justice (DOJ) Secretary Fredderick Vida
Department of Finance (DOF) Secretary Frederick Go
Department of Budget and Management (DBM) Secretary Kim De Leon
Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna

Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) Secretary Francis Tolentino

articles.title: 'Supersized' El Nino could be strongest on record, UN says
articles.summary: The current El Nino could end up being the strongest since records began 40 years ago, the UN warns. It says the phenomenon is being "supersized" thanks to exceptionally warm temperatures in the…

image.caption: El Nino is increasing the risks of extreme heat, drought and floods, according to the UNImage: Myo Kyaw Soe/Xinhua News Agency/picture alliance

blocks.text: The El Nino weather phenomenon is set to intensify and will almost certainly last until February next year, the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) said in an update Thursday.

The UN weather agency warned El Nino would develop into a "very strong" event in the coming months, heightening the risks of extreme heat, drought and flooding while threatening livelihoods and economies.

"El Nino is being supersized before our eyes," UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres said in a statement. "The science leaves no room for doubt: the planet is in uncharted waters, and those waters are heating up."

WMO head Celeste Saulo told a press conference in Geneva that, on the current trajectory, the El Nino, "may be stronger than anything since our monitoring began, so literally off the charts we have used for the past four decades."
What is El Nino?

El Nino is a natural climate phenomenon that happens every two to seven years and is not caused by climate change. But scientists say it can worsen the impacts of global heating caused by the continued burning of fossil fuels.
The WMO classifies El Nino events as weak, moderate, strong or very strong, with the current El Nino set to reach the highest intensity level on that scale.
This winter's El Nino could be strongest on record
The phenomenon begins with the warming of surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean, triggering changes in winds, pressure and rainfall patterns around the world.
For example, it often brings dry conditions and drought to Australia, Indonesia and parts of the Amazon, while East Africa and the southern US may experience heavy rainfall.
El Ninos typically begin between March and June, peaking toward the end of the year and lasting around nine to 12 months.
Ocean temperatures already 'exceptionally' high

WMO head Saulo said there was "an exceptionally high likelihood of nearly 100% that El Nino will persist through to February 2027," adding that it was the first time the organization had "expressed such a degree of certainty. "

Sea surface temperatures in the tropical Pacific region , which drive El Nino and reshape weather and climate patterns thousands of kilometers away, are already well above average and continuing to rise, according to the UN agency.
"Subsurface ocean temps are also exceptionally high and in some areas more than 8 degrees Celsius above normal during July and early August," Saulo said.
While El Nino is expected to peak toward the end of the year, its knock-on effects will likely last well into 2027, she added.
Global average temperatures are often particularly high the year after an El Nino. For example, the 2023-2024 El Nino contributed to 2024 being the warmest year on record.
"We should not be surprised if this record is broken," Saulo said.
How climate change is teaming up with 'Super El Nino'
'We have no time to lose'
Saulo said droughts, floods and extreme heat were already causing disruption and devastation, and warned these impacts would "multiply and cascade as El Nino intensifies."

Saulo stressed that the weather phenomenon would "deliver a major blow to communities, economies and supply chains across the globe" and called for preparations to safeguard climate-sensitive sectors.
"We have no time to lose," she said.

articles.title: COA: Nearly 50 flood control projects under fraud audit
articles.summary: The Commission on Audit (COA) said it has conducted fraud audits on nearly 50 flood control projects as it continues its investigation into alleged irregularities in government infrastructure…

blocks.text: Published September 3, 2026 5:38pm

The Commission on Audit (COA) said it has conducted fraud audits on nearly 50 flood control projects as it continues its investigation into alleged irregularities in government infrastructure projects, with Bulacan currently serving as its main area of focus.

COA chairperson Gamaliel Cordoba disclosed this during the Senate hearing on the commission’s proposed budget for 2027, where senators pressed the constitutional audit body on its role in investigating the alleged flood control anomalies.
Nearly 50 projects audited
Cordoba said COA began concentrating its fraud audits in Bulacan because the province accounts for a significant share of the Department of Public Works and Highways’ (DPWH) flood control spending.

“P98B or 18% of the total worth of flood control projects implemented by DPWH from 2022-2025 ay sa Bulacan napunta,” Cordoba said, referring to about P98 billion worth of projects, or roughly 18% of the total, implemented in the province during the period.
“So doon kami nag-concentrate,” he added.
Cordoba said the fraud audits remain ongoing and that the number of projects covered had reached “almost 50.”
The COA chief said the commission had already issued notices of disallowance based on the conclusions of some of its fraud audits.
“Naging conclusion sa fraud audit, so we issued notices of disallowance. And we already submitted this to the Office of the Ombudsman,” Cordoba said.
He added that COA had also previously submitted audit findings to the now-defunct Independent Commission for Infrastructure (ICI), which investigated alleged irregularities in flood control projects.
Cordoba said COA could provide the Senate with the audit reports, including information on the persons found liable in the cases.
“We can submit it to the honorable finance committee. At makikita niyo ang persons liable, nandoon naman po,” he said.
No link to Sen. Villanueva
During the hearing, Senator Joel Villanueva asked COA about the results of its fraud audits in Bulacan and whether he had been implicated in any of the projects examined by the commission.
Cordoba said COA had not found Villanueva linked to the projects it had audited.
“Ano na-audit niyo?” Villanueva asked.
“Wala po kami nakikita,” Cordoba replied.
He clarified that COA’s findings were focused on the implementing agency, the DPWH, and its personnel in Bulacan.
“It’s really the DPWH people yung nag-implement because it’s the budget of the DPWH and it’s their personnel sa Bulacan,” Cordoba said.
COA says audits will continue

Cordoba said the commission would continue its fraud audits and coordinate with the Office of the Ombudsman, whose investigators have been using COA personnel as witnesses in preliminary investigations and cases filed before the Sandiganbayan and regional trial courts.
“We are committed to the Office of the Ombudsman,” Cordoba said, adding that COA fraud auditors have already appeared as witnesses in cases involving the alleged anomalies.
He said the commission’s work would continue “until we cover them all."
For now, he said, Bulacan remains COA’s principal focus because it has emerged as the “ground zero” of the flood control projects being scrutinized.—LDF, GMA News

articles.title: 'Beautiful, vibrant' Disney star Carla Jeffery dies at 33
articles.summary: Jeffery was known for playing cheerleader Bree in 2018 Disney Channel movie Zombies and two sequels.

blocks.text: US actress Carla Jeffery, who was known for appearing in 2018 Disney Channel movie Zombies and two sequels, has died at the age of 33.
Announcing the news, her agent Carla Alexander described her as a "beautiful, vibrant and incredibly talented woman whose radiant smile could light up any room".

Jeffery played cheerleader Bree in Zombies and its follow-ups in 2020 and 2022, and previously had a recurring role in Curb Your Enthusiasm as one of the Black family, who moved in with Larry David after Hurricane Katrina.
No cause of death has been given.
Her management company Alexanders Talent wrote on Instagram, external: "Our hearts are broken as we mourn the loss of our beloved Carla Jeffery.

"For more than 20 years, Carla was part of the Alexanders Talent Management family and watching her grow from a talented young girl into the beautiful, vibrant woman and actress she became was an incredible privilege.
"We will remember her infectious smile, her laughter, her talent, and the beautiful light she carried everywhere she went.

"Our deepest love and condolences are with Carla's family and loved ones. We ask that their privacy be respected during this incredibly difficult time. Rest beautifully, Carla. You will be deeply missed and forever loved."
Jeffery's twin brother Carlon, who is also an actor, reposted that statement as well as a clip of his sister on a beach and a screenshot of an undated text message.
"Hey Sis, call me back when you get this. I was just calling to see how your day went! I love you to the moon & back sis," it read.

"I just want you to know how proud I am of you. Your resilience, your grace, your infectious smile that lights up a room. You are truly a light that shines bright. Don't let anyone dim that light, even yourself.

"The light you carry is special and must be protected at all times. You are the best sister a brother could ask for. Pray we continue to grow closer to one another along this journey. I got your back in this life and the next."
Her co-stars also paid tribute, with Chandler Kinney, who played Willa in Zombies, writing that the actress's death "doesn't feel real".
"Carla. The sweetest, most sparkly gal. You made every day better and brighter with your infectious positivity," Kinney wrote.

"I think part of why you brought such effervescence to Bree (aside from your immense talent) is because that's really who you were in your heart; a bubbly, vivacious heart-of-gold cheerleader who loved nothing more than to uplift those around her."
Milo Manheim, who played Zed, shared a series of photos with the caption: "Love you Carlaboo, the sweetest, kindest, most loving person."

articles.title: Marcos invites inventors, innovators to help address national challenges
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. asked urged country’s inventors and innovators to work with the government in addressing food insecurity, flooding, energy shortages, and other…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. asked urged country’s inventors and innovators to work with the government in addressing food insecurity, flooding, energy shortages, and other challenges facing the country.

In his speech at the 2026 Presidential Filipinnovation Awards National Competition Awarding Ceremony on Thursday, Marcos said his administration would continue to support them in turning their ideas and inspirations into usable breakthroughs.

“To every innovator across the country: I know that you have come a long way to reach this point. I also know that there is still much to do to turn your ideas into solutions that can improve the lives of our people, our communities, and our nation,” he said in his speech at the Crowne Plaza Galleria in Quezon City.
“I call on each of you to work with the government in addressing modern challenges—from food insecurity, flooding, soil erosion and energy shortages,” the President added.
Marcos also expressed his commitment to creating an environment where more inventors and innovators can pursue their ideas.
“This administration appreciates your efforts in helping building a safer, more comfortable, and more sustainable life for every Filipino,” he said.

Citing a famous quote from Thomas Edison, the President commended the inventors and innovators for their curiosity and discipline in creating and pursuing new ideas, as well as their determination to make a difference in the lives of others.

“After all, whenever I read phrases like that, I am reminded of Thomas Edison’s answer when he was asked to define his genius. And his answer was rather simple and he said, ‘my genius consist of one percent inspiration and 99 percent perspiration’,” he said.
“So, that sticktoitiveness, that persistence, that commitment to it is a critical part of everything that we have achieved here,” Marcos said.
The five winners out of 16 finalists of this year’s Presidential Filipinnovation Awards National Competition are as follows:
– Compact Easy to Operate and Economical Biodiesel Reactor for Benteng Diesel, Capistrano Research and Development on Biotechnology
– Philippine Native Chicken helping Industry through Scientific Innovations, Golden Sprout Corporation
– Saltric Marissa Turbine: Turning Rivers into 24/7 Power for Off-Grid Filipino Communities, PDG Engineering Services
– Gasification Process for Waste Disposal: Advance Waste Solution, Vic Metal Fabrication and Environmental Services, Inc.
– OstreaVent2 A Prototype Ventilator for Mechanically Ventilated Adult Patients, Breath of Life Foundation, Inc.

The awardees received P3.5 million worth of cash grants and post-competition support which includes training and mentoring, participation in local and international platforms, and opportunities to connect with potential investors, clients, and business partners.

articles.title: Prosecution may drop bribery raps to expedite impeach trial – Luistro
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Article III or the bribery allegation against Vice President Sara Duterte may be dropped to expedite the impeachment trial and allow the prosecution to raise before the court…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Article III or the bribery allegation against Vice President Sara Duterte may be dropped to expedite the impeachment trial and allow the prosecution to raise before the court other issues, Batangas Rep. Gerville Luistro said on Thursday.

In an ambush interview after a committee hearing at the House of Representatives, Luistro — lead public prosecutor — confirmed that dropping Article III of the Articles of Impeachment is being considered to expedite the proceedings to give the Senate impeachment court some breathing room.

She, however, also noted that since Article I or the alleged misuse of confidential funds touched on the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) already, they may skip Article III since it deals with claims that Duterte bribed DepEd procurement officials.

“We do not want to drag this impeachment trial too much because we understand that somehow naapektuhan ‘yong buhay ng mga Pilipino and even the focus of the parties concerned […] Narinig natin ‘yong manifestation ni Presiding Officer na talagang medyo challenged na sila considering that three important functions are being addressed by the Senate at the same time,” Luistro told reporters.

(We do not want to drag this impeachment trial too much because we understand that somehow it affects the lives of Filipinos and even the focus of the parties concerned […] We heard the manifestation of the Presiding Officer that they are being challenged considering that three important functions are being addressed by the Senate at the same time.)

“I’m not saying that it is the weakest, but you see it pertains as well to […] DepEd to be very specific, ‘no? Ito ‘yong payola envelops na inimbestigahan din ng House of Representatives, no? So, lahat sila ay malakas, lahat sila ay strong, but we have this confidential fund already na pertaining to both the OVP and DepEd. Siguro, we focus on something else as part of our consideration,” she added.

(I’m not saying that it is the weakest, but you see it pertains as well to […] DepEd to be very specific, right? These are about the payola envelopes that the House of Representatives investigated. So, all of them are strong, but we have this confidential fund already pertaining to both the OVP and DepEd. Maybe, we can focus on something else as part of our consideration.)

Luistro said it is also a measure of being confident about the evidence and testimonies that they have presented for both Article I and Article IV or the allegation that Duterte betrayed public trust when she issued grave threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his relatives.
She clarified that they are also confident about the bribery allegations, but it eventually boils down to time constraints and their goal of presenting something different from Article I.

“It is a validation na confident kami do’n sa grave threat, confident kami dito sa confidential fund, and as a matter of fact, we are equally confident pagdating dito sa unexplained wealth,” Luistro said.
(It is a validation that we are confident about the grave threat, confident with the confidential fund misuse, and as a matter of fact, we are equally confident when it comes to unexplained wealth.)

“Well, it does not discount the fact that we are similarly confident with bribery, kaya lang it concerns the same irregularities in the same agency which is the Department of Education. But I just want to point out, no official decision yet,” she added.
On Wednesday, Manila Rep. Joel Chua confirmed in an ambush interview that the prosecution panel is considering to refrain from presenting Article III.

In a press briefing later that day, Chua clarified that the bribery allegation against Duterte remain strong, noting that the only reason why the prosecution panel has considered this article as expendable is due to priorities and a yearning to expedite the trial.
Chua explained that if they push through with the withdrawal of Article III, this will be similar to what the prosecution panel for the impeachment trial of former Chief Justice Renato Corona did.

However, Chua also stressed that this is not a new matter, reminding the public that they said before that if the prosecution is satisfied with the evidence and testimonies at hand, they will let go of one article.
Of the four Articles of Impeachment, the prosecution has finished presenting evidence for Article IV, and is on track to finish Article I by September 9.

A total of 10 witnesses have been presented by the prosecution team for Article I. On Wednesday, the panel presented former Education Undersecretary Michael Poa, who also happens to be a member of the defense panel.

Prior to Poa, the prosecution panel presented two Land Bank of the Philippines officials from which the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and DepEd withdrew their CFs; state auditors who checked on the confidential expenditures made by Duterte’s offices; OVP staffers like former special disbursing officer Gina Acosta; and on Tuesday, two Philippine Army (PA) officials. /gsg

articles.title: Pagadian opens banana tissue culture laboratory
articles.summary: PAGADIAN CITY, Zamboanga del Sur – Local banana growers here are set to benefit from disease-free planting materials with the opening of a local government unit (LGU)-owned banana tissue…

blocks.text: PAGADIAN CITY, Zamboanga del Sur – Local banana growers here are set to benefit from disease-free planting materials with the opening of a local government unit (LGU)-owned banana tissue culture laboratory on Wednesday.

The facility, located in Barangay Macasing, marks a major agricultural milestone as the first fully functional banana tissue culture laboratory in the Zamboanga Peninsula (Region 9). While similar ventures were attempted previously across the region, Pagadian City is the first LGU to sustain operational culture production successfully.

“Many have tried and started similar laboratories, but so far, we are the only one who sustained it,” said city agriculturist Engr. Ramon Rodrigo Jr. “We hope to continuously propagate tissue-cultured seedlings through this facility.”
Designed to uplift rural livelihoods, the laboratory directly supports City Mayor Samuel Co’s initiative to convert idle city lands into productive agricultural areas.
The facility will primarily produce high-yielding Lakatan banana seedlings to address the city’s persistent local market deficit.
“Currently, our local market lacks a steady supply of locally grown bananas,” Rodrigo noted, adding that existing produce from upland barangays like Lison Valley remains insufficient.

Bananas offer immediate benefits—first for household consumption, and second for commercial sale. “If production scales up significantly, we will prepare market linkages outside Pagadian, such as Manila and Cebu,” he added.
The laboratory eliminates the financial burden on smallholder farmers, who previously had to buy expensive seedlings brought in from other regions.

To encourage adoption, Co announced that initial distributions of Lakatan seedlings will be free of charge to small-scale and backyard growers, alongside technical monitoring from the City Agriculture Office.

“For those doing backyard farming, we will provide the seedlings for free,” Co stated. “However, for large-scale commercial plantations requiring hundreds or thousands of seedlings, planting materials will be offered at a minimal cost.”
The Macasing laboratory currently yields 5,000 to 10,000 seedlings per cycle, with a maximum capacity to produce up to 15,000 tissue-cultured plantlets. /coa

articles.title: DENR chief orders closer watch on flood threats after Nepal disaster
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Environment Secretary Juan Miguel “Mitch” Cuna has ordered closer monitoring and risk assessment of flood threats and intensified law enforcement and use of science and…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Environment Secretary Juan Miguel “Mitch” Cuna has ordered closer monitoring and risk assessment of flood threats and intensified law enforcement and use of science and technology in forest and watershed protection, using drones, satellite imagery, and near-real-time forest disturbance alert systems to detect threats early and reduce risks to downstream communities.
“Protecting our forests and watersheds requires timely information and decisive action,” Cuna said.
“Drones, satellite imagery, and near-real-time monitoring tools allow us to identify risks earlier, deploy personnel effectively, and strengthen enforcement in hard-to-reach areas.”

Cuna made the order in the wake of the Nepal mudslide disaster that killed at least 1,000, noting that, though that country’s mountain hazards differ from those in the Philippines, debris flow and flash floods caused by natural landslide damming could also happen here.
The DENR statement pointed out one instance: In 2012, Typhoon Pablo triggered a massive debris flow in New Bataan, Compostela Valley (now Davao de Oro).
The DENR noted this lesson from the experience: “Upstream risks rapidly threaten downstream populations when vulnerable landscapes, altered conditions, and extreme weather converge.”

“What happens in the headwaters does not stay in the headwaters,” Cuna explained. “Flood resilience begins upstream by protecting forests, understanding landscape hazards, and making sound land-use decisions.”

The DENR stressed the importance of watershed protection — which has been established in the Philippines starting with the revised Forestry Code of 1975 — in mitigating flooding, erosion, sedimentation, and landslides.
So the country now has watershed protection policies on integrated planning, reforestation, climate adaptation, and Watershed Management Councils.
Science-based geohazard info, land-use planning

Cuna stressed that preparedness relies on reliable environmental and geohazard mapping to help local government units (LGUs) in settlement planning, infrastructure development, and disaster readiness.
The DENR’s Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB) provides geohazard maps for landslide and flood risks to guide local evacuation and land-use decisions.

Similarly, the National Mapping and Resource Information Authority (NAMRIA) supplies authoritative base maps and topographic data to integrate hazard awareness into development planning and emergency response.

Complementing these spatial tools, the Forest Management Bureau (FMB) relies on the Satellite Land Monitoring System (SLMS), which uses satellite imagery, GIS, and cloud platforms to make biannual land use and forest cover change maps, ensuring local planning and climate reporting are grounded in precise, up-to-date forest resource data.
Strong environmental law enforcement
“We will continue to use every lawful tool to protect critical ecosystems and hold violators accountable,” Cuna affirmed.
This involves monitoring technologies matched with firm regulatory action against illegal mining, logging, and other activities that threaten ecosystem integrity.

Citing an example, he said that, as of the second quarter of 2026 alone, 93 cease-and-desist orders had been issued to mining companies violating and not complying with requirements, enforcing strict compliance with environmental safeguards.
Community preparedness and risk reduction
The DENR urges flood- and landslide-prone communities to heed official weather advisories and local authority warnings during severe weather.
The Nepal disaster underscores that risk reduction must begin upstream through ecosystem management, informed land use, and continuous downstream readiness.
“Our goal is to reduce risks before they become disasters by protecting ecosystems, enforcing laws, and collaborating with local communities,” Cuna. /atm

articles.title: Gov’t releases P8.68-billion additional fund for teachers’ salary upgrade
articles.summary: The DBM approved the release of additional funds for the salaries of promoted and reclassified public school teachers.

blocks.text: September 3, 2026 | 5:15pm
Students of the Marikina Elementary School in Marikina City attend a two-hour class orientation before the formal school opening on August 23, 2023.
STAR / Walter Bollozos

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Budget and Management (DBM) approved on Thursday, September 3, the release of an additional P8.68-billion fund for the salary upgrade of public school teachers.
The DBM said in a press release that 93,344 teachers under the Department of Education (DepEd) could benefit from the additional funding for the Expanded Career Progression (ECP) System.
It will cover the salary differentials of public education personnel who have been reclassified under the ECP.

“This P8.68-billion release means more than 93,000 qualified public school personnel can receive the compensation that comes with their reclassified positions. Pinaghirapan nila ang career advancement na ito, kaya dapat maramdaman din nila ang benepisyo nito,” Acting Budget Secretary Kim De Leon said in the press release.
(They worked hard for this career advancement, so they should also feel its benefits.)

The ECP is a competency-based promotion system in which qualified teachers can advance their careers either by applying for a vacant higher position or reclassifying an existing position to a higher ECP position.
Higher positions under ECP carry a higher salary grade.
The additional funding is set to cover the salaries of personnel for 2025 and 2026 whose reclassified positions and appointments have been officially approved.
The regional offices of the budget agency will process and facilitate the release of additional funds to respective DepEd regional branches to ensure timely implementation.
Meanwhile, DBM said the government is proposing higher funding for the public teachers’ career advancement system.
The proposed 2027 national budget allocated P12.09 billion for the ECP, which, according to the DBM, is P5.94 billion or 96.6% higher than its 2026 fund.

articles.title: Bulacan flood control fraud audits found no link to Joel Villanueva, says COA
articles.summary: The Commission on Audit (COA) said it found no link between Senator Joel Villanueva and the flood-control projects in Bulacan covered by its fraud audits.

blocks.text: Published September 3, 2026 5:09pm
The Commission on Audit (COA) said it found no link between Senator Joel Villanueva and the flood-control projects in Bulacan covered by its fraud audits.

Villanueva raised the issue during the Senate hearing on COA’s proposed 2027 budget, asking the commission whether its ongoing examination of flood control projects in his home province had found him connected to any of the projects under review.
“Puwede niyo sabihin kahit sa harap ni Chairman JV (Ejercito) hindi po ako mahihiya sabihin kung si Joel Villanueva ba kasama sa projects ng flood control sa mga nakita po ng COA,” Villanueva said.
COA chairperson Gamaliel Cordoba responded that the commission had not found such a link.
“Wala po kaming nakikita,” Cordoba replied.
COA findings point to implementing agency
Cordoba said the audits so far have focused on the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH), which implemented the projects and whose personnel were assigned to the Bulacan district.
“It’s really the DPWH people yung nag-implement because it’s the budget of the DPWH and it’s their personnel sa Bulacan,” Cordoba said.
He added that Villanueva was not involved in implementing the projects and was not identified by COA in connection with the audit findings discussed during the hearing.

The exchange came as COA reported that its fraud audits of flood-control projects in Bulacan remain ongoing. Cordoba said the commission had so far covered “almost 50” projects and had issued notices of disallowance based on findings from some of the audits.
COA to submit reports to Senate
Cordoba said COA had already submitted fraud audit findings to the Office of the Ombudsman and could provide copies to the Senate.

The commission has also been coordinating with the Ombudsman, with COA fraud auditors serving as witnesses in preliminary investigations and cases filed before the Sandiganbayan and regional trial courts.

COA previously ordered a fraud audit of DPWH flood-control projects in Bulacan following concerns over the implementation of flood-mitigation projects in the province. Subsequent COA reports have flagged projects that auditors found to be nonexistent, constructed at locations different from those approved, or unsupported by required documentation.
Cordoba said the commission would continue its audits, with Bulacan remaining its principal focus because of the volume of flood control projects implemented there.
“Wala namang hihinto, tuloy-tuloy lang hanggang sa ma-cover po namin lahat,” he said. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Sandiganbayan orders release of ex-DPWH chief Manuel Bonoan
articles.summary: The Sandiganbayan has ordered the release of former Public Works Secretary Manuel Bonoan from police custody, following the formal dropping of charges against him earlier this week.

blocks.text: September 3, 2026 | 5:08pm
Former Public Works and Highways secretary Manuel Bonoan attends the Senate Blue Ribbon Committee hearing on the flood control controversy on Jan. 19, 2026.
Senate PRIB / Released

MANILA, Philippines — The Sandiganbayan has ordered the release of former Public Works Secretary Manuel Bonoan from police custody, following the formal dropping of charges against him earlier this week.
The Sandiganbayan Fifth Division signed the order directing the Philippine National Police General Hospital to release Bonoan from its custody on Thursday, September 3.
This comes after the court earlier this week excluded Bonoan from the flood control-related plunder and graft charges filed against Sen. Jinggoy Estrada and other officials.
The Ombudsman had earlier asked the Sandiganbayan to remove Bonoan as a co-accused to make him a potential state witness in other flood control cases.
With Bonoan now ordered set free, he is no longer facing plunder and graft charges over the alleged Estrada-related P573-million worth of kickbacks from flood control works.
The former public works chief has been under hospital arrest since June due to a host of illnesses that include chronic kidney disease and prostate cancer.

articles.title: 15-year-old Tacloban shooter faces 10 additional murder-related raps
articles.summary: Authorities found that the kid "acted with discernment."

blocks.text: September 3, 2026 | 5:05pm
Policemen stand near the crime scene of a school compound after a shooting incident at a high school compound in Tacloban City, Leyte province on June 22, 2026.
AFP / Noel Sianosa

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Justice (DOJ) Tacloban City prosecutors are set to file four counts of frustrated murder and six counts of attempted murder charges against the 15-year-old student behind the Tacloban school shooting incident in June.

DOJ Undersecretary Ian Norman Dato said in a press briefing on Thursday, September 3, that their prosecutors found that the minor shooter acted with discernment and in conspiracy with the 14-year-old second suspect.
“The prosecutors have looked into the entirety of the documentary evidence. I believe some psychological reports have been looked into,” Dato said.
The charges were directed to be filed before the Regional Trial Court in Tacloban City.
A P72,000 bail for each count of frustrated murder and P36,000 for each count of attempted murder were recommended by the DOJ. The total recommended bail amounts to P504,000.

In June, the Police Regional Office in Eastern Visayas had already filed three counts of murder, three counts of frustrated murder and multiple counts of physical injury against the 15-year-old shooter.

Meanwhile, the 14-year-old shooter, according to Dato, is exempt from criminal liability but will undergo intervention mechanisms under the restorative justice mandate of the country’s juvenile justice system.

“The 14-year-old is a minor…so the criminal causes will not apply to him. But the intervention or the jurisdiction over him is now under the local social welfare and development office because a 14-year-old is exempt from criminal liability,” Dato explained.
Last week, Tacloban City prosecutors recommended the filing of reckless imprudence resulting in multiple homicide and physical injuries against the policewoman aunt of the younger suspect.
The aunt, who was a police staff sergeant before the incident, owned the government-issued 9mm firearm used by her nephew to open fire at San Jose National High School, killing three students.
The 15-year-old suspect, meanwhile, used a .38-caliber revolver registered to a Cebu security agency.
Both minor shooters are currently under the custody of a rehabilitation facility under the Department of Social Welfare and Development.

articles.title: DOTr to regulate e-trikes to ensure safety, roadworthiness of vehicles
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Transportation (DOTr) will regulate electric tricycles (e-trikes) to ensure that drivers are qualified to drive and their vehicles will be roadworthy and…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Transportation (DOTr) will regulate electric tricycles (e-trikes) to ensure that drivers are qualified to drive and their vehicles will be roadworthy and registered, its Secretary Giovanni Lopez said on Thursday.

During the House committee on appropriations’ briefing for the proposed DOTr budget for 2027, Caloocan City Rep. Edgar Erica asked if the department has plans to help drivers who use e-trikes for a living, noting that many of them are prone to extortion as they don’t have franchise to ply routes.

Erice then cited the Section 447 of the Local Government Code where the local government units are mandated to regulate the operations of tricycles, subject to the guidelines released by the DOTr. As Lopez acknowledged that its regulation is within the local government’s jurisdiction, he said that the agency will release a department order (DO).
“Maglalabas po kami ng DO at ireregulate po namin kung anong tama po na pamamaraan,” Lopez said.
(We will release a DO and we will regulate the proper guidelines.)
Lopez emphasized that e-trikes must be registered and the drivers must be qualified and have a license.
“Sa pananaw namin, the moment na ginamit yang e-trike na yan at it involves passenger and it involves national highway, kailangan na maregulate yan,” he added.
(From our perspective, the moment that an e-trike is used and it involves passenger and national highway, it needs to be regulated.)
He said that the initial DO needs to be polished as the regulation of e-trikes is a “noble case” as many e-trikes are also being used as public transportation modes.
This initiative was welcomed by Erice, saying that the local government units must have a legal basis in provision of franchises and licenses to e-trikes.

“Panahon na para yung mga pwedeng e-trikes, sabi nyo nga may specifications para yung hindi susunod sa specifications, medyo maisantabi na natin at yung pwede, mabigyan ng registration sa LTO [Land Transportation Office] para mayroon silang legal basis yung local government to grant franchises,” Erice expressed.

(It’s about time for e-trikes, you said that there will be specifications so those that will not follow the specifications can be set aside while those who are qualified will be given registration by the LTO so the local government can have a basis to grant franchises.)

The LTO earlier clarified that there is no blanket ban on electric bicycles (e-bikes) and e-trikes as they can still operate on city and municipal roads. The LTO noted that they are only restricted on national highways and major thoroughfares. /mr

articles.title: Fire forces Dinagat water shutdown
articles.summary: SAN FRANCISCO, Agusan del Sur — The San Jose Water District in Dinagat Islands has suspended its entire water supply operation after a large fire swept through a watershed area and reached…

blocks.text: SAN FRANCISCO, Agusan del Sur — The San Jose Water District in Dinagat Islands has suspended its entire water supply operation after a large fire swept through a watershed area and reached facilities serving communities in three towns.
The shutdown came as the province recorded a dangerous heat index of 45 degrees Celsius at noon on Thursday, raising concerns over residents’ access to water amid extreme heat.
The water district said the fire began around 8 p.m. on Saturday, Aug. 29, in Sitio Palo Doce, Barangay Doña Helen in Basilisa town. It spread rapidly by 3 p.m. the following day.
The blaze eventually reached the pumping station in Sitio Manoligao, Barangay Del Pilar in Cagdianao, and moved toward the upper portion of the watershed in Barangay Cuarinta, San Jose.
The fire remained active in parts of the watershed as of Thursday, said the water district.
Clearing operations, a rapid damage assessment, and needs analysis were underway to determine the condition of the water facilities and the extent of the damage.
“Water supply operations will resume once the status of our facilities is declared safe and secure,” the water district management said in an advisory.
Repair and restoration work will begin immediately after the assessment, it added.
The shutdown comes as residents contend with dangerous heat.
At noon Thursday, the air temperature reached 34°C, with a dew point of 27°C, producing a heat index of 45°C—classified as “danger.”
Under such conditions, prolonged exposure or physical activity may cause heat cramps, heat exhaustion, or heat stroke.

Residents were advised to drink plenty of water, avoid unnecessary outdoor activities, wear light-colored clothing, use umbrellas, and limit strenuous activities during midday and afternoon. They were also advised to avoid alcoholic drinks.
The water district appealed for patience and cooperation, acknowledging that the shutdown would worsen the existing water shortage.
“Our priority is public safety and the restoration of water supply service at the earliest possible time,” it said./coa

articles.title: What Stories Will Our Children Grow Up With?
articles.summary: What do children remember from the stories they watch? Sometimes, it is a character who made them laugh. A song

blocks.text: What do children remember from the stories they watch?
Sometimes, it is a character who made them laugh. A song they could sing by heart. A lesson they carried long after the episode ended.

For many of us who grew up in the 90s, it was Bayani, Sineskwela, MathTinik, and other programs that made learning part of childhood. We watched them because they were entertaining, but somewhere along the way, they taught us how to think, how to understand the world, and sometimes, how to imagine a better one.

We may not have realized it then, but those stories were shaping us, and that is the power of media. A story can make a child curious, it can make them question what they see, teach them to empathize with someone whose life is different from theirs. It can give language to something they have experienced but did not know how to express.

But the opposite can also be true. A story can normalize violence, it can turn someone’s suffering into spectacle, it can make harmful behavior seem ordinary, or make a child believe that what they are experiencing is something they simply have to endure.

And today, children are bombarded by more stories than ever before. They encounter them not only on television, but through YouTube, TikTok, across streaming platforms, games, social media, and the endless scroll of a digital world designed to capture their attention.
But when everything is competing to be seen, what happens to the stories that deserve to be heard?

This is why child-friendly media matters. Not because children need to be protected from every difficult story, but because they deserve stories that help them understand difficult realities without taking away their dignity, their curiosity, or their hope.

Through institutions like National Council for Children’s Television (NCCT), they recognize the responsibility to help create a media environment where children are not simply audiences, but young people whose rights, experiences, and perspectives matter.
Because creating content for children is not simply about making something colorful, entertaining, or easy to understand. It is about asking: What kind of world are we helping children make sense of?

This responsibility becomes even more important when telling stories about children themselves. As journalist and documentarist Kara David reminds us through her work and advocacy on responsible journalism, stories involving children require extra care as they must be the first priority. Behind every statistic is a child. Behind every headline is a person. And behind every story is a life that should never be reduced to a shocking image, a viral moment, or a convenient narrative.
Children deserve to be represented not merely as victims of the world’s problems, but as people with voices, dreams, agency, and dignity.
Perhaps this is why documentary storytelling matters.
A documentary asks us to slow down, look closer, listen longer, and to sit with stories that algorithms might otherwise ask us to scroll past.

Now in its 10th year, NCCT’s DokyuBata continues to provide a space for stories that put children and young people at the center. For a decade, it has helped keep alive the idea that children’s stories deserve to be documented, not because they are always easy or pleasant, but because they are real, important, and worth listening to.

In a time when attention is increasingly measured in seconds, telling a meaningful story becomes an act of intention. It says: This story is worth your time. This child is worth listening to. This experience should not be forgotten.

And perhaps that is what media literacy should ultimately help us understand. It is not enough to teach children what to watch. We must also ask ourselves: What are we giving them to watch? And when they look back at the media they grew up with, will they find stories that helped them become more compassionate, more critical, more informed, and more hopeful human beings?
The stories we tell children today become part of how they understand themselves and the world around them.

So let us tell stories that do more than fill their screens. Let us tell stories that open their minds, affirm their dignity, deepen their understanding, and remind them that they, too, have a place in shaping the world.
DokyuBata Dekada is still accepting submissions until September 17, 2026, at 11:59 PM.
Because sometimes, the story that changes how a child sees the world is simply the story someone chose to tell.

articles.title: Prosecution prepares to present unexplained wealth charges vs Duterte
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The prosecution panel is now preparing for the possible presentation of evidence for its unexplained wealth allegations against Vice President Sara Duterte. This phase means it…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The prosecution panel is now preparing for the possible presentation of evidence for its unexplained wealth allegations against Vice President Sara Duterte.
This phase means it will start calling witnesses and showing proof, should there be changes to the schedule, Bicol Saro party-list Rep. Terry Ridon said on Thursday.

Ridon said in a press briefing that he is aware of the possibility that the team will be called by mid-September to present its case, should the prosecution panel decide to drop Article III or the bribery case.
The lawmaker is a public prosecutor and prosecution team leader for Article II of the Articles of Impeachment.
Article II deals with allegations that Duterte and her husband Manases Carpio had unexplained wealth which were not declared on her Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN).
Article III focuses on allegations that the vice president bribed several officials of the Department of Education.
“The team tasked to present the unexplained wealth case is preparing for the entry of our article,” Ridon told reporters at the Batasang Pambansa.

“And we also acknowledge that there are conversations as to no longer presenting bribery accusations and moving straight to the unexplained wealth article. We will decide (on) it in due time,” he noted.

“But as far as the unexplained wealth team is concerned, we are preparing so that by the middle of September or towards the end of the month, we can lay down evidence before the Senate Impeachment Court,” he added.
The prosecution also confirmed that its members have received copies of the bank and tax records of the Duterte-Carpio couple and their business interests.
These materials will be studied by the team to see if these items can be presented in the impeachment trial.
“Yesterday afternoon, the prosecution was given a copy of all the bank information of our vice president, her husband and their companies,” Ridon said.
“The Senate Impeachment Court also gave the prosecution panel a copy of all the tax documents of the vice president, her husband and their companies,” he noted.

“So, in the coming days, we will study and scrutinize all these documents, as this will constitute the last important pillar of the evidence that we will use to prove the allegations under the unexplained wealth article,” the legislator said.
It was Ridon who focused on the alleged issues with Duterte’s SALN when the House committee on justice tackled the two impeachment complaints against the vice president.
Ridon said last April that there was an increase in the vice president’s net worth that is not proportionate to her salary, noting that her net worth rose by over 1,000 percent from 2008 to 2024.

He explained that Duterte’s SALN in 2008 showed a net worth of P18.4 million, while her net worth in her 2023 SALN grew to P77.5 million and P88.5 million for 2024 — representing a 378 percent increase from 2008 to 2024.

However, the lawmaker noted that if figures were based on Duterte’s 2007 SALN — the first year that she became a public official — the jump from a net worth of P7.2 million to 2024’s P88.5 million represents a 1,120 percent spike.
Aside from the SALN issue, Ridon also previously pointed out before the confirmation from Anti-Money Laundering Council Executive Director Buenaventura.
Buenaventura affirmed that they saw covered and suspicious transactions made by Duterte and Carpio, and a total of P6.7 billion in total transactions from bank accounts from the couple.
This includes a total of P4.4 billion in inflows and P1.5 billion worth of outflows.
Meanwhile, several members of the prosecution confirmed that they are mulling whether they will drop Article III or the bribery allegations due to time constraints.
On Wednesday, Manila Rep. Joel Chua confirmed in an ambush interview that the prosecution panel is considering to refrain from presenting Article III.
In a press briefing later that day, Chua clarified that the bribery allegations against Duterte remain strong.
He noted that the only reason why the prosecution panel has considered this article as expendable is due to priorities and a yearning to expedite the trial.
Chua explained that if they push through with the withdrawal of Article III, this will be similar to what the prosecution panel did for the impeachment trial of former Chief Justice Renato Corona.

However, he also stressed that this is not a new matter, reminding the public that the group had said before that if the prosecution is satisfied with the evidence and testimonies at hand, it will let go of one article. /apl

articles.title: Tulfo questions Hiraya Water’s SEC registration as pub operator
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Raffy Tulfo on Thursday questioned Hiraya Water Corporation over its Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filings that listed restaurants, parlors, beer houses and…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Raffy Tulfo on Thursday questioned Hiraya Water Corporation over its Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filings that listed restaurants, parlors, beer houses and snack bars as its nature of business despite its operation of water utilities.
Tulfo, who chairs the Senate Committee on Public Services, asked Hiraya President Jose Paulino Santamarina about the company’s corporate records.

“According to your SEC records, ang nature of business ninyo ay beer house and beauty parlor. So kung expert kayo sa pagpapatakbo ng mga GRO, mamasan, beauty parlor, paano pa kaya itong patubig?” Tulfo said during Thursday’s hearing.

(According to your SEC records, your nature of business are beer houses and beauty parlors. So if you’re an expert in operating GROs, pimps, and beauty parlors, how will you be able to handle water concerns?)
Santamarina said he was unaware of the discrepancy and that he would have to check the company’s SEC filings with its legal counsel.
Tulfo said Santamarina, as president of the company, should have been aware of the contents of its SEC filing.

“I apologize po. Ang alam ko lang po, nagbago na ang management at bagong direksyon at bago na ang investment para po sa Prime. Kailangan naming palitan dahil nagbago na po lahat. Hindi ko alam na ganito ‘yung finile,” Santamarina said.

(I apologize. All I know is that the management has changed, and there is a new direction and new investment for Prime. We needed to change it because everything had changed. I did not know that this was what had been filed)
Page 2 says otherwise

According to Santamarina, the company’s primary purpose is establishing, maintaining, operating, managing or administering and supervising a waterworks system, including authority to own and operate drilling rigs, machinery, pumps and other equipment necessary for the operation.
SEC Representative lawyer Ria Alexandra Castillo later clarified that the company’s latest General Information Sheet (GIS), filed on May 29, 2026, reflected waterworks as its primary purpose.

On the second page, however, under the description of the nature of business, the filing listed “restaurants, refreshment centers, parlors, bars, beer houses, snack bars, fast-food centers, and other similar establishment.”
“Maybe it’s an oversight on your part?” Tulfo asked the SEC.
Castillo then said they will further validate the matter.

The exchange came amid the committee’s broader inquiry into the transition from PrimeWater to Hiraya Water Corporation, including the company’s service obligations, capital expenditures and contracts with local water districts.
SEC asked to look into Hiraya Water name
Meanwhile, Tulfo also raised concerns over Hiraya Water Corporation’s registered name, which was causing confusion with a tech company also using the “Hiraya Water” name.
Hiraya Technology Solutions, Inc., a smart water management company, is registered with the SEC as “Hiraya Water.”

The tech company’s CEO, Stephen Larcia, told the Senate panel that the similarity in names had resulted in consumers mistakenly sending complaints intended for Hiraya Water Corporation to their tech company.
This, he said, was causing problems for their company, particularly with its after-sales and customer-related concerns.
Tulfo then instructed the SEC to look into the possibility of requiring Hiraya Water Corporation to change its corporate name, or taking other appropriate action, to prevent further confusion.
Castillo supported Tulfo’s position.

The hearing also tackled complaints from consumers over poor water supply, high water bills, limited service hours, and muddy-looking water, as well as questions surrounding Hiraya’s capital expenditure commitments and its assumption of existing PrimeWater contracts and obligations. /gsg

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Sandiganbayan Fifth Division on Thursday ordered the release of former Public Works and Highways Secretary Manuel “Manny” Bonoan.

This came two days after the court granted a motion by state prosecutors to exclude Bonoan from the graft and plunder charges against him, Sen. Jose “Jinggoy” Estrada and three former DPWH district engineers.
The motion came amid a bid by the Office of the Ombudsman to use Bonoan as a state witness in other cases related to the flood control corruption scandal.
Bonoan had been under hospital arrest since last June at the Philippine National Police General Hospital (PNPGH) in Camp Crame due to several illnesses.

Estrada, then-South Manila District Engineering Office (DEO) chief Manny Bulusan, then-Quezon City 1st DEO chief Arturo Gonzales Jr. and then-North Manila DEO assistant chief Denryl Caesar Cortuna are accused of amassing a total of P573.75 million in kickbacks through projects included in the 2025 national budget.

In an interview in Camp Crame later on Thursday, PNP public information chief Col. Allen Rae Co said, “We defer always to the orders of the Sandiganbayan kung siya ay free na to go as long as he’s able.”
(We defer always to the orders of the Sandiganbayan if he’s free to go as long as he’s able.)

blocks.text: CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY — The Army’s 4th Infantry Division (4ID) coordinated closely with the 1st ID (1ID) on Wednesday in case any untoward incident arose from the military’s move to bar a Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) convoy from entering Kolambugan, Lanao del Norte.

The police and military intercepted the MILF convoy involving some 200 individuals, half of whom were armed, due to a lack of coordination, causing fears and traffic delays along the highway. The MILF members were on the way to Munai, Lanao del Norte to attend a meeting. They agreed to be escorted back to Picong, Lanao del Sur after authorities talked with their leaders.

Col. Joe Patrick Martinez, 4ID spokesperson, said on Thursday that an inter-military command coordination happened during the incident. He said that while division territories are clearly marked, mission flexibility always takes precedence over territorial borders.
“Kolambugan is part of 1ID’s area of responsibility (AOR). Usually, we secure adjacent boundaries of the two divisions to provide support,” Martinez said.
He added: “But if the situation escalates, (the Eastern Mindanao Command) will task us to deploy units inside 1ID’s AOR to support them directly.”/coa

articles.title: Data centers are everywhere. Here's what they're doing to the planet.
articles.summary: As data centers multiply to meet AI demand, they're straining power grids, draining water supplies, and reshaping the land and air around them.

image.caption: Rows of servers hum inside Google's data center in Douglas County, Georgia — one of thousands of facilities worldwide powering the AI boom.Image: Connie Zhou/ZUMA/picture alliance

blocks.text: Every question sent to AI models provides an instant reply that seems to appear out of nowhere, but answering queries requires physical infrastructure that consumes real energy, water, and land.

Somewhere around the world — maybe in Virginia or Sao Paolo or Hong Kong — a massive warehouse filled with fiber-optic cables and seemingly endless rows of humming servers, is working to provide the processing power for the more than 2.5 billion questions ChatGPT alone fields daily.

AI models, along with cloud storage, streaming, web hosting and social media, all have a very real physical footprint. If data centers were a country, their level of electricity use would make them the 11th largest electricity consumer in the world, according to researchers from the United Nations University.
From energy to water to land, here's the real toll data centers take on the environment.

blocks.caption: Every query typed into a chatbot like ChatGPT sets off a chain of physical processes in data centers around the world.Image: CHRISTIAN BEUTLER/KEYSTONE/picture alliance

blocks.text: An insatiable appetite for power

Data centers are becoming some of the world's fastest-growing sources of electricity. These warehouses of servers, routers and Internet-connected devices run 24/7, while cooling systems operate continuously to keep the tech from overheating.

In Frankfurt, Germany, the grid is currently so saturated that no new connections will be available until at least the 2030s. There, data centers consume about 41% of the city’s electricity. In Dublin, it’s double that.

And data center electricity consumption is growing rapidly — it’s expected to double by 2030 to about 945 terawatt-hours, around what Japan consumes annually, according to the International Energy Agency.
How the AI boom could slow climate progress
All that energy has to come from somewhere, increasing reliance on fossil fuels.

One 2024 study found that more than half of the United States’ data centers are powered by fossil fuels, emitting in excess of 105 million tons of CO2. Offsetting that would take more than 31,000 wind turbines running continuously for a year.

The buildout is also keeping old coal plants alive. Utilities have delayed the retirement of 15 coal-fired plants nationwide to meet surging demand, plants that together emitted nearly 65 million tons of greenhouse gases in 2023 alone.

blocks.caption: A technician checks equipment at an Amazon Web Services data center in New Carlisle, Indiana, one of the facilities straining local power grids to keep up with demand.Image: Noah Berger/REUTERS

blocks.text: And utilities are also constructing new gas-fired power plants, with more than 100 GW of additional facilities across the country already announced. That would lead to more carbon emissions than burning 111 million pounds (50.4 million kilos)of coal.

Of course, data centers can also be powered by renewable energy. Pairing a facility with on-site renewables can ease pressure on the local power supply, and any surplus energy can even be sold back to the grid, making it more stable.
However, using green electricity for data centers means there is less available for electrifying transport or decarbonizing other emissions-heavy industries.
The hidden water demand

Many data centers consume millions of gallons of water to stay cool. Servers generate constant heat, and water is one of the most effective ways to absorb and carry that heat away through evaporation.

A single large facility can use up to 5 million gallons a day, roughly the same as a town of 10,000 to 50,000 people. About 80% of the water withdrawn for cooling simply evaporates; the rest becomes wastewater that can overwhelm local treatment systems never designed to handle that volume.

In Northern Virginia, the almost 300 data centers clustered in one region, supply about a third of the world’s online traffic. There, in what is known as the world's data center capital, facilities collectively used nearly 2 billion gallons of water in 2023.

There are several more efficient ways to cool data centers. These include immersion cooling, where devices are bathed in a coolant, and closed-loop cooling systems which recycle water and can reduce freshwater use by up to 70%.

blocks.caption: Demonstrators in Fredericksburg, Virginia, joined a nationwide protest against data centers in July 2026, with many signs targeting the industry's heavy water use.Image: Evelyn Hockstein/REUTERS

blocks.text: Data centers are making cities hotter
Cooling a data center doesn't get rid of the heat, it just moves it outside, which can exacerbate the urban heat island effect, which is when cities experience higher tempertures than rural areas.

Researchin Phoenix, Arizona, found a single large data center can emit as much waste heat as tens or even hundreds of thousands of households, raising nearby land surface temperatures by up to 9 degrees Celsius and air temperatures by up to 2 degrees Celsius. Those effects can be felt as far as half a kilometer away.

Since cities are already 0.5–4 degrees Celsius warmer than their surroundings, these higher temperatures can increase heat stress risks for nearby residents and push up air conditioning demand, requiring still yet more energy.

Not all of that heat goes to waste: a growing number of data centers are capturing it and piping it into nearby homes and businesses — this process, called thermal energy networks, can reduce data center power demand by up to 30%.
Data centers in space: Solution or disaster?
Coal, gas, and diesel all contribute to dirty air
Powering and running data centers pollutes the air on two fronts.
First, coal and gas plants release toxic particulate matter, which can lead to respiratory disease, heart disease, asthma and more health conditions for nearby communities.
On-site diesel generators, used as backup power when the grid fails, also release harmful air pollutants. These generators pump out 200 to 600 times more nitrogen oxides than natural gas plants.

One estimate found that when backup generators for all of Virginia’s data centers were emitting at just 10% of their permitted level, they could contribute to 14,000 cases of asthma symptoms, more than a dozen deaths and up to $300 million in public health costs a year.
The land data centers take over
Data center construction requires large plots of land to build on. Repurposing natural and agricultural areas into industrial zones can threaten biodiversity and disrupt local ecosystems.

In Hattersheim, Germany, for example, an 18-acre parcel reserved for agriculture and groundwater protection — a local green space known for its rapeseed blossoms — was rezoned in 2024 to make way for a five-building data center campus.
The damage often extends beyond the site itself. Gas pipelines and power plants built to supply these facilities require their own land, fragmenting habitats and eroding soil along their routes.
Why does AI need so much energy?

articles.title: Sandiganbayan orders release of Manuel Bonoan from hospital detention
articles.summary: The Sandiganbayan on Thursday ordered the release of former Public Works Secretary Manuel Bonoan from hospital detention.

blocks.text: Published September 3, 2026 4:51pm
The Sandiganbayan on Thursday ordered the release of former Public Works Secretary Manuel Bonoan from hospital detention.

According to its resolution dated September 1, the Sandiganbayan Fifth Division ordered Bonoan's release because of its earlier ruling removing the former secretary from the list of accused in the P573 million plunder and graft cases related to the flood control scandal.
Bonoan, in exchange, will serve as one of the government witnesses in its flood control-related cases.

“Accordingly, the oral motion of Atty. Ong is hereby granted. The Commitment Orders (Pending Trial) issued by this court against Manuel Manligas Bonoan in Crim. Case No. E-SB26CRM0005 and Crim. Case No. E-SB26CRM0006, dated June 19, 2026, are hereby recalled,” the resolution read.

The same resolution tasked Police Brig. Gen. Portia Manalad of the Philippine National Police (PNP) Health Service General Hospital to release Bonoan from custody “unless he is being detained for other lawful reason.”
Bonoan’s counsel, Stefanie Liz Ong, moved for the release of Bonoan before the anti-graft court on Thursday, September 3.
Bonoan is still facing a graft charge also in relation to the flood control mess before the Sandiganbayan's Second Division.
Graft, however, is a bailable offense, and he has already posted a P90,000 bail in connection with that charge. –NB, GMA News

articles.title: Sandiganbayan affirms denial of Jinggoy Estrada's plea to fix bail in plunder case
articles.summary: The Sandiganbayan has affirmed its July 2026 decision denying Senator Jinggoy Estrada"s motion to fix bail in the P573-million plunder case he is facing over his alleged involvement in the flood…

blocks.text: Published September 3, 2026 4:48pm

The Sandiganbayan has affirmed its July 2026 decision denying Senator Jinggoy Estrada’s motion to fix bail in the P573-million plunder case he is facing over his alleged involvement in the flood control mess, citing lack of merit.
In its September 3 resolution, the Sandiganbayan Fifth Division said Estrada’s appeal “failed to demonstrate any substantial error of fact or law.”

“Accused Estrada’s motion for reconsideration places considerable emphasis on circumstances which, according to him, establish that he poses no risk of flight. He repetitively points to his incumbency as a Senator, his long tenure in public service, and his history of compliance with this court’s travel conditions. The court does not disregard these, but they do not answer the main issue presently confronting the court,” the Sandiganbayan said.

“The constitutional query in a case involving an offense punishable by reclusion perpetua is not confined to whether the accused is likely to flee. It principally requires a judicial determination of whether the evidence of guilt is strong. An accused’s established ties to the community, public position, previous compliance with travel restrictions, or history of appearing before the courts cannot substitute for that determination,” it added.

The anti-graft court noted that even assuming Estrada is not a flight risk, this circumstance is not sufficient for the court “to dispense with the requisite bail proceedings and immediately fix bail.”
“Until a hearing determines that the evidence of guilt is not strong, the court has no basis to set a bail amount,” it said.
Estrada has already filed a petition for bail before the Fifth Division.

Aside from the plunder charge, Estrada is also facing two counts of graft in connection with the alleged flood control corruption scandal—one before the Fifth Division and another before the Second Division.
Estrada refused to enter a plea in the plunder and graft cases on Thursday, prompting the Fifth Division to enter a not guilty plea on his behalf. — VBL, GMA News
