articles.title: Marcoleta raises jurisdiction issue over campaign contribution case
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Rodante Marcoleta said the issue regarding the P75 million campaign donation he received, which became the subject of his plunder case should be under the jurisdiction of…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Rodante Marcoleta said the issue regarding the P75 million campaign donation he received, which became the subject of his plunder case should be under the jurisdiction of the Commission on Elections (Comelec) and not the Sandiganbayan Third Division.

Marcoleta, a lawyer by profession, relayed this position through his counsel David Gabriel during Thursday’s court hearing where both of his motions to dismiss the case and withhold his 90-day suspension as senator were tackled.
“It is the position of accused Senator Marcoleta that it (the jurisdiction) should be with the Comelec,” Gabriel told the court.
Associate Justice Karl Miranda, Third Division chairperson, said the matter regarding his two motions are now submitted for resolution.
Gabriel also said Marcoleta filed a petition for certiorari before the Supreme Court, seeking the high court’s review of the anti-graft court’s ruling.
The lawyer said they questioned the validity of the information containing the formal criminal charges against Marcoleta due to issues on jurisdiction.
Associate Justice Ronald Moreno, however, said that Marcoleta already pleaded not guilty in the formal criminal charges against him in his arraignment in July.
At that time, Marcoleta even “voluntarily” withdrew his pending motion to quash information or his bid to junk the case so he could be finally arraigned.
Moreno said the court would have dismissed Marcoleta’s case if the information was not “valid” in the first place.
Gabriel, however, maintained that Comelec has “continuing jurisdiction” in Marcoleta’s case “because it is related to elections.”
Prosecutor Joshua Tan, however, noted that Marcoleta himself “made it clear that it is not a campaign contribution.”
During Marcoleta’s bail hearing, Victoria Kadeja Besinio of the Comelec’s Political Finance and Affairs Department said the senator declared the P75 million as a “personal fund.”
However, during cross examination, Besinio said that: “We did not determine if it is an election contribution or personal funds.”

Marcoleta, his donors former Rep. Mike Defensor and businessmen, Joseph Espiritu and Aristotle Viray face plunder over a P75 million campaign donation the senator received while being a sitting party-list lawmaker, which, according to prosecutors, was not declared in the senator’s financial and campaign disclosures.
Of the said amount, P30 million allegedly came from Defensor, P25 million from Espiritu, and P20 million from Viray. /gsg

articles.title: Haze triggers poor air quality in Northern Mindanao
articles.summary: CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY — Environment and health agencies in Region 10 have warned the public that prolonged exposure to haze and fine particulate matter (PM) poses health risks, particularly for people…

blocks.text: CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY — Environment and health agencies in Region 10 have warned the public that prolonged exposure to haze and fine particulate matter (PM) poses health risks, particularly for people with respiratory and cardiovascular conditions and those who spend extended periods outdoors.

The Environmental Management Bureau-Region 10 (EMB-10) urged vulnerable groups in Northern Mindanao to take precautions after it recorded elevated PM2.5 levels in several monitoring stations across the region.

The bureau particularly reminded children, older persons, pregnant individuals, and people with existing respiratory or cardiovascular conditions to stay vigilant, as exposure to fine particulate matter may pose greater health risks.

As of Thursday, the DENR-X monitoring station in Cagayan de Oro recorded a PM2.5 reading of 133 based on the 24-hour rolling average. The level falls under the “Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups” category, meaning people with respiratory illnesses, including asthma, may be more vulnerable to the air pollution and should limit prolonged or strenuous outdoor activity.

Meanwhile, air quality was considerably poorer in Tagoloan, Misamis Oriental, and Iligan City, where PM2.5 readings reached 234 and 244, respectively. At these levels, the pollution is a greater health concern for people with heart and respiratory conditions, prompting recommendations to remain indoors, rest, and avoid unnecessary travel.
EMB-10 recommended wearing a well-fitting N95, particularly in areas experiencing elevated pollution levels.
The agency also encouraged residents to stay updated on official air-quality readings as conditions can change anytime.

In a separate advisory, the Department of Health Center for Health Development in Northern Mindanao (DOH-10) called particular attention to people whose occupations require prolonged outdoor exposure.
Among those identified were public utility drivers, delivery riders, street vendors, field workers, and others who spend extended periods outside.
People who develop difficulty breathing, persistent coughing, eye irritation, or other concerning symptoms are advised to seek appropriate medical attention, the DOH-10 said.
The DOH-10 also urged the public to monitor official health and air quality advisories and follow recommended safety measures while the haze persists./coa

articles.title: Mayors, treasurers form strongest corruption link
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The officials most frequently connected in corruption cases are not two politicians working together, but an elected official and a bureaucrat whose position provides access to…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The officials most frequently connected in corruption cases are not two politicians working together, but an elected official and a bureaucrat whose position provides access to the government’s finances.

This was pointed out by Dr. Alicor Panao, a data scientist for the Inquirer and an associate professor at the University of the Philippines, in a network analysis of more than 1,800 public officials involved in over 400 cases before the Sandiganbayan from 2016 to 2025.
Panao explained that corruption is often imagined as a deal between politicians, with one elected official helping another divert public resources and steer or manipulate government contracts.

But Panao said this is not always the case, stressing that a closer look reveals a more intricate picture — one involving elected and appointed officials, such as local chief executives and treasurers.

blocks.caption: inqmetrics

blocks.text: “Together, these relationships suggest that corruption networks are not confined to political alliances. They also run through the administrative relationships that connect political authority to the government bureaucracy,” he said.

Based on the network analysis, Panao said mayors and treasurers formed the strongest connection, with a weight of 83, followed by accountants and mayors at 72. Accountants and treasurers registered a weight of 63.

The connection between accountants and budget officers had a weight of 51, while budget officers and local chief executives were connected in 45 cases. Budget officers and treasurers were connected in 38 cases.
“The pattern extends across the local government machinery, with engineers linked to mayors 30 times and to treasurers 25 times,” Panao said.

A different but equally revealing pattern emerged at the national level, Panao said. Bureau directors were most frequently connected with members of the House of Representatives, while representatives also had recurring links with chief accountants.
Accountants and regional directors likewise formed a notable connection, with a weight of 18.

“Public money rarely moves through a single office. A government transaction typically passes through a chain of political decisions, budgeting, procurement, accounting, approval and disbursement,” Panao said.
Based on the established network, “officials occupying different points along this chain repeatedly appear together in graft cases.”
“Corruption, therefore, may be shaped not only by individual choices but also by the institutional relationships through which government transactions are carried out,” Panao explained.
“This has important implications for anti-corruption efforts,” he said.

“If corruption repeatedly concentrates at the points where political authority intersects with financial and administrative control, then those institutional connections may deserve scrutiny alongside the individuals who occupy them,” Panao said. /dm

“The second one is on September 15, which is the submission of the counter-affidavits of the respondents,” Dato said.
Baterbonia and Adili died in a drowning incident during a team-building activity of the Ateneo de Manila University Blue Eagles in Dipaculao, Aurora, on June 8.

Following the incident, the Philippine National Police-Criminal Investigation and Detection Group recommended filing complaints against Baldwin and others for alleged violations of the Anti-Hazing Act, as well as homicide and reckless imprudence resulting in homicide.

When asked about the hazing charge, Dato said only the complaint for reckless imprudence resulting in homicide passed DOJ Department Circular No. 20, which requires prosecutors to participate in case build-up.
“They would have to agree on the appropriate charges, and the one charge that was able to pass DC 20 was reckless imprudence resulting in homicide,” he said.
Meanwhile, DOJ spokesperson Polo Martinez said the complaint for violations of the Anti-Hazing Act remains under case build-up.
In a video posted by the university on June 12, Baldwin apologized to the families of the student-athletes. However, Baterbonia’s mother said an apology was not enough.
Baldwin and former team manager Epok Quimpo resigned following the incident. — VBL, GMA News

articles.title: UK mortgage borrowers brace for rate jump amid global bond sell-off
articles.summary: Swap rates rise to three-year high as increase in oil prices leads to fears of higher inflation

blocks.text: Homeowners in the UK are braced for a jump in mortgage rates, driven by higher inflation and interest rate increase expectations amid turmoil in the global bond markets.
UK swap rates, which lenders use to price mortgages, have risen to a three-year high, as this week’s global bond market sell-off ripples through the economy.
The five-year swaps rate rose above 4.52% on Wednesday, the highest level since October 2023. This is expected to result in higher interest rates on fixed-term mortgages.

A jump in oil prices, as the US and Iran have exchanged fire this week for the first time in a month, has led to fears of higher inflation, leading investors to sell bonds, which pushes up their yield, or interest rate. The moves in gilts, as UK government bonds are known as, have been bigger than those in other countries.
Although the turmoil in the bond markets eased on Thursday, the consequences of the jump in bond yields could be serious for borrowers.
That is because UK swap rates – the interest rates that banks charge when they borrow from each other – have been pushed up by the rise in gilt yields.

Russ Mould, the investment director at the trading platform AJ Bell, said: “Credit card, mortgage and auto loan interest rates will rise if bond yields rise, as the lenders seek to preserve loan book margins and manage their risk.”
If the cost of government borrowing continues to remain high, it could undermine Andy Burnham’s efforts to ease cost of living pressures.

The new prime minister attempted to calm volatile bond markets on Wednesday, using his first appearance at prime minister’s questions to promise decisions for the autumn budget would be “grounded in fiscal responsibility”.

He spoke as the yield on UK 10-year government debt hit its highest level since 2008 for a second day, before retreating thanks to a drop in the oil price. On Thursday, Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, dipped 0.6% to $95 a barrel.

Oil has been one of the key factors driving the bond market sell-off, as inflationary pressures from high prices could force central banks to raise interest rates, along with worries over high government spending. Government bonds are also competing with a flurry of corporate debt issuance by technology companies keen to fund their spending on AI infrastructure.
after newsletter promotion

Tom Simpson, the managing director of homes at Yorkshire Building Society, said swap rates were now 0.7% above where they were a year ago, but there was “much more volatility” in March, at the start of the Iran war.

“All things being equal, you would expect a modest increase in mortgage rates based on what we’ve seen so far,” he told the BBC, advising people who were worried about this to speak to an independent mortgage adviser.

“When there is a movement in the market, that can pull forward demand. People will try to lock those rates in.” However, he added that the 0.1 percentage point increase over the past week was below the 0.5 percentage point increase in the 10 days after the US and Israel first launched airstrikes on Tehran.
Fixed-year mortgage rates were unchanged on Thursday, according to the latest figures from Moneyfacts. The average two-year fix is 5.59%, while a typical five-year fixed deal costs 5.63%.

articles.title: Greens’ Zack Polanski to stand in byelection for Keir Starmer’s seat – UK politics live
articles.summary:
Green party leader announces run in Holborn and St Pancras constituency in north London following the resignation of former PM

Here is the Camden New Journal’s

blocks.text: Polanski says he can win Holborn and St Pancras for Greens attacking Labour as party of 'corporations and big money'

Zack Polanski has confirmed that he wants to be the Green party’s candidate in the Holborn and St Pancras byelection in an interview with the Camden New Journal – the local paper where Keir Starmer also announced he was standing down as the constituency’s MP.
He said:

double quotation markI have lived and worked in this community over many years, I know it well and I love it It represents so many of the things that make London so special. I am so excited by the prospect of representing this place in parliament. Holborn and St Pancras has everything that’s the best of our country and so much potential. But for too long now it’s been held back by governments who have failed to make the changes to improve people’s lives. We know that the Greens can win here, and by electing me, voters will have someone who will always fight their corner – never scared of big donors or the party whip. Too often Labour has stood up for corporations and big money. I will stand up for people struggling to pay their bills.

Starmer had a majority of 11.572 at the last election and polling figures, and the results of the May local elections, suggest Labour should win the byelection. But Polanski has shown he is a formidable campaigner, and with him as the Green party’s candidate, Labour will face a much tougher challenge holding the seat.
Polanski said he would put “making life more affordable” at the heart of his campaign.

double quotation markIt’s a clear fight between Labour and the Green party. We know that people are struggling – that the things we used to afford are increasingly out of reach – and this is a chance to send a very clear message that we won’t sit by as we get poorer and extreme wealth is concentrated at the very top. What voters in Holborn and St Pancras will get with me as their MP is someone totally dedicated to standing up for them. Put simply I will use my place in parliament to force the current Labour government into making life more affordable for the people who live here.

Before Polanski officially becomes the Green party’s candidate, he has to be selected by the local party. But it is not expected that this will be a problem for him. Polanski is hugely popular with party members, and last year won the leadership contest with 84% of the vote.

blocks.text: These are from Rob Ford, a politics professor and elections specialist, on what Zack Polanski being the Green party’s candidate means for the Holborn and St Pancras byelection.

double quotation markBig stakes now for both parties. Greens have chance to turn the tide on recent decline & show Polanski is a winner. Labour have a chance to show the Burnham bounce is real, consolidate the left in a London heartland seat, & deal a potential knockout blow to Green insurgency.

double quotation markAs I said a couple of days ago, Polanski candidature may change how voters in the seat see contest. No longer just Green vs Lab - it is now “would you like the national leader of the Green party or a generic Lab backbencher as your local representative?”

double quotation markIt is quite possible for Labour to lose despite being popular nationally and, indeed, in seat itself, because voters understand stakes: Green gain still leaves Burnham in charge with huge majority, but means a high profile progressive voice in Commons, representing Holborn & St P

double quotation markIf you are a young progressive voter who thinks “I like Burnham but I don’t trust him to listen to us, particularly given how the first two yrs of this govt went”, then a “vote Polanski in to keep Burnham honest” message is going to be quite attractive.

double quotation markThere are an awful lot of such voters in this seat - lots of students & young grad professionals (seat is v near UCL), & lots of migrant origin & ethnic minority voters too. All groups Lab has struggled with in recent yrs - what will Burnham’s message be to win back their trust?

blocks.text: Zack Polanski to stand as Green party's candidate in Holborn and St Pancras byelection
Green Party leader Zack Polanski has said he will stand in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election which was triggered when Keir Starmer announced he was quitting as an MP.
Burnham meets Macron at No 10, as more French officers deployed to stop small boat crossings

Good morning. Nothing is new in life or politics, and the concern that people feel about small boats crossing the Channel now is minimal compared to the alarm that Britons must have felt in 1066 as the Duke of Normandy’s invasion force arrived in England. Almost 1,000 years later, the horror is long forgotten and Andy Burnham was with the French president, Emmanuel Macron, at the British Museum last night to celebrate the Bayeux Tapestry as “the best possible symbol” of the “entente amicale” between France and the UK, as King Charles put it in a speech last night.

blocks.caption: Left to right: Andy Burnham, France’s President Emmanuel Macron and King Charles III inspecting the the Bayeux Tapestry at the British Museum in London. Photograph: Ludovic Marin -Pool/SIPA/Shutterstock

blocks.text: This morning Burnham is hosting Macron for political talks in Downing Street and another fleet of small boats will be on the agenda. As Rajeev Syal reports, ahead of the meeting No 10 has announced that the UK and France have increased the number of police on the French coast to stop so-called “mega dinghies” from launching across the English Channel. Rajeev says:

double quotation markWhile the combined total number of boat crossings over the summer months has dropped to its lowest since 2019, smugglers appear to have started loading more people onto fewer, larger vessels. Dinghies are now being launched as far as 150 miles southwest of Calais. Downing Street said measures to counter the trend include deploying a surge team of 45 officers to France’s western beaches in the coming weeks, almost tripling resources in the area. A specialist French intelligence and judicial team seeking to root out and prosecute smuggling networks has grown from 18 to 30 officers. And a new 75-strong unit focused on curbing crossings has begun operations in northern France, taking the total number of officers to nearly 1,050. Home Office officials have recently claimed that 15-metre boats which can carry 230 people are being launched because hardline tactics used by French police and funded by the UK are working. The BBC reported on Thursday that people smugglers are being forced to work together and use larger boats, and have increased their prices for a Channel journey from €1,300 to €1,700 (£1120 to £1460) over the last year.
Critics are saying both governments should be doing more.
There are other important issues on the agenda for the talks too. Kiran Stacey has a preview here.
We will also be hearing a lot today from the Conservatives and Reform UK. Here is the agenda for the day.
10am: Kemi Badenoch gives a speech on defence, and how the Conservatives would fund a rise in defence spending to 3% of GDP by 2030.

11am: Robert Jenrick, the Reform UK Treasury spokesperson, speaks on a panel at the Reform conference’s ‘business day’. Suella Braverman, the education spokesperson, is also speaking at an event. The main conference starts tomorrow.
Around 11am: Emmanuel Macron, the French president, arrives at Downing Street for talks with Andy Burnham.

articles.title: Embattled Spanish PM insists there were no prior warnings before Ceuta crisis
articles.summary: Pedro Sánchez tells parliament it is absurd to think the government knew and did nothing, after thousands join protests in Spanish cities.

blocks.text: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has said no-one foresaw the influx of 72,000 migrants in the exclave of Ceuta, as pressure mounts over his handling of the crisis.

"It's absurd to think that the government knew and did nothing," Sánchez told Spain's parliament on Thursday, hours after tens of thousands of people joined protests across the country backed by opposition parties.
Sánchez also maintained there was no evidence Morocco was behind the mass crossing and there had been "close co-ordination" between the two countries.
A Spanish police report has highlighted the "total permissiveness" of Moroccan security forces, although senior officials insist it does not point the finger at Rabat.
Although most of the migrants have been sent back to Morocco, some 5,000 remain on the streets and beaches of Ceuta, on the North African coast, including as many as 1,400 children.

There have been several reports that Spanish officials had been warned of a rise in sea arrivals over the border at Ceuta, following a Spanish court ruling that many migrants misunderstood to mean they would not be pushed back if they swam across.

Sánchez has been careful until now not to criticise Morocco, but he complained of "unacceptable" statements by two Moroccan ministers about Ceuta and its fellow Spanish exclave of Melilla. The two cities have the EU's only land borders in North Africa.
Spain's handling of the migrant influx angered some of its European partners, and Italy responded by imposing border restrictions on arrivals from Spain.
"Ceuta is not the border of Spain, it is Spain on the border [of Europe]," Sánchez told parliament.

He praised the response of Ceuta police who had chosen to "defend human life" when the influx took place, rather than defend the border. He also highlighted close co-operation with Moroccan authorities over the return of more than 90% of the migrants in the following 72 hours.
He addressed the "difficult times" faced by the residents of Ceuta, as he explained the "complexity" of what had happened on 30 and 31 July.
He spoke of an "episode in which numerous actors and interests converge", doubling down on his assertion that hoaxes and rumours spread by social media had sparked the crisis.

He has already blamed trafficking gangs and angered Russia and Israel for highlighting social media linked to both countries along with "an international far-right movement". He told MPs that there was no evidence of state actors being involved but doubled down on his allegations of accounts linked to the two countries.
Ceuta was "a humanitarian crisis and also an administrative challenge within the city itself", he added.

Foreign Minister S Jaishankar arrives in Poland, next stop Ukraine
India's External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar has reached the Polish capital of Warsaw as he kickstarts an official visit to Poland and Ukraine on Thursday.

During the three-day tour, which runs until Saturday, Jaishankar is scheduled to meet Poland's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski and Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha for bilateral consultations, the foreign ministry in New Delhi said in a statement.
The ministry added that the visit is focused on "enhancing bilateral relations" and will also provide an opportunity to "exchange views on regional developments and issues of mutual interest."
The foreign minister was greeted at the airport in Warsaw on Wednesday by India's ambassador to Poland, Neeta Bhushan.
Jaishankar's trip to Poland comes amid speculation about a visit by Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk to India.
Earlier in August, Poland's top envoy to India said that Tusk's visit, which would be his third to New Delhi, would send a strong signal for cooperation.
There is yet to be formal confirmation of Tusk's India tour.
The visit also reflects broader efforts by New Delhi to deepen engagement with Central and Eastern European partners.
Following the Poland leg of his tour, Jaishankar will head to Ukraine.
Jaishankar's Ukraine visit comes after key Modi-Putin meeting

The Ukraine leg of Jaishankar's tour comes days after Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Russian President Vladimir Putin during the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, on Monday. During the meeting, Modi urged an end to the war in Ukraine.

Ahead of Jaishankar's arrival in Kyiv, Ukraine's First Deputy Head of the Office of the President, Sergiy Kyslytsya, said on Tuesday that he had met India's Ambassador to Ukraine, Anjani Kumar, to discuss Kyiv-New Delhi ties and India's role in efforts to end Russia's war against Ukraine.
Kyslytsya said he discussed with Kumar Modi's message to Putin in Bishkek, in which the Indian prime minister urged a "move from endless war to end of war" in Ukraine.
"We look forward to continued dialogue with India and to translating this shared interest in peace into concrete steps," Kyslytsya added.

articles.title: Nepal PM warns of risks as scientists flag more glacial disasters
articles.summary: KATHMANDU — Prime Minister Balendra Shah has urged the international community to recognise the August 26 Bhotekoshi flood as a warning of the growing climate risks confronting the Himalayan…

blocks.text: KATHMANDU — Prime Minister Balendra Shah has urged the international community to recognise the August 26 Bhotekoshi flood as a warning of the growing climate risks confronting the Himalayan region.

Briefing the House of Representatives on the losses caused by the disaster and the government’s response on Wednesday, he said the moment has come to bring these growing risks more urgently to the attention of the international community.

“Experts have said that the flood in the Bhotekoshi River in Rasuwa was triggered by a massive rockslide in the Himalayan region,” Shah said. “The incident is a serious indication that the risks we face in the Himalayan region are increasing.”
The prime minister said Nepal must tell the international community more forcefully that climate change is driving the disasters and risks it faces.
“Climate change is a global problem,” Shah said. “Mitigating and managing its impacts is a shared responsibility of the international community.”

His remarks come amid a massive search-and-rescue operation in the aftermath of the disaster, with scientists and climate experts on both sides of the Nepal-China border still working to determine the disaster’s trigger and whether such events could become more frequent.

According to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, the flood’s death toll rose to 1,204 as of Wednesday evening, while 4,216 remained out of contact. Around 1.6 million people in Rasuwa and Nuwakot were directly affected by the disaster.
The floods completely swept away 41 concrete bridges and damaged four others. In Nuwakot alone, 1,267 houses were completely damaged and another 1,253 partially damaged.

But beyond the immediate devastation, the disaster has raised a larger question about the increasing instability of the Himalayan cryosphere and the possibility of similar events occurring more frequently as temperatures rise.
According to the National Climate Centre (NCC) of China, glacier-related disasters could indeed become more frequent as global warming weakens glacier stability on the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau.
Gao Rong, deputy director of the Centre, said at a press conference on Wednesday that global warming was accelerating the melting of mountain glaciers worldwide.

“Mountain glaciers in China are concentrated mainly on the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau and surrounding areas. Against a backdrop of a warmer and wetter climate, glaciers across the region are generally undergoing accelerated melting,” Gao said.

He added that the internal structural stability of glaciers on the plateau is expected to decline further. “Glacier-related disasters could become more frequent and trigger cascading effects that amplify the scale of destruction and expand their impact,” he warned.
The warning comes as the global scientific community is increasingly linking the rise in extreme weather events to a warming planet.

The United Nations Environment Program said on Wednesday that global temperatures are set to cross the 1.5°C threshold, likely within the next few years, pushing climate risks and impacts to increasingly dangerous levels.

Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal has also blamed climate change for the increasing risks faced by Nepal and said the international community must recognize its responsibility towards countries such as Nepal that contribute little to global emissions but face disproportionate consequences.
The government has already approached the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage for immediate support and compensation for the devastation caused by the August 26 floods.

Manjit Dhakal, an adviser to the Least Developed Countries Group in UN climate negotiations, said the Loss and Damage Fund was established precisely to respond to catastrophic events affecting vulnerable countries.

“As someone involved in the Transitional Committee that helped establish the Fund, I clearly remember our discussions about making it more responsive to the realities and urgency of loss and damage,” Dhakal said.

“The FRLD now has an opportunity to demonstrate what it was created to deliver: timely, accessible and grant-based support when vulnerable countries face catastrophic loss and damage. We sincerely hope no country has to face such a tragedy. But today, Nepal needs solidarity translated into action,” he added. /dl

articles.title: India rejects Hague ruling on Indus waters: What’s next?
articles.summary: The Indus Waters Treaty is facing a fresh dispute after India rejected a Hague-based Court of Arbitration ruling that the 1960 agreement remains in force. Pakistan has welcomed the decision and said…

blocks.text: The Indus Waters Treaty is facing a fresh dispute after India rejected a Hague-based Court of Arbitration ruling that the 1960 agreement remains in force.
Pakistan has welcomed the decision and said India remains bound by the treaty.
India’s Ministry of External Affairs described the tribunal as a “so-called Court of Arbitration” that was “illegally constituted.”

It said the body had been established by the World Bank in breach of the treaty and that India “categorically rejects its so-called award, just as it has firmly rejected all prior pronouncements by this illegally constituted body.”
“The Court of Arbitration has no jurisdiction whatsoever to pronounce on India’s sovereign decisions,” the ministry said.
What to know about the treaty
The Indus Waters Treaty, brokered by the World Bank, governs the use of water from six rivers flowing through India and Pakistan.

The agreement largely gives India rights over three eastern rivers while Pakistan has rights over the western Indus, Jhelum and Chenab. India is allowed to use the western rivers for specified purposes including certain hydroelectric projects.
The treaty had endured wars and prolonged periods of intense hostility between the two nuclear-armed neighbors.

But India placed the treaty in abeyance in April 2025 as part of a package of diplomatic and economic measures announced after a deadly attack in India-administered Kashmir killed 26 people, mostly tourists.
New Delhi accused Islamabad of backing the attack. Pakistan has denied the charges.
High stakes for Pakistan
Millions of people in Pakistan depend on the Indus, Jhelum and Chenab rivers for drinking water, farming and daily life.
The rivers are particularly important to Punjab and Sindh provinces, whose agriculture is central to the country’s food supply and rural economy.
After India’s move to suspend the treaty, Pakistan approached the court in The Hague over the status of the accord.
Pakistani officials have repeatedly warned that any attempt to deny the country its share of the waters of rivers flowing across the border would be treated as an act of war.
Ajay Bisaria, a former Indian high commissioner to Pakistan, said India had challenged the treaty on both political and legal grounds.
“Politically, abeyance hands India a new point of leverage, one more lever to press Pakistan into changing its behavior on cross-border terrorism,” Bisaria told DW.
He also pointed to India’s earlier requests to renegotiate the treaty, citing climate change, new dam-building technology and the deterioration of relations between the two countries.
India chose to put the treaty in abeyance rather than formally abrogate it. Bisaria said the ruling in The Hague would not change that course.
“The tribunal will not alter this trajectory,” he said. “India’s course on the Indus Waters Treaty is set. The treaty will not be revived in its present form.”
Legal battle over water
Pakistan has taken the opposite view.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said the ruling “decisively rejects” India’s attempt to place the treaty in abeyance and reaffirmed that it remains “fully in force and binding on both parties.”
“The Award vindicates Pakistan’s consistent position that a binding international treaty cannot be unilaterally suspended or set aside,” Dar said in a post on X.

Pakistan welcomes the unanimous Award of the Court of Arbitration today, which decisively rejects India’s unlawful attempt to place the Indus Waters Treaty “in abeyance” and reaffirms that the Treaty remains fully in force and binding on both parties. The Award vindicates… — Ishaq Dar (@MIshaqDar50) August 31, 2026
He added that India must comply with its obligations under the treaty and with binding decisions arising from its dispute settlement mechanisms.
Ayesha Siddiqa, a Pakistani political scientist and defense analyst, said the ruling may be difficult to implement if India refuses to accept it.
“The arbitration court’s ruling may not be implementable because the court doesn’t have the force to do so,” Siddiqa told DW.
But she said the decision gave Pakistan an advantage as a lower riparian state.
“It does give Pakistan a moral edge,” said Siddiqa, a senior fellow in the Department of War Studies at King’s College London.
She also questioned what India’s rejection of the ruling could mean for its international position, particularly given that India has accepted international legal decisions in other disputes.
“This is not just an issue of pure military power but an international standing where India will not be able to justify its position to the world any longer,” she said.
Shanthie Mariet D’Souza, a South Asia analyst and founder of the Mantraya think tank, said the ruling did not materially change India’s position.
“The Permanent Court of Arbitration is an administrative body, not a conventional sovereign court with enforcement capabilities,” D’Souza told DW.

“In this particular case, India chose not to participate in the proceedings. This allows it not to recognize the tribunal’s rulings. Therefore, it has no enforceable constraint on India and nothing changes materially for New Delhi,” she said.
A dispute over the rules
India and Pakistan have disagreed for years over the interpretation of the treaty, particularly over Indian hydropower projects on rivers allocated primarily to Pakistan.

Uttam Kumar Sinha, a senior fellow at the Manohar Parrikar Institute for Defence Studies in New Delhi and author of “Trial by Water,” said India is now no longer merely contesting the interpretation of the treaty, but rather “contesting the authority of the treaty’s dispute-settlement mechanism itself.”
New Delhi maintains that the tribunal was improperly constituted and that its decisions have no legal effect on India.
Sinha described the emerging contest as “lawfare,” with Pakistan likely to use the ruling in international forums and frame the dispute around treaty obligations and international law.
The limits of India’s leverage
The practical implications will also depend on what India does with its infrastructure on the western rivers.
D’Souza said the treaty’s abeyance gave India more political and psychological leverage than an immediate ability to alter the flow of the rivers.

“To effectively stop or significantly alter the flows of the Indus, Jhelum and Chenab rivers, substantial infrastructure like dams, canals and large storage systems would be required, and such structures do not currently exist,” said D’Souza.
“Furthermore, geographical and technical constraints limit India’s capacity to block these rivers.”
Sinha echoed this view.
“India cannot simply ‘turn off’ the western rivers,” he said.

Large storage and diversion projects would take years or decades, require substantial investment and involve difficult construction in the mountainous Himalayan region, as well as environmental and domestic approvals.
“There is a significant gap between India’s potential strategic freedom on the western rivers and its actual physical capacity to change water flows,” Sinha said. /dl

articles.title: Zubiri:’Tired’ remark due to ‘present condition,’ will work 24/7 if needed
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Senate majority leader Juan Miguel “Migz” Zubiri on Thursday cleared the air on his statement expressing exhaustion for working 12 hours a day. His remark came amid the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Senate majority leader Juan Miguel “Migz” Zubiri on Thursday cleared the air on his statement expressing exhaustion for working 12 hours a day.
His remark came amid the coinciding schedules of the second regular session, the budget hearings and the impeachment trial in the Senate.

When the impeachment court was discussing its potential schedule for the trial of Vice President Sara Duterte in consideration of the chamber’s urgent legislative work, Zubiri had said he was “very tired,” having to go to the Senate from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. almost daily.
His pronouncement was met with scrutiny from netizens who pointed out that his exhaustion does not compare to lower to middle-class earners who work the same hours for less income.
Some said that it is part of a lawmaker’s job to work long hours when necessary.
“It doesn’t matter if I’m tired. We will do our job as senators and impeachment court judges. If we have to work 24/7, we will do it 24/7,” Zubiri said in a media briefing.
The senator also explained that he was being “honest” about his condition at that time.
“I just mentioned my present condition at that time, because it was very difficult to juggle the three very important activities of the Senate,” he explained.
“It was the first time that there was an impeachment, a budget and a legislative session,” he said.
In a social media statement, Zubiri further explained that his message was primarily on the schedule of all their present duties.
“This was my only point yesterday: Time must be maximized for the impeachment trial, regular session and budget season because these are important,” he said.
“The goal: To finish these three properly, on time, and still be sane,” he added. /apl

articles.title: Unicef: 1 in 5 youths targeted by online sexual abuse
articles.summary: The internet is not a safe place for unsupervised children and young people — by now, that’s common knowledge. Social media platforms are adept at tweaking their algorithms to ensure users of…

blocks.text: The internet is not a safe place for unsupervised children and young people — by now, that’s common knowledge.

Social media platforms are adept at tweaking their algorithms to ensure users of any age remain on their sites. To do that, they often disseminate content that can be dangerous and upsetting for young people.

Studies regularly find a connection between what’s known as doomscrolling and a higher risk of psychological problems in the young, including suicidal thoughts. And some of the latest trends in video creation on platforms like TikTok directly endanger the safety of users.
In the United States, Meta, which owns both Instagram and Facebook, recently opted to settle a case against it out of court. A number of US states had claimed that the two platforms harmed children.

Meta agreed to pay up to $17.1 billion (€14.7 billion) to the states involved and to limit teenagers’ access to its platforms to just two hours a day. During the night, access will be completely blocked.

A new survey by UNICEF, the UN agency for children, puts the spotlight on another danger that young people constantly face in the digital world: sexual assault, a threat experienced by one in five people between the ages of 12 and 17 over the past year.
What are the key findings?
The UNICEF report, which DW saw in advance of publication, explains how such attacks often happen.
“It often begins without warning,” the authors of the study wrote. “Conversation becomes coercion, and coercion becomes entrapment.”

The survey found that more than 15 million children had been exposed to unwanted sexual content. An estimated 9 million were pressured into sexual conversations or asked to share sexual images, while some 4 million had sexual images shared without their consent. The report’s authors, however, warn that the true scale is likely far higher.

“The report reveals a painful reality,” said UNICEF Executive Director Catherine Russell. “These experiences cause profound emotional and mental distress. Many children suffer in silence, unsure where to turn for help.”

Often, the perpetrator of the assault puts pressure on a victim. The victims then feel ashamed and this makes it difficult to tell anybody about what has happened. Of those surveyed, 41% had never told anybody about their assault. Others said they had first confided in friends, siblings or their mothers. Fewer than 1% were reported to authorities.

blocks.caption: UNICEF: 1 in 5 youths targeted by online sexual abuse

blocks.text: The stereotype many have of a complete stranger harassing young people online actually only applies in 16% of cases. Most perpetrators — 57% — are already known to their victims. They may be friends, family members or even romantic partners.

In addition, 27% of respondents were not able to identify the people behind the profiles. When perpetrators are known, they include adults but also minors. In many cases, attacks take place in real life as well as online.

The major social media platforms are also the main gateways for this kind of behavior. The UNICEF report says 60% of assaults come primarily from Facebook, WhatsApp and Instagram (all of which are owned by Meta), followed by Snapchat, TikTok and YouTube. And 14% of respondents cited online gaming platforms as the location of an assault — gaming platforms usually have direct messaging channels.
How was the data collected?

The report polled around 21,000 young people in 21 countries, aged between 12 and 17, who regularly use the internet. Data from 12 countries — Ethiopia, Indonesia, Cambodia, Kenya, Malaysia, Mozambique, Namibia, the Philippines, Tanzania, Thailand, Uganda and Vietnam — had already been collected in 2020 and 2021 and analyzed in an earlier report.

For this new report, additional data was collected in Armenia, Brazil, Colombia, the Dominican Republic, Mexico, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Pakistan and Serbia. The surveys were also supplemented by longer interviews with 100 young people who had experienced abuse.

blocks.caption: Children and young people also come into contact with inappropriate content in the form of fakes created by generative AI, such as these images generated by Grok of the platform XImage: Leon Neal/Getty Images

blocks.text: Europe, US surveys find similar results
Researchers familiar with this issue would not be surprised by the scale of the problem.
The 2020 EU Kids Online Survey, based on a poll conducted in 19 European countries, indicated that 22% of all participants had received sexually explicit messages online.

In a Spanish study conducted in seven secondary schools in 2021 and 2022, 21% of female respondents said they were sexually harassed online “occasionally,” while 5% said this happened “frequently.” For male respondents in the Spanish study, the percentages were a few points lower.

A similar survey conducted by the Pew Research Center in 2022 found that 17% of 13- to 17-year-olds in the US said they had been sent explicit images without their consent. The survey did not differentiate between sexually explicit content and other material that showed things like violence.

blocks.caption: UNICEF: 1 in 5 youths targeted by online sexual abuse

blocks.text: The UNICEF report calls on governments, tech companies and other stakeholders to better protect children and young people in the digital world.
Among the requests:

items: Design more secure digital platforms, with stronger protection for the privacy of minors.
Strengthen national regulations and criminal law, and close loopholes.
Establish trustworthy reporting and support systems for young people.

blocks.text: Coming just after Meta’s out-of-court settlement in the US, the new UNICEF report will likely add fuel to the fire for those seeking to ban social media for young people, an ongoing debate in many countries.

In December 2025, Australia became the first country in the world to introduce an age limit for social media in order to protect minors. There, anyone under 16 is prohibited from having an account on platforms like YouTube, X, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat, a rule the platforms themselves are required to monitor.

A similar age limit will come into effect in the UK in 2027, while France is the first EU country to have passed a law adopting an age limit — 15 years old — for social media users. However, it has since been blocked by France’s top court, the Constitutional Council, which ruled it might infringe on freedom of expression and privacy.
In June, a German commission proposed a tiered model. This would come with age limits, requirements for proof of age and strict rules requiring the cooperation of social media platforms. /dl

articles.title: LOOK: Marcos inspects renovated PICC ahead of Asean Summit
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. on Thursday conducted a walkthrough of the Philippine International Convention Center (PICC) in Pasay City to personally assess the venue’s…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. on Thursday conducted a walkthrough of the Philippine International Convention Center (PICC) in Pasay City to personally assess the venue’s readiness and preparations for the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) Summit and Related Summits in November.
The regional bloc’s gathering is scheduled to from November 10 to 12, with some related events set through November 15.

blocks.caption: (Photo courtesy of the Presidential Communications Office)

blocks.text: Designed by Filipino National Artist for Architecture Leandro V. Locsin, the PICC is Asia’s first international convention center.
It underwent a six-month renovation in 2025 and reopened in September last year.
Among its notable new works are the repair of marble tiles in the lobby, repainting of the ceiling, laser cleaning of concrete walls, and restoration of pieces of furniture that date back to 1976.

blocks.caption: (Photo courtesy of the Presidential Communications Office)

blocks.text: The damaged tiles were also replaced, and all the new marble slabs were restored.
The lawn was also revived to its original 1976 design, with 3,068 restored shining droplights that will welcome visitors in the lobby.
Moreover, new infinity waterfalls, modern lighting, and a 30-speaker audio system were also installed.
Aside from the PICC, the historic Coconut Palace has also been revitalized ahead of the Asean Summit and is set to reopen to the public in 2027. /gsg

articles.title: PNP: MILF convoy only coordinated movement in Lanao del Sur
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The reason why the convoy of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) was stopped at a checkpoint in Kolambugan, Lanao del Norte was because only their movement within Lanao del…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The reason why the convoy of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) was stopped at a checkpoint in Kolambugan, Lanao del Norte was because only their movement within Lanao del Sur was coordinated, the Philippine National Police (PNP) said on Thursday.

“Ngayon ay mayroon naman silang prior coordination, but ang prior coordination po nila was made only for movement inside Lanao del Sur. So nung lalabas po sila at pupunta sila sa Lanao del Norte, ‘yun po ay chineck po sila ng Philippine National Police kasama po ang ng Philippine Army dahil po sa para po sa kaligtasan na rin ng ng publiko at ng lahat po ng involved,” PNP public information chief Col. Allen Rae Co told reporters at Camp Crame.

(“They did have prior coordination, but that coordination was only for movement within Lanao del Sur. So, when they were about to leave and head to Lanao del Norte, they were checked by the Philippine National Police and the Philippine Army for the safety of the public and everyone involved,”)

This came after at least 23 four-wheel vehicles and five motorcycles of the MILF were flagged during checkpoint operations in the area. Police authorities of the Lanao del Norte said some of the 200 members were armed.
“Ngayon lamang ay hindi nga po sila nakapag-coordinate properly at syempre, it’s alarming yung ganong karaming tao na mga armado na magta-travel po,” Co expressed.
(“It is just that, in this instance, they failed to coordinate properly, and naturally, it is alarming to have such a large number of armed individuals traveling,”)
The group was said to attend an event of MILF leader Abdullah Macapaar, or better known as Commander Bravo, in Lanao del Norte. Co said they also have no prior coordination regarding their visit.

“And wala rin daw silang prior na coordination sa kanila na pupunta at hindi pa ano kung kung may imbitasyon ba talaga para sa mag-attend po. Ang sabi naman po ng grupo nga na pupunta sana doon ay since it’s a meeting ng MILF ay lahat ng commanders naman ay kumbaga ay parang given na na invited sila doon,” Co explained.

(“They reportedly had no prior coordination regarding the visit, and it remains unclear if there was an actual invitation for them to attend. However, the group intending to go maintained that since it was an MILF meeting, it was essentially a given that all commanders were invited,”)
Meanwhile, Co said five unarmed civilian vehicles were allowed to pass through.
The remaining vehicles were escorted back to Picong, Lanao del Sur after they failed to present the necessary travel documents.

“Usually, because when there is a move with no prior coordination and no clear purpose mentioned to our authorities, it will cause an alarm. That is why our troops checked and put a checkpoint,” Co said.

In less than two weeks, the historic Bangsomoro Parliamentary elections in Sept. 14 will commence, wherein 2.3 million voters are expected to vote 80 members of the Bangsomoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) parliament.
The Philippine Army said it heightened security across BARMM, particularly in 29 areas under red category, or those with serious threats and history of election-related violence. /mr

articles.title: Human fat, blood dumped into sinks, toilets at Seoul clinics
articles.summary: Twenty-five plastic surgery and dermatology clinics in Seoul violated medical-waste rules, including two cases in which human fat and blood from cosmetic procedures were dumped into sinks and…

blocks.text: Twenty-five plastic surgery and dermatology clinics in Seoul violated medical-waste rules, including two cases in which human fat and blood from cosmetic procedures were dumped into sinks and toilets, the Seoul Metropolitan Government said Thursday.

The city’s special judicial police investigated 120 sites — 112 medical clinics and eight waste collection and transport companies — from January 2025 through July this year. Investigators uncovered 36 violations at 25 clinics.

In the two cases of illegal disposal, human fat and blood from liposuction and other cosmetic procedures were poured into sinks or toilets. Medical waste was also discarded in ordinary trash bins alongside household waste.

Other violations involved improper storage. Some clinics mixed human tissue waste with general medical waste and kept it at room temperature before handing it over for disposal. Others stored medical waste for three to six months beyond the permitted period.

Blood, bodily fluids, used needles and other medical waste must be handled separately because of the risk of infection. Human tissue waste, including fat, must be kept in designated containers at 4 degrees Celsius or below.

“Human tissue waste can rapidly decompose at room temperature, increasing odors and the risk of infection,” said an official from the city’s special judicial police bureau. “Medical institutions must strictly comply with storage and disposal standards from the moment the waste is generated.”

Investigators booked 25 people in connection with the violations and referred them to prosecutors in August with recommendations for indictment. Violating medical waste disposal standards is punishable by up to two years in prison or a fine of up to 20 million won ($14,700), according to the city.
The investigation also found that some doctors, nurses and waste-handling workers lacked sufficient knowledge of disposal requirements.

The city plans to improve training and inspection procedures and revise penalties to reflect the seriousness of each violation. It will share the cases with district offices and continue investigating related waste collection and transport companies.

The findings come amid a surge in medical tourism to Seoul, driven largely by demand for dermatological and cosmetic procedures. A record 1.76 million foreign patients received treatment in the city in 2025, up 75.6 percent from a year earlier. /dl

articles.title: Cracked in under 24 hours: 1 dead, 1 nabbed in Ozamiz heist
articles.summary: CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY — In less than 24 hours, police cracked a nighttime heist at a commercial establishment in Ozamiz City, Misamis Occidental, arresting one suspect and killing another in a gunfight…

blocks.text: CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY — In less than 24 hours, police cracked a nighttime heist at a commercial establishment in Ozamiz City, Misamis Occidental, arresting one suspect and killing another in a gunfight on Wednesday.

The Police Regional Office 10 (PRO-10) reported that the robbery occurred at around 11:15 p.m. on September 1. The suspects breached the building by smashing a hole through the rear concrete wall, forcibly opened the vault, and fled with an estimated P60,000 in cash.

Investigators from the Ozamiz City Police Station quickly analyzed the crime scene and the CCTV footage, identifying the perpetrators as alias “Joe” and alias “Boy,” both residents of Ramon Magsaysay, Zamboanga del Sur.
Records revealed that “Joe” has an existing arrest warrant for robbery under Criminal Case No. 2022-10-4516 in Zamboanga del Sur.
According to initial police findings, the duo are alleged members of the Pondoyo Robbery Group operating across Zamboanga del Sur and neighboring provinces.
Authorities also tied them to two earlier heists: one in Gingoog City, Misamis Oriental, in February 2026, and in Tudela, Misamis Occidental, on April 24, 2026.
Tracking the leads, operatives launched a hot pursuit operation and captured “Joe” at his residence.

When police moved in on “Boy’s” nearby home, the suspect allegedly opened fire with a .45 caliber pistol. Officers returned fire in self-defense, inflicting fatal gunshot wounds on “Boy,” who was declared dead at the scene.
Brig. Gen. Nestor Babagay Jr., PRO-10 regional director, lauded the Ozamiz police force for swiftly resolving the case.
“This accomplishment demonstrates the value of focused and intelligence-driven policing,” Babagay said.

“In less than 24 hours, our personnel developed vital leads, identified the suspects, and acted swiftly to place one of them under arrest. We will continue to pursue individuals and groups involved in robbery and other criminal activities through lawful and properly coordinated police operations,” he added.

PRO-10 pointed out that the swift operation aligns with the agenda of the Philippine National Police leadership and directives from the Department of the Interior and Local Government to ramp up responsive anti-criminality campaigns./coa

articles.title: Nepal flood survivors lack space even to mourn their dead
articles.summary: KATHMANDU — Families of people who went missing in the Bhotekoshi floods have begun performing the funeral rites of their loved ones using effigies made of kusha grass, as they did not receive…

blocks.text: KATHMANDU — Families of people who went missing in the Bhotekoshi floods have begun performing the funeral rites of their loved ones using effigies made of kusha grass, as they did not receive any clues of their whereabouts even after eight days of the disaster.
Most flood victims have been left without a place to observe the mourning rituals, as the floodwaters not only swept away family members but also their houses.
Those who lost everything in the floods and came to the capital city seeking shelter have also been unable to find space at public facilities for the rituals.

Nirajan Poudel of Nuwakot reached the Kiriyaputri Bhawan at Rudramati Mahadev Temple in Tarakeshwar-5 after losing family members in the devastating floods. “After we could not find any space to stay during the mourning period, we came here,” he said. “We managed to get a room here.”

Poudel, a resident of Bidur Municipality-7, lost his father, mother, uncle, aunt and sister (his uncle’s daughter) in the devastating August 26 disaster. On Wednesday, he and his cousin performed the funeral rites of all five using effigies made of kusha, the grass holy for Hindus with the scientific name Desmostachya bipinnata, and began the mourning rituals.

The Rudramati Mahadev Temple and Kiriyaputri Bhawan are still under construction. However, after flood victims requested a place to observe mourning rituals for relatives lost in the Bhotekoshi floods, the temple management committee decided to open the facility in whatever condition it was, said Raj Kumar Phuyal, treasurer of the temple management committee.

“The entire country is currently in mourning. To help the relatives of the victims, we opened this Kiriyaputri Bhawan after the floods,” he said. “As construction isn’t over yet, mourners may face some difficulties.”
There are currently eight groups staying at the Kiriyaputri Bhawan, and each group has lost three to five members of the family in the Rasuwa flood.

“There is no space to accommodate even one more mourner family,” said Sudarshan Chapagain, a social activist. “So many people have come asking for a place to observe the mourning ritual but we have not been able to accommodate them all.”

He said construction of the Kiriyaputri Bhawan was still underway and that a lack of funds had delayed its completion for years. The Tarakeshwar Municipality had provided only Rs1 million for its construction while local residents also collected donations to build the three-storey building.

Like in Rudramati Mahadev Temple and Kiriyaputri Bhawan, all eight rooms at the nearby Gupteshwar Mahadev Temple’s Kiriyaputri Bhawan are occupied by families who lost relatives in the Bhotekoshi floods. After more and more people began coming to request a place to observe the rituals, the building management committee put up tents and created six additional rooms.

“Now we do not have any room available until the current groups complete their mourning,” said Rishi Prasad Nepal, a member of the Gupteshwar Temple Kiriyaputri Bhawan management committee. “We keep receiving phone calls from flood victims for a place to mourn but we simply do not have one to offer.”
The committee has decided to charge only Rs1,000 for each family for using its room to mourn and complete rituals.
“Mourners’ families themselves have to bring gas, as we are unable to manage gas for them,” said Nepal. “LP gas is no longer available for purchase.”

Rajan Raila of Bidur Municipality-7, who lost his mother, younger brother and sister-in-law in the floods, performed the funeral rites of the deceased using kusha effigies at Pashupati Aryaghat on Wednesday and then came to Gupteshwar Temple to observe the mourning rituals. He said he and his brothers, who are observing the rituals together, were given only one room.

“We got only one room for the mourning rituals of three deceased family members,” he said. “Even that room has not yet become available. We will get it only after those whose 13th-day ritual is completed today leave. Until then, we have to wait outside.”

Relatives of victims said they had begun performing the rituals using kusha effigies because there was little possibility of finding their missing family members, and even if bodies were recovered, identifying them had become difficult. They also complain that bodies were being buried rapidly in mass graves, leaving families with no option but to perform symbolic funerals.
Victims said around 100 people were missing in Sole of Bidur Municipality-7 alone in the floods.

“There could be many more, as we do not know how many people who were staying indoors, walking along the roads or working at construction sites were swept away,” said Ram Chandra Dhakal, a flood victim displaced from Bidur-7, Sole.

Dhakal and his brother Uttam are also observing the mourning ritual for their mother at the Kiriyaputri Bhawan in Gupteshwar. She was found dead after being caught in the flood. Although the body was cremated in their village, they had to come to Kathmandu, as there was no house in the village where they could observe the mourning rituals, he said.

Victims said all the rooms at the Kiriyaputri Bhawan at a place known as Gumba in Balaju-16 have also been occupied by people who lost relatives in the floods. Even those displaced by the floods who came to Kathmandu to stay with relatives or in rented rooms have struggled to observe mourning rituals, as it is not possible to conduct such rituals in their relatives’ homes or their own rented rooms.
The lack of space at public kiriyaputri buildings has compounded their difficulties in observing the mourning rituals.

More than 1,200 bodies of people who died in the August 26 floods have been recovered while thousands are still missing. Pilgrims, tourists, engineers and others are among those who disappeared in the floods.

The floods swept away more than 7,000 houses, while many of the houses that are still standing have become uninhabitable. Dozens of concrete and suspension bridges and roads have been washed away. Dozens of settlements along the Trishuli riverbanks have been completely destroyed in the floods. /dl

articles.title: Guitar used by George Michael in Faith video goes up for auction
articles.summary:
Gretsch Synchromatic 160 acoustic guitar expected to sell for as much as £120,000, as star lot in auction of items owned by late personal assistant Siobhan Bailey

One of the most iconic…

blocks.text: One of the most iconic items in George Michael’s career, the acoustic guitar he energetically strummed in the video for 1987’s Faith, is going up for auction.

The guitar, a Gretsch Synchromatic 160 with a sunburst finish to the body, has an estimated sale price of £60,000-£120,000. It comes with a case featuring the words Rockabilly Rebel pasted on it – a reference to the twangy, 1950s-referencing sound of Faith, which topped the US charts for four weeks and became a foundation stone of Michael’s post-Wham! solo career.
The guitar is part of a broader auction from the archive of Michael’s former personal assistant, Siobhan Bailey, who died in 2014 aged 56. It is being arranged via her widower.

Bailey worked for Michael for more than 20 years, and amassed a sizeable trove of memorabilia. The star lot is the Gretsch guitar, but there are 31 others spanning everything from gold and platinum discs to tour programmes – and a metal lighthouse statue presented to Michael by Malaga city council in 1989 (estimated price £200-£400).

There are glimpses into the machinations for George Michael and Wham! tours via private itinerary documents, including one of Bailey’s handwritten notebooks, and a running order document for 1985’s Live Aid. Another itinerary details Wham!’s 1985 tour of China, when they became the first western act to tour the country. The trip was documented – in fractious circumstances – by director Lindsay Anderson in the film Wham! in China: Foreign Skies, recently reissued in an altered form as Wham! 10 Days in China.

The auction also features the ultimate version of Michael’s album Older – a promotional box set not made available to the public, expected to sell for £300-600 – and invitations that Michael received to various events including a reception by TV soap EastEnders, and a lunch with David and Victoria Beckham in 2002 (“rickshaws at nightfall, dress: white tie and diamonds”). Another lot features 49 photos, some of them taken by Bailey and previously unseen.

Coincidentally, another Faith-era item is going up for sale at a separate auction announced this week: Ray-Ban sunglasses worn by Michael on the Faith tour are expected to sell for £15,000 to £30,000 at the upcoming Music Memorabilia Live auction held in London on 1 and 2 October.
The auctions arrive as the 10th anniversary of Michael’s death approaches in December, along with a broader re-appreciation of the Faith era.

A new film, George Michael: The Faith Tour, will be released on 6 November, drawn from rediscovered footage of a 1988 concert in Paris. The film is co-directed by Andy Morahan, who directed the Faith music video, and is assembled from footage generated by 14 35mm cameras which captured Michael’s performance. It will be preceded by a short film by Mary McCartney, pairing unseen images of Michael by acclaimed photographer Herb Ritts with an unheard interview with Michael. An 18-track live album, also titled George Michael: The Faith Tour, is being released alongside it.
The Siobhan Bailey auction takes place 29 October, both online and in person at Sworders in Stansted Mountfitchet, Essex. The items go on display at Sworders’ London branch from 20-27 October.

articles.title: Is Quebec actually the most taxed jurisdiction in North America?
articles.summary: With the rising cost of living front and centre in the Quebec election campaign, a familiar refrain has emerged: Quebec is the most taxed jurisdiction in North America. But is the claim actually…

image.caption: Quebec Conservative Leader Éric Duhaime has made cutting back on taxes a key part of his campaign. (Jacques Boissinot/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Montreal·Analysis

With the rising cost of living front and centre in the Quebec election campaign, a familiar refrain has emerged: Quebec is the most taxed jurisdiction in North America. But is the claim actually true? We took a closer look.
Tax burden in the province is Canada's highest — until you factor in the returns
With the rising cost of living front and centre in the Quebec election campaign, a familiar refrain has emerged: Quebec is the most taxed jurisdiction in North America.
Conservative Party of Quebec Leader Éric Duhaime is leaning on that claim to justify his promise of deep income and corporate tax cuts to help address the cost of living.
"Quebecers face the highest tax burden in North America. It is now the government's turn to tighten its belt,” Duhaime said in a news release last Friday.
He repeated that point during a news conference the same day, saying Quebec is "the worst one" among 60 states and provinces across Canada and the U.S.
But is the claim actually true? We took a closer look.
An overall heavy burden

The short answer is yes — with an asterisk. It depends on what exactly is being measured, according to Luc Godbout, a professor and the research chair in taxation and public finance at the Université de Sherbrooke.

One way to answer this question is through what economists call the "overall tax burden." This involves adding up all taxes paid to federal, provincial and local authorities by individuals and businesses, and then expressing that as a percentage of the gross domestic product (GDP).

By that measure, Quebec does indeed have the highest taxes among all 10 Canadian provinces, sitting at 38.6 per cent of its GDP for 2024, according to an annual study prepared by Godbout and other researchers at the university.
Quebec also has a higher overall tax burden than the United States and Mexico.
As this chart shows, the province's tax burden sits closer to the average of advanced countries in the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD).
Another way to measure the tax burden is by analyzing it at the individual level and looking at personal income taxes, social contributions and consumption taxes, Godbout explained to CBC News.
On that front, Quebec’s gross individual tax burden is heavier than all other provinces except one: Nova Scotia, Godbout pointed out.
On the whole, if Nova Scotia's tax system were applied to Quebecers, they would actually pay more.
Taxes shrink wealth gap
The picture becomes more nuanced when evaluating what's called the "net tax burden."
This measure takes into account not only what individuals pay in taxes, but also what they get back through refundable tax credits and family allowances paid directly to households.

By this metric, the tax system in Quebec actually results in a lighter burden for individuals than in four of the nine other provinces. Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, Newfoundland and Labrador, and New Brunswick all have a higher net tax burden, Godbout pointed out.

For example, a single-parent family earning $56,714 (which is two-thirds of the average wage) in Quebec gets back 12 per cent more in government transfers than they pay in total taxes — the lowest net burden in Canada, according to the annual study.
On the flip side, high-income earners with no children are heavily taxed in the province.
A single person earning $141,362 (which is two-thirds more than the average wage) faces a net tax burden of nearly 35 per cent, the highest in the country.
As the chart below illustrates, Quebec's tax system significantly shrinks the wealth gap.
Before taxes, Quebec's Gini coefficient, which measures inequality, is 0.43, but government transfers drop it to 0.27, leaving the province with some of the lowest income inequality in the country.
Colin Pratte, a researcher at the Institut de recherche et d’informations socioéconomiques (IRIS), argues higher tax collection in Quebec serves as an effective mechanism for wealth redistribution.
He points to the latest numbers from Statistics Canada, that show Ontario’s poverty rate is 50 per cent higher than in Quebec.
“It is actually the main tool for a given government, a given society, to make sure that wealth is well distributed among people of that society,” he said.

So, while Duhaime’s campaign rhetoric rings true for corporations, high-income earners, and childless individuals, Quebec's system of government transfers means lower-income families actually face some of the lightest net tax burdens on the continent.
