articles.title: Giorgia Meloni is Italy's longest-serving postwar leader. Will that stability last?
articles.summary: On Friday, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's administration will celebrate 1,413 consecutive days in office, overtaking a record set by Silvio Berlusconi's second administration to become the…

image.caption: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's administration on Friday will celebrate 1,413 consecutive days in office, becoming the longest-lasting government in Italy's postwar history. (Manon Cruz/AFP via Getty Images)

blocks.text: World·Analysis

On Friday, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's administration will celebrate 1,413 consecutive days in office, overtaking a record set by Silvio Berlusconi's second administration to become the longest-lasting government in the country's postwar history.
Marking 1,413 days in office, caution — not confrontation — has defined far-right leader's governing style

On Friday, on a quay in the southern Italy port city of Bari, more than 10,000 supporters will have room to celebrate a number that once seemed about as likely as an Italian putting ketchup on spaghetti: 1,413.

That is how many consecutive days Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government will have survived on Sept. 4, overtaking the record set by Silvio Berlusconi's second administration to become the longest-lasting government in the postwar history of the Italian Republic.

The milestone is being marked with a rally organized by Meloni's Brothers of Italy party at Bari's port, where the prime minister will be joined by ministers, lawmakers and other supporters for what's being billed as a celebration of the government’s record longevity.
For a country that has cycled through 68 governments in the 80 years since the end of the Second World War, the record may say more about Meloni than Italy.
Italy's first female leader rose to power with a public persona constructed around combat and defiance.

Raised largely by her mother in Rome's working-class Garbatella neighbourhood after her father left, Meloni, 49, entered politics in the 1990s through the youth movement of the post-fascist Italian Social Movement.
A self-described "underdog," she describes resistance as a main source of her motivation, recently telling the New York Times, "a 'No' is one of the things that most mobilizes me."

Her political communication is similarly personal. The rally cry that helped make her famous — "I am Giorgia, I am a woman, I am a mother, I am Italian, I am Christian" — was catchy enough to be turned into a dance remix.
Governing by coalition
But for someone who built her image on fighting, it is caution, not confrontation, that has most marked her governing style.
While Italian politics is littered with the wreckage of male leaders undone by overreach, Meloni has built her staying power on knowing when not to push her luck.

It's patience she displayed even before reaching office. When almost every major party entered Mario Draghi's broad coalition government in 2021, Meloni kept her small, outlier Brothers of Italy party alone in opposition.

After the 2022 collapse of Draghi's government, Meloni claimed power, heading a three-party, right-wing coalition that gave her a clear parliamentary majority. The politician who had railed against Brussels now largely toed the European Union's fiscal rules, remained steadfastly pro-Ukraine and fell silent on earlier talk of challenging the euro.
She's also managed to keep together that sometimes-fractious alliance with Matteo Salvini's anti-immigration, pro-Russia League and Antonio Tajani's centre-right Forza Italia.
That combination — fiery political identity, pragmatic governing — has helped her beat the odds.

Lorenzo Pregliasco, a head pollster with YouTrend, calls Meloni's durability "highly unusual." Brothers of Italy is polling slightly above its 2022 election result right now, in a country where governing parties typically start losing support within months.
But Pregliasco said that shouldn't be mistaken for an overwhelming love of the party's leader.
"Meloni's strength in the polls doesn't reflect a genuine, overwhelming support for a government," he said. "The key issue here is how much Meloni is seen as credible, as opposed to the alternative."

items: Just call her Giorgia: Italian PM Meloni's transformation from the margins to power broker
Italy's far-right threat has vanished, but a familiar dread returns as Meloni settles into office

blocks.text: That alternative — an opposition led by the Democratic Party and populist Five Star Movement that has shifted left — remains divided. Meloni, meanwhile, remains politically dominant within her own coalition, with Brothers of Italy polling well ahead of both the League and Forza Italia.
Her governing style also involves knowing when rhetoric and policy can quietly clash.

Migration is a case in point. Meloni campaigned vociferously on stopping migrant arrivals by sea to Italy — numbers that have sharply fallen from their 2023 peak — and built controversial offshore migrant processing centres in Albania.
Yet at the same time, her government has authorized almost half a million legal entries for non-EU workers between 2026 and 2028 to fill severe labour shortages driven by Italy's aging population.
The same pragmatic compromise has marked her foreign policy.

The only EU leader to attend Donald Trump's inauguration, Meloni was widely cast as Europe's natural bridge to the U.S. president. But building that bridge to Trump proved akin to engineering one across an Italian fault line: the relationship buckled over the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran and Trump's attacks on Pope Leo.
Italy's Meloni tells Trump to focus on his own popularity
That ability to adapt without appearing to abandon her political identity helps explain the credibility voters still give her, Pregliasco said.

She still talks about nation, family, motherhood and traditional values. She has tightened the rules around same-sex parenthood, and criticized feminists for focusing on gender quotas and symbolic battles over language, saying real equality meant a woman being free to become prime minister in the first place.
It's language that speaks squarely to a conservative electorate in one of the world's oldest countries.

items: Italy's PM Meloni fires back, tells Trump to worry about his own popularity
Is it normal for the U.S. president to spar with the Pope?

blocks.text: Stability vs. growth

But economist Veronica De Romanis, with Rome's Luiss University, says the same caution that has shielded Meloni politically has also held back deeper structural change in a country whose debt-to-GDP ratio is second only to Greece in the EU.
"Stability is an instrument," she said. "The goal is growth, economic growth, and we haven't seen that."

De Romanis credits the Meloni government with fiscal discipline, but adds its leader has failed to exploit four remarkably stable years to tackle weak productivity, low education spending or the precarious foothold women and young people have in Italy's labour market.

Higher female employment rates and higher fertility are positively correlated across Europe, she said, pushing back against the idea that getting more women into the workforce worsens Italy’s demographic problem.
"We cannot afford having one out of two women at home," she said.
Pressure from the right

As elections approach next year, a stagnant status quo is not Meloni's greatest threat. The outsider who built her career attacking the political establishment is now experiencing what it means to become the target.

Former general Roberto Vannacci, positioning himself to Meloni's right after breaking off from Salvini's League, is now trying to outflank her on immigration, security and social issues, including his opposition to 2SLGBTQ+ and abortion rights.
Vannacci gives Meloni something she has long avoided, Pregliasco said: "An opposition from the right which can basically speak the language of her electorate."
After a record 1,413 days in power, Meloni has demonstrated a rare instinct in modern Italian politics: knowing when to fight, when to back down and when to wait it out.
But whether Italians believe Meloni can transform political stability into lasting change may be a question they decide at the polls next year.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Megan Williams has been covering all things Italian, from politics and the Vatican, to food and culture, to the plight of migrants in the Mediterranean, for more than two decades. Based in Rome, Megan has also told stories from other parts of Europe and the world and won many international prizes for her reporting, including a James Beard Award. Her radio documentaries can be heard on Ideas and The Current. Megan is also a regular guest host on CBC national radio shows.

articles.title: Sara Duterte's bank, tax records furnished to impeachment trial prosecutors
articles.summary: The prosecution panel in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has been furnished with copies of her bank and tax records, those of her husband, Atty. Mans Carpio, and their businesses.

blocks.text: Published September 3, 2026 3:58pm

The prosecution panel in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has been furnished with copies of her bank and tax records, those of her husband, Atty. Mans Carpio, and their businesses.

This was announced by Bicol Saro Rep. Terry Ridon, the prosecutor assigned to handle the Article of Impeachment on alleged unexplained wealth. He said his team is already preparing for the presentation of evidence for the said article.

"Noon poong hapon ay binigyan na po ng kopya ang prosecution panel ng lahat ng bank information na hiningi mula po sa ating pangalawang pangulo, sa kanya pong asawa, at sa kanila poong mga kumpanya," Ridon said in a news conference.
"Binigyan na rin po ng kopya ng Senate impeachment court ang prosecution panel ng lahat po ng tax documents na nga ng pangalawang pangulo ng kanyang asawa, at ng kanila poong mga kumpanya," he added.

"So sa mga susunod pong mga araw, pag-aaralan at bubusisiin po namin yung lahat po ng mga dokumento pong ito. At ito po yung nagko-constitute ng last important pillar noon pong mga ebidensiya na gagamitin para sa unexplained wealth article," Ridon said.

(This afternoon, the prosecution panel was given a copy of all the bank information that was requested from our vice president, his wife, and their companies. The Senate impeachment court also gave the prosecution panel copies of all the tax documents for the vice president, his wife, and their companies. So in the coming days, we will study and scrutinize all these documents. And this is what constitutes the last important pillar of evidence that will be used for the unexplained wealth article.)
Ridon said the prosecution panel's unexplained wealth team is preparing to present evidence in mid- to late September.

"So we will study all the bank accounts and tax documents of Vice President Sara Duterte, her husband, and her companies to see if this evidence will constitute proof of the allegations in the unexplained wealth article, which would constitute a betrayal of public trust," Ridon said.
The Senate impeachment court on July 30 formally received Duterte and Carpio's financial and tax records in relation to her ongoing impeachment trial.
It also received around the same time the documentary evidence from the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC).

The court, the week before, started issuing subpoenas for Duterte’s tax and bank records in relation to the impeachment trial. Among those issued with subpoenas were the BIR, the AMLC, and several banks.

Impeachment trial clerk of court Renato Bantug at that time said, “The Senate Impeachment Court maintains the highest level of physical and procedural security over these records. Access is strictly controlled, and the chain of custody is heavily documented."

"The Clerk of Court will release the documents to the parties only after the meticulous inventory process is complete, and in the case of the AMLC, after the Presiding Officer completes his ‘in camera’ review," Bantug said then.
"The Impeachment Court will not rush the chain of custody. Security and accuracy take precedence over speed,” he added. –NB, GMA News

articles.title: Gilas ready for Asian Games defense with 11 players if Brownlee stays sidelined
articles.summary: Gilas Pilipinas head coach Tim Cone says Justin Brownlee, the hero of the 2023 championship squad, has yet to confirm his participation for the upcoming Asian Games

blocks.text: HERO. Justin Brownlee in action for Gilas Pilipinas against China in the 19th Asian Games.
PSC-POC Media Pool
Gilas Pilipinas head coach Tim Cone says Justin Brownlee, the hero of the 2023 championship squad, has yet to confirm his participation for the upcoming Asian Games

items: Gilas Pilipinas head coach Tim Cone confirmed that the team may only field 11 players in the Asian Games due to the uncertain availability of naturalized player Justin Brownlee, who is dealing with injuries.
The team has reserved the final roster spot for Brownlee, who has not yet confirmed his participation while working on medical clearances.
Despite the potential lack of a full roster, Cone believes that having fewer players can be beneficial for coaching, as it allows for extended playing time for those available.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – Gilas Pilipinas head coach Tim Cone confirmed the possibility of fielding only 11 players in the Asian Games as the availability of naturalized star Justin Brownlee remains uncertain.

Cone and his coaching staff have reserved the 12th and final roster spot for Brownlee, the hero of the 2023 squad that ended the country’s 61-year wait for a men’s basketball gold medal in the Asian Games.

Brownlee, however, has been hampered by injuries that kept him out of the Philippines’ last three games in the FIBA World Cup Asian Qualifiers, sitting out a blowout loss to Australia in the third window in July and then missing home wins over Jordan and Iran in the fourth window in August.
“We haven’t had a confirmation yet from Justin whether he’s going to be here or not. The door is still open for him,” Cone told reporters in an online press conference on Thursday, September 3.

“He’s still working on clearances from doctors in the States. So as soon as that’s all cleared up, we’ll have a clearer picture as well. But at this point, no, we don’t have a 12th player in mind to come over.”

Gilas Pilipinas’ Asian Games lineup features a mix of new faces and returning players, with Robert Bolick, Brandon Ganuelas-Rosser, and Don Trollano making their national team comeback, and Sedrick Barefield, Adrian Nocum, Zavier Lucero, Brandon Bates, and Jerrick Ahanmisi debuting for the squad.
They will be joined by RJ Abarrientos, Justine Baltazar, and Justin Arana — the only holdovers from the Asian Qualifiers crew.

Cone sees no problem with having only 11 players on the roster, noting that the national team thrived under similar circumstances when it reached the semifinals of the 2024 FIBA Olympic Qualifying Tournament (OQT) in Latvia.
If anything, Cone feels that coaching fewer players gives him less to worry about.

“We didn’t miss a beat there,” Cone said of the OQT, where the team lost Scottie Thompson just before the start of the tournament. “And I think we’ll be fine. These guys are all willing to play extended minutes.”

“And I think 11 is a really good number from a coaching standpoint in terms of not feeling like you have to force some guys who should be out there longer to play less because you want other guys to play.”
“It’s easier from a coaching standpoint, having oftentimes less players than having more.”

Gilas Pilipinas is currently in South Korea for a pair of tuneup games against its national team before it flies to Japan for the Asian Games, where the men’s basketball tournament will be held from September 10 to 20.
Bunched in Group C, the Philippines will face China, Bahrain, and Kazakhstan. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Senate scrutinizes Ombudsman's P1.66-B staffing request amid 51% vacancy rate
articles.summary: The Office of the Ombudsman"s request for P1.66 billion to fill 1,247 vacant positions came under scrutiny at the Senate finance committee hearing on Thursday, with lawmakers questioning whether the…

blocks.text: The Office of the Ombudsman’s request for P1.66 billion to fill 1,247 vacant positions came under scrutiny at the Senate finance committee hearing on Thursday, with lawmakers questioning whether the anti-graft agency can absorb the funds while more than half of its plantilla remains unfilled.

The Ombudsman has 2,439 authorized positions but only 1,192 filled positions, translating to a 51.1% vacancy rate, according to figures presented during the hearing on the agency’s proposed 2027 budget.
Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla said the agency was already working to fill the vacancies, noting that it had hired 60 lawyers this year and expected to hire another 40 by November.
He said the hiring process could take seven to eight months, from application to appointment, because of the agency’s stringent screening procedures and government personnel rules.

“For the 100 lawyers we’re hiring this year, including the 60 we already hired, there were 3,700 applicants. It’s a very, very good position for lawyers to aspire for, and the quality of the applicants is actually very, very impressive,” he said.
Remulla also cited space constraints in the Ombudsman’s existing offices as another factor affecting its capacity to expand its workforce. The agency is seeking funding for a new office building.
Senator Panfilo Lacson said the Ombudsman’s proposed staffing allocation could take years to fully utilize.
Remulla said that if given the resources, the agency could hire more than 400 personnel within a year, but acknowledged that filling all the vacancies could take about three years.
“It’s the absorptive capacity of the office. Hindi po tayo sanay sa malaking puwersa,” he said.
(It’s the absorptive capacity of the office. We are not accustomed to having such a large workforce.)

Lacson suggested that part of the staffing allocation could instead be realigned toward other Ombudsman priorities, including the proposed Ombudsman Marshal Service, particularly if the agency would not be able to obligate the entire staffing fund within the period covered by continuing appropriations.
The proposed Ombudsman Marshal Service would initially require 100 positions, with personnel deployed across Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao.
Remulla warns long-running graft cases risk dismissal
The staffing discussion came as Remulla emphasized the need to increase the Ombudsman’s capacity to investigate and prosecute corruption cases before they become bogged down in lengthy proceedings.
He told senators that some cases before the Sandiganbayan have been pending for decades.
The prolonged proceedings, he said, can result in cases being dismissed because of inordinate delay.

“We had cases which were filed in 1987, which are still in the Sandiganbayan. And there are so many cases that have a 15-year life already, and which of course results to dismissal because of the inordinate delay of justice," he said.

Remulla said the Ombudsman has set a target of continuously presenting its cases within one year from filing, which he described as an ideal timeline that would require cooperation from the Sandiganbayan.
“Among the most important of these is to be able to present our case continuously for one year, and our target is to be able to present our cases within a one-year period from filing,” he said.
He said shortening the period for resolving cases would help prevent problems involving lost evidence and witnesses, while ensuring that cases do not remain pending indefinitely.
The Ombudsman reported that as of June 30, 2026, it had 4,219 pending cases: 1,955 criminal cases, six forfeiture cases and 2,258 administrative cases.
The agency has also revised its procedures to shorten the fact-finding stage, with simple cases now subject to a 60-day period and complex cases to 90 days.
Resident Ombudsman program reactivated
Alongside the push to increase its overall workforce, the Ombudsman said it has also reactivated its Bureau of the Resident Ombudsman, which had been inactive for several years.
The agency has now hired 10 additional lawyers to augment the bureau.

After appropriate training, the lawyers will be deployed to government agencies, particularly high-revenue-generating agencies, where they are expected to investigate complaints and gather information on possible irregularities.

The Ombudsman initially proposed a P12.8-billion budget for 2027, but the National Expenditure Program recommended only P7.23 billion, prompting senators to examine which proposed programs and expenditures should be restored. — VBL, GMA News

articles.title: When you see the Ynares name, you know you’re in Rizal
articles.summary: The Ynares dynasty is intertwined with the province’s life and history

blocks.text: Editor’s note: This is part of a Rappler series on Filipino families that have held political power for generations. The series traces how they built their influence, where it is strongest, and how it has endured over time. Each profile examines family ties, political networks, business interests, and roles in local and national government.
Inside the grounds of the Rizal provincial capitol in Antipolo City is the Ynares Center, an indoor arena of 7,400 seats.
Scratch that. Rather: Inside the Ynares Center Complex is the Rizal provincial capitol.

Across Rizal, a province of 13 towns and one component city, are old waiting sheds with Y-shaped concrete columns. Covered courts have blue galvanized roofs and a facade with white painted text: Ynares multi-purpose covered court. The older ones are white and have the same name. Plastic chairs have “Ynares” embossed on the back.

Rizal sits east of Manila and used to be bigger until 1975, when Metro Manila was created and carved out some parts of it. The towns that were left went much farther east: Tanay and Pililia touching the borders of nearby provinces Laguna and Quezon. Binangonan’s Talim Island wedged in the middle of Laguna de Bay.

1901 was the year Rizal province was created. 1901 was when the story of the Ynares clan started as well — the year their patriarch, Don Jose Ynares y Granados, was appointed as presidente (or mayor) of Binangonan. Then he was elected in 1902 and went on to serve for four years.
The Ynares patriarch’s leadership was tied with the American colonizers. “With help from the Americans, Ynares made remarkable improvements in the town,” the town website said.
The next Ynares to claim Binangonan’s mayoralty was Casimiro Ynares Sr., son of Don Jose Ynares, from 1945 to 1946.

It is Casimiro “Yto” Ynares Jr., son of Casimiro Ynares Sr., who is more remembered in very recent history. Before becoming Rizal governor, Yto was Binangonan mayor for 15 years due to Martial Law, from 1971 to 1988. When Yto became Rizal governor in 1992, it was exactly 90 years after the first Ynares was elected in a Rizal town.
Since 1992, family members have occupied the position. Yto was Rizal governor for nine consecutive years (1992 to 2001) and served another term from 2004 to 2007.

Yto’s brothers, Cesar and Cecilio (known as Boyet), eventually became Binangonan mayors when Yto went on to become governor. Cesar prevailed for three terms and his brother Boyet succeeded him when he reached his term limit.
Not all of the siblings went to politics. Their sister, Consuelo Ynares-Santiago, was a Supreme Court justice who started as municipal judge of Cainta, Rizal.

blocks.caption: CLAN. Ynares family members who joined politics and held positions in Rizal. Many held top positions in Binangonan, while governorship was passed among Casimiro Ynares Jr.’s nuclear family. Graphic by Sam Calleja/Rappler

blocks.text: Casimiro “Jun” Ynares III, the only son among Yto’s three children, was the first to succeed his parents in the governorship.
His mother, Rebecca “Nini” Ynares, substituted for husband Yto when Yto was term-limited in 2001. Nini then substituted for son Jun in 2013 when Jun was term-limited as well.
Nini, the wife of Yto, served until 2022. When she reached her term limit, she was succeeded by their daughter, Nina Ricci Ynares, who is now on her second term as governor.
There are currently five members of the Ynares clan holding public office.
Jun is now Antipolo mayor. It was under his term that Antipolo City received its fourth seal of good governance in 2024.

His youngest sibling, Mia Ynares, is the congresswoman of the 1st District of Rizal, which is composed of four towns that include the Angono, the art capital; and Taytay, known as the garments capital of the Philippines.
Their cousins hold the fort in Binangonan: Rhea Ynares is mayor and Russel Ynares is vice mayor.

When Jun Ynares was term-limited in 2019, his wife Andrea “Andeng” Ynares, succeeded her husband. A member of the Revilla dynasty of Cavite, Andrea served as Antipolo mayor for only one term — as if just a placeholder until Jun could run again.

During the 2013 elections, crowds in yellow shirts gathered to protest alleged vote buying in Antipolo. Their placards read, “Lantarang pagbili ng boto ng mga Ynares.” (Open vote buying by the Ynareses.)
Jun Ynares had won by a razor-thin margin over reelectionist Antipolo mayor Nilo Leyble. Ynares got 128,108 votes against Leyble’s 121,032.

Jun denied the allegation. “Alam ‘nyo po dito sa napakatagal po natin sa larangan ng pulitika, wala hong ganyan…sa buong lalawigan ng Rizal,” Jun, who at the time was Rizal governor, said in an interview with GMA News on May 15.
(You know, I’ve been in politics for such a long time, there have been no [vote buying] in the province of Rizal. In the whole province of Rizal.)

blocks.caption: COURT. Multi-purpose covered courts across Rizal bear the Ynares name. Photo courtesy of Ralff Nestor Nacor/Wikimedia

blocks.text: The spat between the camps of Ynares and Leyble boiled over to an alleged murder plot against Jun and his father Yto. The assassination plot did not push through because according to the hitman allegedly hired to do the killings, the information given them were wrong and the plot supposedly became unnecessary because nobody thought Jun would win his first term as Antipolo mayor.

In 2025, there were no obstacles to Jun’s reelection bid. There was no real rival to pose a threat. There were no protests on the streets. Jun had 208,100 votes, a landslide victory over runner-up Red Llaga, who only got 55,027 votes.
That same year, Nina Ynares also won the gubernatorial race by a landslide, leading the second placer by more than 200,000 votes.
Since Jun’s close race in 2013, there had been no serious contenders against the Ynareses.
Another family, however, enjoys strong recall in Rizal: the Duavits, who opted for self-preservation and not to go against the Ynareses.

The Duavits ran alongside the Ynareses to ensure their grip on the congressional seat representing Rizal’s 1st District. The baton passed from Gilbert Duavit Sr., who started his term in 1994, to his sons Jack and Joel. Jack was Rizal congressman from 2001 to 2010, and again from 2016 to 2025.
In the last polls in 2025, no Duavit ran for the congressional post. At the time, Mia Ynares ran and won.

Other political stalwarts follow the same playbook. The politicians in the Puno and Acop families do not run against the Ynareses and instead go for lower posts. Josefina “Pining” Gatlabayan, another Rizal politician, served as Antipolo vice mayor to couple Jun and Andeng Ynares. She is now vice governor to Nina Ynares.

blocks.caption: GREETING. Mia Ynares with Jack Duavit, posted by the congresswoman for a birthday greeting online in February 2026. Photo courtesy of Mia Ynares/Facebook

blocks.text: Online, there are more disgruntled netizens complaining of the Ynareses. The threads touch on similar things: their more than three decades of rule over Rizal, alleged corruption and business links, and a general discontentment on matters of progress.
Lately, when the rainy season comes around, people would air out frustrations online over flooding and the seeming lack of viable solutions.

Beyond hearsay, however, any damning proof of corruption against the Ynareses has yet to surface. In 2022, the anti-graft court Sandiganbayan acquitted Yto Ynares of graft in relation to the procurement of fertilizers. Yto was Rizal governor in 2004, the year the fertilizer fund scam broke.

Rizal residents continue to vote for them. The Ynares name has recall and the heft of history intertwined with the province. It is a name that 30-year-olds grew up seeing on waiting sheds, in hospitals they visited for checkups, in the schools they attended.
“Wala namang ibang pagpipilian (There’s no one to choose from),” was how one Antipolo resident put it a month before the 2025 elections.
She offered some justification, “Marami naman silang naging achievement dito sa Antipolo eh.” (They had a lot of achievements in Antipolo.) – with a report from Dwight de Leon/Rappler.com

articles.title: DPWH eyes study of Aquino admin flood control master plan -- Malacañang
articles.summary: Malacañang said Thursday that the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) is considering looking into the master plan on flood management by the administration of former president Benigno…

blocks.text: Published September 3, 2026 3:34pm

Malacañang said Thursday that the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) is considering looking into the master plan on flood management by the administration of former president Benigno Aquino III.
Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said this at a press briefing, citing information from Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon.
“Sa ngayon po ay merong nababanggit si Secretary Vince Dizon patungkol do’n sa Aquino-Singson master plan. At ‘yan po ang isa sa mga maaaring pag-aralan,” Castro said.
(Secretary Vince Dizon has mentioned the Aquino-Singson master plan, and that is one of the things that could be studied.)

“Kasama na rin ang binanggit ni Secretary Vince Dizon patungkol sa flood control master plans para sa major river basins. So ‘yan po ay pagsasama-samahin at titignan at kailangan na po rin i-update,” she added.
(He also mentioned the flood control master plans for major river basins. So, these will be consolidated, reviewed, and updated.)
Castro said the President also underscored the need to update plans that would respond to the effects of climate change.

To recall, back in 2012, the Aquino administration approved a P351-billion long-term flood management master plan to solve the flooding problem in the National Capital Region, which was considered the “most expensive and ambitious” at that time.
Then-DPWH Secretary Rogelio Singson said that the full implementation of the flood control plan will only be realized in 2035 because it involves large-scale infrastructure projects.
According to Castro, the master plan was not turned over by the administration of former president Rodrigo Duterte to the current administration.
President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. said Wednesday the country has had a flood control master plan for decades but was never executed until now.

Asked about which master plan was the President referring to, Castro said, “Kung history ang pag-uusapan natin, mga 1940s, 1930s ay meron na pong master plan. Ngunit sa mga nakaraang mga dekada ay hindi ito nasunod.”
(If we talk about history, a master plan already existed as early as the 1930s or 1940s. However, this was not implemented in the decades that followed.) — RSJ, GMA News

September 3, 2026
Police say Munich arson attack may have targeted defense company

Following an arson attack on a construction site in Munich, the Bavarian State Criminal Police Office (LKA) said Thursday it suspects the fire was an attempted attack on a company involved in the defense industry.
Investigators are looking into a possible political motive, an LKA spokesperson said. The spokesperson did not immediately identify the company involved.

However, the Bild tabloid reported that the fire was set at a construction site near the headquarters of Rohde & Schwarz, a technology company that produces communication systems for the Bundeswehr, among other things.
A spokesperson for the company confirmed the police and fire department response, emphasizing, however, "our company premises themselves are not affected," public broadcaster BR reported.
Police said multiple incendiary devices were thrown from a vehicle at the construction site in the Berg am Laim borough early Thursday morning around midnight.

At least one of the incendiary devices sparked a fire that police officers extinguished. Despite the fire, no major damage was caused, a Munich police spokesperson said. However, another incendiary device had to be defused by special forces.
Following a short manhunt, a 28-year-old woman and a 38-year-old man were arrested at a nearby gas station, and were being questioned Thursday.

articles.title: Gov’t vows to address economic woes amid weakening peso
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang on Thursday said the government will continue working to boost the country’s economy after the Philippine peso hit a new record low of P62.565 against the dollar. The…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang on Thursday said the government will continue working to boost the country’s economy after the Philippine peso hit a new record low of P62.565 against the dollar.
The currency weakened 16.5 centavos and closed at P62.565according to data from the Bankers Association of the Philippines.
At a briefing, Palace press officer Claire Castro allayed fears that this could drive up goods and basic commodity prices and disrupt investments.
“Even before alam natin kung ano ang nais ng Pangulo at ano ang nais ng administrasyon na ito: Lahat ng puwedeng gawing paraan upang mas tumaas ang ekonomiya, lumago ang ekonomiya,” she said.
(We already know what the President and this administration wants – To implement every possible measure to boost and grow the economy.)
Castro said it just so happens that the country is significantly affected by the Middle East crisis, especially since it is still relying on the region for crude oil supply.

“Pero hindi po natatapos ang pagtatrabaho ng gobyerno dahil nandiyan pa rin po ang UPLIFT [Unified Package for Livelihoods, Industry, Food, and Transport] kung saan binubusisi kung paano pa maiibsan ang mga nadadanas ng ating mga kababayan lalung-lalo na sa pagtaas ng mga presyo ng bilihin,” said Castro.

(However, the government’s work does not stop there, as UPLIFT [Unified Package for Livelihoods, Industry, Food, and Transport] remains in place to carefully study how to further alleviate the hardships faced by our fellow citizens, especially regarding the rising prices of commodities.)

“So, nakaagapay pa rin po ang gobyerno, nandiyan pa rin po iyong sinasabi nating bente pesos na bigas para sa ating mas nangangailangan, nandiyan pa rin po iyong umiiral natin na zero balance billing para sa DOH [Department of Health] hospitals at sa mga pili na LGU [local governmrnt unit] hospitals, nandiyan din po iyong mga libre na toll fee sa mga buses at sa mga nagde-deliver ng mga agricultural products,” she continued.

(So, the government continues to provide support; the twenty-peso rice program for the needy remains in place, as does the zero-balance billing policy in DOH hospitals and select LGU hospitals, along with toll fee exemptions for buses and vehicles delivering agricultural products.)
Castro said the administration’s economic team is yet to discuss proposals to trim non-essential spending amid the weak peso.

Citing a statement from the Office of the Executive Secretary, Castro said the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas was expected “to act decisively based on available data and intervene when necessary to reduce exchange rate volatility.”

“The administration’s approach is focused on fiscal discipline and more efficient use of public funds; this means reviewing spending proposals carefully and prioritizing programs that have high economic and social returns,” the office’ statement read. /gsg

articles.title: Over 500,000 hectares of land handed out to tillers, DAR says
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – More than 500,000 hectares of farmlands has been distributed to beneficiaries ever since President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. took office in 2022, Agrarian Reform Secretary Conrado…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – More than 500,000 hectares of farmlands has been distributed to beneficiaries ever since President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. took office in 2022, Agrarian Reform Secretary Conrado Estrella III said on Thursday.

During the deliberations on the the proposed 2027 budget of the Department of Agrarian Reform (DAR), Estrella told members of the House of Representatives committee on appropriations that his agency had distributed 410,179 titles covering 556,088 hectares to 376,738 agrarian reform beneficiaries identified.
“The years 2022 to 2026 may aptly be described as banner years for the Department of Agrarian Reform,” Estrella told lawmakers.

From the January to August 2026 period, DAR distributed 16,032 titles covering 23,574 hectares to 14,032 beneficiaries. In 2025, the agency had apportioned 199,838 titles over 23,574 hectares to 176,202 farmers, according to its presentation.
In 2024, 88,310 farmers received 102,546 land titles over 120,772 hectares of land. The agency gave away 69,897 titles for 84,044 hectares to 73,399 beneficiaries in 2023.
In the first year of President Ferdinand Marcos, Jr.’s government, DAR released 21,876 titles over 25,159 hectares to 24,804 farmers, based on the presentation.
Land reform is a contentious issue in the Philippines, a traditionally agricultural nation where vestiges of Spanish colonial land ownership have been inherited and sustained across decades.
About 5.4 million hectares of land were earmarked for distribution to farmers under the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform law, which aimed to reduce inequality by diffusing farmlands to tillers. /mr

articles.title: Tacloban prosecs to file criminal raps vs 15-yr-old boy over school shooting
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines—Department of Justice (DOJ) prosecutors in Tacloban City are set to file frustrated murder and attempted murder charges against a 15-year-old student accused in a shooting in a…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines—Department of Justice (DOJ) prosecutors in Tacloban City are set to file frustrated murder and attempted murder charges against a 15-year-old student accused in a shooting in a public school two months ago.

The prosecutors believe that the accused was “acting with discernment” when he brought a gun at San Jose National High School on June 22 and fired it, leaving left three dead and at least 20 others injured.

According to DOJ Undersecretary Ian Norman Dato, prosecutors are filing of four counts of frustrated murder and six counts of attempted murder before a regional trial court against one of the two Grade 9 students who were identified to be behind the shooting.
“Our prosecutors found that he acted with discernment and in conspiracy with a second minor,” Dato said in a press briefing on Thursday.
The other perpetrator is a 14-year-old Grade 9 student who is considered exempt from criminal liability under existing laws.
Both were placed in custody of a rehabilitation facility managed by the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD).

A bail of P72,000 for each count of frustrated murder and P36,000 for each count for the attempted murder was recommended for the 15-year-old boy, who is now considered a child in conflict with the law (CICL).

The 15-year-old CICL is also facing three counts of murder, three counts of frustrated murder and multiple counts of physical injury, which were filed by the Police Regional Office in Eastern Visayas in June.
Tacloban prosecutors last week, meanwhile, also recommended the filing of reckless imprudence resulting in multiple homicide and physical injuries against Police Staff Sergeant Arla Rey Pacencia.
Pacencia is the aunt of the 14-year-old boy and owner of the government-issued 9mm Glock 17 firearm used in the incident. /apl

articles.title: Some senator-judges eyeing revised impeachment vote threshold – Zubiri
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – With an incomplete roster of senator-judges participating in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial, some senators looking at the possibility of lowering the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – With an incomplete roster of senator-judges participating in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial, some senators looking at the possibility of lowering the 16-vote threshold to either convict or acquit the vice president, Sen. Juan Miguel Zubiri said on Thursday.

When Duterte’s impeachment trial commenced on July 6, three senator-judges were already unable to participate, but the Senate impeachment court ruled that the two-thirds vote required to make a final ruling on the vice president’s case would be maintained.
Twenty-one trial days have lapsed since the ruling was made, and Zubiri admitted that some of his colleagues are concerned about the voting threshold.
“There were some colleagues who would like to revisit the threshold… dahil kasi may mga nasa kulungan at isa pugante-at-large,” Zubiri told the media.
(There were some colleagues who would like to revisit the threshold… because there are some in prison and one is a fugitive-at-large.)
Asked whether some senators hoped that there would be a ruling on lowering the voting threshold, Zubiri answered in the affirmative.
Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa has been on the run since May 14 from his arrest warrant for alleged crimes against humanity issued by the International Criminal Court.
Meanwhile, Sen. Jinggoy Estrada was placed on a 90-day preventive suspension on June 16 by the Sandiganbayan after his arrest on June 1 for plunder.
Likewise, Sen. Rodante Marcoleta was arrested for plunder on July 6.

In August, Sen. Loren Legarda failed to attend the impeachment proceedings after taking consecutive medical leaves. Zubiri, and previously Sen. Panfilo Lacson, said that Legarda is facing a “serious” medical condition. /gsg

articles.title: LRTA: Villar group set to sign pact on LRT-1 Las Piñas station build
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Villar Group of Companies is set to sign an agreement with the national government regarding the donation of parcels of land which will be the site of the Light Rail Transit…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Villar Group of Companies is set to sign an agreement with the national government regarding the donation of parcels of land which will be the site of the Light Rail Transit Line 1 (LRT-1) Las Piñas Station, the Light Rail Transit Authority (LRTA) said.

During Thursday’s briefing of the House of Representatives’ committee on appropriations regarding the Department of Transportation (DOTr) proposed budget for 2027, Las Piñas City Rep. Mark Anthony Santos asked for developments on the construction of the said station.

LRTA Administrator Hernando Cabrera said that upon meeting with the senior executives of Villar group last week, they are confident that the two parcels of land will be released from mortgage this September. Once they are released, Cabrera noted that the Villar group committed to signing a memorandum of agreement (MOA) with them.

“Confident sila na pagdating ng September, marerelease na yung dalawang property na yun kaya willing na silang pumirma anytime at upon signing, nakaintegrate na doon sa MOA na after 30 days pagkapirma ng MOA, pwede na po naming gamitin at pasukin ang property,” Cabrera said.

(They are confident that the two properties will be released from mortgage in September, that’s why they are now willing to sign anytime and it is integrated in the MOA that 30 days upon the signing of the agreement, we can now use and enter the property.)

Amid delays of the construction of Las Piñas station, the Villar group earlier said that they would donate six parcels of land where the station is expected to be built. Of the six parcels, two are mortgaged.

The DOTr previously shared that the group agreed to its terms for the construction of the station, such as giving the agency unconditional permit to enter, waiver of any liability on the part of the government, and cancellation of mortgage on the land to be donated.

Cabrera noted that they also need permits to enter from other parcels of land, aside from those owned by the Villars, for the construction of the station. He noted that land owners did not entertain the government before as there was no assurance that the Villar group would donate its parcels of land.

“Ngayong mayroon nang kaliwanagan, willing na silang ientertain kami at mamadaliin namin na matapos namin yung negotiated procurement at makakuha kami ng permit to enter para maisakatuparan yung mga hakbang,” he added.
(Now that there is clarity, they are willing to entertain us and we will fast track to finish the negotiated procurement and obtain a permit to enter to fulfill our plans.)
The administrator also shared that there are currently no financial and technical issues that can further delay the construction of the Las Piñas station.

Meanwhile, when asked by Santos on the target date of the station’s construction, Cabrera said that it might be done in three years. He explained that this timeline includes factors such as property acquisition, demolition, and designing of the said station.

As the LRT-1 Cavite Extension Project broke ground in 2019, the completion of Las Piñas, Zapote, and Niog stations will bring the total train stations to 28. The LRT-1 currently runs from Fernando Poe Jr. station in Quezon City to Dr. Santos station in Parañaque City. /mr

articles.title: Another portion of Minalin Tail Dike road collapses in Pampanga
articles.summary: MABALACAT CITY, Pampanga — Another portion of the tail dike in Minalin, Pampanga collapsed early Thursday morning due to the strong river current. Minalin Mayor Philip Siojo Naguit said part of…

blocks.text: MABALACAT CITY, Pampanga — Another portion of the tail dike in Minalin, Pampanga collapsed early Thursday morning due to the strong river current.
Minalin Mayor Philip Siojo Naguit said part of the San Fernando-Sto. Tomas-Minalin Tail Dike at Barangay San Nicolas is now impassable to all three-wheel and four-wheel vehicles.
In a social media post, the mayor also said only residents on motorcycles who are buying necessities are allowed to pass along the partially damaged tail dike road.
Naguit said the collapsed portion is about 60 meters away from the section of the tail dike at Barangay Sta. Catalina that was breached by raging currents on August 30.
The Sta. Catalina portion of the tail dike is currently being reinforced by the Department of Public Works and Highways to mitigate flooding in affected villages.
Meanwhile, Naguit appealed to boat owners and helmsmen fetching passengers in deeply flooded areas of his town to be more considerate in charging fees.

“I am making a sincere appeal to boat operators. I know I cannot regulate your rates, but we are in a time when our fellow citizens are struggling financially. I hope you will not raise your charges. I understand you are working to earn a living, but please do not take advantage of the situation,” he said in the vernacular. The mayor did not reveal how much the fees are being contested.
Several Minalin residents who commented on the post lauded the mayor’s appeal.

“Thank you for pointing out the boat fare. It is so expensive. I hope no one takes advantage of the situation because it is heartbreaking to see those who cannot afford the fare forced to wade and walk through the dirty water,” a Minalin resident said./coa

articles.title: Remulla rules out bid for chief justice: “I’m not applying”
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla Thursday said he is not vying for the position of Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, dismissing reports that he was among those aspiring to…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla Thursday said he is not vying for the position of Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, dismissing reports that he was among those aspiring to replace Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo, who is set to retire in November.
“I am not applying,” Remulla told reporters at the sidelines of the Senate finance committee’s deliberations on the Office of the Ombudsman’s proposed 2027 budget.
“I have no more aspirations. This is the job I want for myself…to be able to finish this job,” said Remulla, who was appointed Ombudsman in October 2025 and will serve until 2032.
Remulla, along with other OMB officials, appeared before the Senate body to defend the agency’s proposed P7.2-billion budget for 2027.
The Senate committee has approved at the committee level the proposed budget of the OMB, as lawmakers moved to strengthen the agency’s capacity to investigate and prosecute corruption.
At the hearing, Remulla raised concerns over delays in the justice system, particularly decisions by the Court of Appeals reversing cases dismissed by the Ombudsman.

“It’s just probably unfortunate that I have to mention this. Many of those that we have dismissed in the Office of the Ombudsman institutionally, in many cases, we’re talking about many, many cases, that were reversed by the Court of Appeals,” he said.
“That is a trend that’s known to the whole Office of the Ombudsman,” Remulla said, adding that he had discussed the matter with Supreme Court Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen.

“I told him about this problem that we have because institutionally, it’s very discouraging to be conducting all of these activities only to be reversed by the Court of Appeals decision that came out of nowhere,” he said.
He acknowledged that it was unusual for lawyers to criticize the courts but said the issue needed to be raised.

“As a lawyer, it’s not really common for lawyers to complain about the courts. But sometimes we just have to raise that issue already because it can be the biggest elephant in the room, within our justice system,” he added.
Remulla later told the media that his remarks were prompted by his experience as a lawyer and government official and “something that I have to do for the country.”
“I think my experience as a lawyer and government official and advocate speak for itself, It something that everybody knows but somebody should say it,” he added. /dp

articles.title: Laguna Lake water level stays above critical-high mark
articles.summary: LUCENA CITY — The water level at Laguna de Bay remained at 12.65 meters, still above its critical-high mark, the Laguna Lake Development Authority (LLDA) reported on Thursday. In its 9:15 a.m.…

blocks.text: LUCENA CITY — The water level at Laguna de Bay remained at 12.65 meters, still above its critical-high mark, the Laguna Lake Development Authority (LLDA) reported on Thursday.

In its 9:15 a.m. advisory, the LLDA said the lake’s water level exceeded its critical-high level of 12.50 meters “due to persistent torrential rains brought by the southwest monsoon and a Low Pressure Area.”
The latest reading was unchanged from Wednesday’s 12.65-meter level.
However, it remained 2 centimeters lower than the 12.67-meter level recorded at 10 a.m. Tuesday.
The LLDA considers 10.50 meters as the lake’s critical-low water level and 12.50 meters as its critical-high level.
The agency urged lakeshore residents to remain vigilant and closely monitor official announcements.

Laguna de Bay serves as a natural catch basin for water draining from watersheds in Laguna and Rizal provinces, as well as parts of Metro Manila. Rising lake levels can increase the risk of flooding in low-lying communities along its shores.

Meanwhile, the fisherfolk’s group Pambansang Lakas ng Kilusang Mamamalakaya ng Pilipinas (Pamalakaya) reported on Tuesday that more than 20,000 kilograms of tilapia and bighead carp have died in another fish kill episode at Laguna de Bay.
The group said the incident affected more than 30 fish cages covering over seven hectares in Jala-jala town, Rizal, with initial losses estimated at P700,000.
Fishers and operators suspect chemical waste may have contributed to the fish kill.
The LLDA has yet to issue a report on the incident.

In an Aug. 21 advisory, however, the LLDA said prevailing cloudy conditions and elevated lake levels were generally less favorable for immediate algal growth, which typically thrives in warm, sunny, and stagnant conditions.

The agency said warming waters can accelerate algal growth, which decomposes and consume dissolved oxygen in the water. The agency said dissolved oxygen levels below 5 milligrams per liter can already stress fish, while further depletion may result in fish kills. INQ

articles.title: DFA: ‘Geopolitical forces’ led to failed PH’s UN Security Council bid
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro cited “forces in geopolitical issues” as factors behind the Philippines’ failed bid for a nonpermanent seat on the United Nations…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro cited “forces in geopolitical issues” as factors behind the Philippines’ failed bid for a nonpermanent seat on the United Nations (UN) Security Council.

Lazaro told lawmakers that securing the seat had required a “herculean” campaign, as she faced questions about the Philippines’ loss during a House of Representatives appropriations committee hearing on the Department of Foreign Affairs’ proposed 2027 budget.
“Unfortunately, there are many other forces in geopolitical issues,” she maintained.

“If a reason is being asked why we failed in our bid, the only answer to that is the geopolitical issues. I can spell it, but I would prefer in writing so I can tell you. But, it is geopolitical issues,” she added without further expounding.
The Philippines lost to Kyrgyzstan in its bid last June for a nonpermanent seat on the UN Security Council for the 2026–2027 term.
For its part, Malacañang blamed “political noise from obstructionists” for the country’s loss.
At the hearing, DFA Financial Management Services chief Assistant Secretary Emilio Fernandez noted that their department had been allotted a total of P70 million through its 2025 and 2026 budgets.
Fernandez added that, of the P70 million allotted, only P52.5 million had been utilized.
The Philippines previously served on the council in 1957, 1963, 1980–1981 and 2004–2005, while Kyrgyzstan had never served on the council before. /dl

items: The Office of the Ombudsman reported that 35 cases related to the flood control scandal are pending in courts, with 31 in the Sandiganbayan and 4 in regional courts.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – The Office of the Ombudsman told senators on Thursday, September 3, that a total of 35 cases related to the multi-billion-peso flood control scandal are now pending in courts.
Ombudsman Jesus Crispin “Boying” Remulla said of this number, 31 are with the anti-graft court Sandiganbayan, while the remaining four are with various regional courts.

blocks.caption: 35 flood control cases now pending in courts – Ombudsman

blocks.text: Although the Sandiganbayan is the designated anti-corruption tribunal, certain lower courts are also mandated to handle corruption cases.

Under Republic Act No. 10660, Regional Trial Courts (RTCs) have jurisdiction over graft or corruption cases that do not specify damage to the government, or when the amount of damage is not more than P1 million. Lower courts, designated by the Supreme Court, also handle cases against public officers with salary grades lower than Grade 27, based on Batas Pambansa Bilang 129 or the Judiciary Reorganization Act.
Big ticket cases, like the plunder and graft cases against Senator Jinggoy Estrada, and the graft and malversation cases against former Ako Bicol representative Zaldy Co are with the Sandiganabayan.
Although they have charges before the anti-graft court, former Department of Public Works and Highways engineers like Brice Hernandez also face corruption cases before a Quezon City RTC.
Meanwhile, Remulla said the Ombudsman is currenty conducting preliminary investigation into 166 flood control-related complaints, and 107 lifestyle checks on public officials and employees.
Preliminary investigation is the stage in criminal proceedings where prosecutors are determining whether a complaint has enough evidence to become a case and be filed before a court.
Remulla took office in 2025, just as the flood control scandal erupted.

Estrada is so far the highest-ranking official to be arrested in connection with the scandal. However, efforts to hold others linked to the flood control corruption accountable have faced hurdles, including Co’s continued evasion of the law. The former lawmaker has been out of the country since 2025 and has yet to get his day in court. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Poa admits he could face liability if VP Duterte is found guilty
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines —Michael Poa, who previously worked as Vice President Sara Duterte’s chief of staff, undersecretary for finance and spokesperson at the Department of Education (DepEd), admitted…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines —Michael Poa, who previously worked as Vice President Sara Duterte’s chief of staff, undersecretary for finance and spokesperson at the Department of Education (DepEd), admitted on Wednesday that he could face liability if Duterte is found guilty of misusing millions of pesos in confidential funds, though he maintained that he had no personal knowledge of how the money was spent.

Poa is currently serving on Duterte’s legal defense team, but is taking the stand as a hostile prosecution witness on Day 21 of her impeachment trial, also said he learned about the unusual names appearing in acknowledgment receipts for confidential fund payments only during congressional hearings in 2024, even though he had prepared DepEd’s response to a Commission on Audit (COA) audit observation memorandum (AOM) questioning P112.5 million in confidential expenditures.

Asked by Senator-judge Risa Hontiveros whether Office of the Vice President (OVP) and DepEd personnel could be held accountable if Duterte were found liable, Poa said: “It’s possible. Just being objective, Your Honor.”
Hontiveros then asked if Poa himself could face liability.
“It’s possible. I hope not, but possible,” he replied.
No operational role

Poa maintained that he had no operational role in handling the confidential funds. He said his involvement began only after he received the COA’s AOM flagging DepEd’s confidential fund reward payments. Before that, he said, he had no personal knowledge of how the funds were used.

After receiving the AOM, Poa said he approached then Undersecretary for Administration Nolasco Mempin to obtain proof of the success of activities supposedly funded through the rewards, particularly accomplishment reports.

Mempin, whom Poa said also had no personal knowledge of the funds’ use, eventually obtained certifications from Armed Forces of the Philippines officers, including Col. Manaros Boransing II and Col. Magtanggol Panopio.

But Boransing and Panopio told the impeachment court on Tuesday that they did not know their certifications would be used to support the liquidation of DepEd’s confidential expenditures. The two Army officers said their documents merely recorded participants’ attendance in eight Army-sponsored Youth Leadership Summits and 53 Information Education Campaign activities. They also testified that neither DepEd nor the OVP provided the AFP with confidential funds for those programs.
“Unfortunately, all that really came to me was this certification. So, that’s all I attached to our response to COA,” he said.
‘Impression’ and ‘theory’

Poa also softened his earlier explanation to the House that activities supported by the confidential funds were targeted based on information supplied by informants, describing that explanation as merely his “impression” and “theory.”

Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian pointed out that Poa’s written response to the COA sounded more definitive, making it appear that information from informants had directly contributed to successful operations.

“How do you now prove that this success is from confidential information, from payment of rewards? How do you connect this to a successful payment of reward that led to a successful operation?” Gatchalian asked.
He also told private prosecutor Benjamin Tolosa Jr. that buying information from informants did not necessarily guarantee an immediately successful operation.

“Not all information purchased will necessarily result [in] immediate success,” Poa said when asked whether proof of success was required under Joint Circular 2015-01, which governs the use of confidential and intelligence funds.
Senator-judge Joel Villanueva questioned Poa on the basis for using AFP certifications to support DepEd’s P15.54 million in confidential fund expenditures.
‘Abogadong walang alam’

Poa said he did not consider the certifications in isolation, pointing to language in the documents referring to a “synergistic exchange of intelligence and information” that enabled authorities to identify areas where activities would be conducted.

The prosecution’s offer of Poa’s testimony triggered a sharp exchange after Tolosa described him as “ang abogadong walang alam (lawyer who knew nothing),” referring to his being tasked by Duterte to answer the COA despite repeatedly saying he did not know how the confidential funds were used.

Defense lead counsel Sheila Sison vehemently objected, saying Poa had rights under the trial rules to be protected from irrelevant, improper and insulting questions and from harsh or insulting treatment. Tolosa apologized and said he meant only that Poa had repeatedly testified in the House that he knew nothing about the funds.
Presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero ordered the phrase stricken from the record, saying it was discourteous and should not be used in referring to a fellow lawyer.
Names surfaced in House
Poa’s testimony also underscored the limits of his knowledge of the documents used to liquidate the confidential funds.

Asked by Senator-judge Erwin Tulfo whether he was familiar with names appearing in acknowledgment receipts submitted to the COA as proof of payment to supposed confidential informants, Poa said he did not remember seeing anything fictitious while at DepEd. He said he saw the unusual names only when the receipts were shown during the House inquiry in 2024, including the controversial “Mary Grace Piattos.”

When he asked former DepEd special disbursing officer Edward Fajarda for documents evidencing payments required for the COA audit, Poa said Fajarda initially handed him a sealed envelope, saying the documents were confidential. Poa asked to see at least one sample because he was responsible for submitting DepEd’s response to the COA. The envelope was opened and he was shown an acknowledgment receipt.
‘First time’ hearing of Nolasco

Poa prepared DepEd’s response to COA’s AOM covering confidential expenditures for the first three quarters of 2023. The COA had flagged the lack of documents supporting the use of P112.5 million in confidential funds. Poa submitted DepEd’s response for the first two quarters in February 2024 and for the third quarter in April.
Poa likewise testified that he first learned during the 2024 congressional hearings that the confidential funds had allegedly been transferred to a security officer.

He had previously said that only Duterte and Fajarda were privy to the use of the funds. But Fajarda testified during the House inquiry that he had turned over the funds to Col. Dennis Nolasco, then deputy chief of the Vice Presidential Security and Protection Group.

Tolosa asked whether Fajarda’s statement was the first time Poa learned of Nolasco’s involvement. Poa said it was, adding that it was also the first time he learned that Nolasco was a security officer and that Fajarda had transferred the funds to him.
Poa agreed that when he prepared DepEd’s response to the COA, he did not know about Nolasco’s role and could not have spoken with him about payments supposedly made to informants.
Meanwhile, the House prosecution panel is weighing whether to abandon the bribery article against Duterte.

Public prosecutor Joel Chua said in a press briefing that the panel was studying whether to proceed directly to the unexplained wealth article after completing its presentation on the alleged misuse of P612.5 million in confidential funds.
“We are considering dropping one article,” Chua told reporters, stressing that no final decision had been made. The panel is still weighing an option.

Chua said dropping one article could shorten the proceedings, with the prosecution hoping to finish its presentation by the first week or middle of October, the defense by November and the impeachment court potentially issuing a decision by December. — With reports from Zacarian Sarao and Keith Clores /das

articles.title: US, Australia to boost defense ties amid China's growing influence
articles.summary: The two countries said they had agreed to speed up cooperation and boost US military presence in Australia to counter China's unprecedented military buildup.

image.caption: Australian Defense Minister Richard Marles (left) said collaborating with the US was key to continued stability in the regionImage: Mark Schiefelbein/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: The United States and Australia have announced plans to boost defense ties and strengthen deterrence amid China's growing influence in the Pacific.

US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth met his Australian counterpart, Richard Marles, in Washington on Wednesday, saying Canberra understood "the gravity of maintaining a favorable balance of power in the region."

Marles told reporters that "American force ⁠posture ⁠in Australia is growing" and that the expanding cooperation was a response to "the biggest conventional military build-up by any country in the world since the Second World War in the form of China."
"We need to be ensuring that we build deterrence, that we build balance, so that we can provide for the peace and stability of the region in which we live," he added.
China's gray zone warfare in the Pacific
What did the two countries agree?

The Pentagon said the two countries agreed to "accelerate force posture initiatives at Australian bases, bolster cooperation in combined logistics, and build greater interoperability through joint exercises."
The force posture initiatives are agreements allowing the US military to train and store equipment in Australia, including the rotational deployment of aircraft and logistics support for US vessels.

While Australia does not permit foreign military bases on its soil, it does host several key joint exercises and rotations of US Marines in the northern city of Darwin. It was not clear if the agreement will see more US troops stationed in Australia.
According to the Pentagon, the two countries also discussed progress on cooperation "to enable shared capacity for guided weapons and next-generation capabilities."
Hegseth said in a statement ⁠that ​there was "strong alignment" between the national defense strategies of both countries.
He also stressed the importance of allies investing in their own sovereign security and the need for them to "both plan together but also ensure our capabilities match and are complementary."
How Pacific islands beat the China-Australia power struggle
Australia has sought to strengthen its defense force in recent years, focusing on boosting its missile strike capability and deepening strategic alliances.

Cooperation between the US and Australia also includes the AUKUS defense pact with Britain. As part of that pact, American defense personnel are working at the HMAS Stirling naval base in Western Australia, which is set to host a rotating force of US-commanded submarines from 2027.
China has called the AUKUS pact dangerous and warned it could spark a regional arms race.

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz drops first set, rallies to reach US Open 3rd round
articles.summary: NEW YORK— Carlos Alcaraz was already in the final by the time he dropped a set last year in the U.S. Open. When it happened in his second match this year, Alcaraz tried to look at the positives.…

blocks.text: Carlos Alcaraz, of Spain, reacts during a match against Jaime Faria, of Portugal, during the second round of the U.S. Open tennis championships, Wednesday, Sept. 2, 2026, in New York. (AP Photo/Adam Hunger)
NEW YORK— Carlos Alcaraz was already in the final by the time he dropped a set last year in the U.S. Open.
When it happened in his second match this year, Alcaraz tried to look at the positives. After missing four months with a right wrist injury, the extra work might help.

“I wanted to be quick, to be honest. I’m not going to lie,” Alcaraz said. “But at the end, I realized that just playing four sets, it was really good for me to test everything physically, to test my body, how I feel, and tomorrow how I’m going to feel after this match.”
The defending champion rebounded from a quick deficit by winning eight straight games and beat Jaime Faria 4-6, 6-0, 6-3, 6-2 on Wednesday night.
The No. 2-seeded Alcaraz dropped his serve midway through the first set but soon was back to playing long stretches of flawless tennis.
“After that I just tried to be focused, tried to stay calm and I’m thinking that good things are going to happen again,” Alcaraz said.

He didn’t drop a set last year until the final against Jannik Sinner, becoming the first man since Roger Federer in 2015 to go through his first six matches without doing so. He then beat Sinner in four sets for his second U.S. Open title.
The 23-year-old Alcaraz then picked up his seventh major title at this year’s Australian Open and is on a 16-match winning streak in Grand Slam tournaments.

blocks.caption: Carlos Alcaraz, of Spain, left, meets Jaime Faria, of Portugal, at the net after winning a match during the second round of the U.S. Open tennis championships, Wednesday, Sept. 2, 2026, in New York. (AP Photo/Adam

blocks.text: Carlos Alcaraz, of Spain, left, meets Jaime Faria, of Portugal, at the net after winning a match during the second round of the U.S. Open tennis championships, Wednesday, Sept. 2, 2026, in New York. (AP Photo/Adam Hunger)
But after missing the French Open and Wimbledon during his absence, even Alcaraz said he didn’t know what to expect in Flushing Meadows, where he won his first major title in 2022 at 19.
Daniil Medvedev, the U.S. Open champion the year before that, said a player of Alcaraz’s caliber is always a top contender any time he is in the field.
“We have no idea how Carlos’ wrist is going to feel, body is going to feel going later into the tournament, but he’s definitely a top favorite for the title,” Medvedev said.
Faria, three months younger than Alcaraz, broke for a 4-3 lead in the first set and used a powerful serve to stay ahead. Alcaraz felt after getting broken that he was rushing too much.
“After that I just wanted to play short points, which was a mistake for me,” he said. “I just needed to play patient, to play long rallies, three, four, five shots, and then go for it.”
Alcaraz stressed again that he is no longer in pain and has been hitting his forehand without any restrictions in practice.

“I know once I step on the court, I’ve just got to go for it every time. I’ve got to feel normal,” Alcaraz said. “I have to hit like I was hitting before the injury, and let’s see what happens after that.
“I’m just feeling great,” he added. “There is no reason to be afraid and not hitting normal.”

articles.title: Another portion of Minalin Tail Dike road collapses in Pampanga
articles.summary: MABALACAT CITY, Pampanga — Another portion of the tail dike in Minalin, Pampanga collapsed early Thursday morning due to the strong river current. Minalin Mayor Philip Siojo Naguit said part of…

blocks.text: MABALACAT CITY, Pampanga — Another portion of the tail dike in Minalin, Pampanga collapsed early Thursday morning due to the strong river current.
Minalin Mayor Philip Siojo Naguit said part of the San Fernando-Sto. Tomas-Minalin Tail Dike at Barangay San Nicolas is now impassable to all three-wheel and four-wheel vehicles.
In a social media post, the mayor also said only residents on motorcycles who are buying necessities are allowed to pass along the partially damaged tail dike road.
Naguit said the collapsed portion is about 60 meters away from the section of the tail dike at Barangay Sta. Catalina that was breached by raging currents on August 30.
The Sta. Catalina portion of the tail dike is currently being reinforced by the Department of Public Works and Highways to mitigate flooding in affected villages.
Meanwhile, Naguit appealed to boat owners and helmsmen fetching passengers in deeply flooded areas of his town to be more considerate in charging fees.

“I am making a sincere appeal to boat operators. I know I cannot regulate your rates, but we are in a time when our fellow citizens are struggling financially. I hope you will not raise your charges. I understand you are working to earn a living, but please do not take advantage of the situation,” he said in the vernacular. The mayor did not reveal how much the fees are being contested.
Several Minalin residents who commented on the post lauded the mayor’s appeal.

“Thank you for pointing out the boat fare. It is so expensive. I hope no one takes advantage of the situation because it is heartbreaking to see those who cannot afford the fare forced to wade and walk through the dirty water,” a Minalin resident said./coa

articles.title: Cendaña pushes for budget restoration for Edsa busway system
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Akbayan Party-list Rep. Percival Cendaña on Thursday asked the House of Representatives to restore the budget of the Epifanio delos Santos Avenue (Edsa) bus carousel system for…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Akbayan Party-list Rep. Percival Cendaña on Thursday asked the House of Representatives to restore the budget of the Epifanio delos Santos Avenue (Edsa) bus carousel system for 2027 to help more Filipino commuters in their everyday lives.

During the House committee on appropriations’ briefing on the proposed budget of the Department of Transportation (DOTr) for next year, Cendaña pointed out that the service contracting program (SCP) and fuel subsidy for the Edsa busway were not allotted funding.

When asked of the reasons why, Transport Secretary Giovanni Lopez said that the same programs under the Edsa busway system were also not given budget under the 2026 National Expenditure Program (NEP). He noted that they were just allotted funding afterwards due to the crisis in the Middle East which affected many livelihoods of public utility vehicle (PUVs) drivers.

The national government implemented the SCP earlier this year, where PUVs such as modern and traditional jeepneys and buses were paid corresponding amounts based on plying certain kilometers. The government also extended fuel subsidies worth P12 per liter in response to the rising oil prices for passenger jeepneys and UV Express.
Lopez then said that they were informed that the lack of budget for these programs was due to the limited fiscal space and the agency’s obligation rate of its allocated funding.

“So makikita naman natin yung rason ay talagang sinusolusyonan kaya nakikita naming sanhi ay siguro yung limited fiscal space ng gobyerno at hindi dahil may kakulangan ang DOTr,” Lopez added, noting that the agency’s obligation rate for 2026 already stood at 82.4% as of July 2026.
(We can see that there were solutions, that’s why we can see that the reason was due to limited fiscal space of the government, and not because of DOTr’s shortcoming.)
With this, Cendaña called for the restoration of funding for the Edsa busway system as he emphasized the importance of public transportation to commuters.
“Napakarami sa ating mga kababayan ang umaasa sa public transport para makapasok sa kanilang trabaho at makauwi sa kanilang mga tahanan,” the lawmaker said.
(Many Filipinos depend on public transport to go to work and go home to their loved ones.)
“I hope that the Congress through this committee will not take this budget cut lightly and act to restore the Edsa bus carousel budget and kasama nyo kami para tiyakin ito,” he added.
(I hope that the Congress through this committee will not take this budget cut lightly and act to restore the Edsa bus carousel budget and we are with you to push for this.) /mr

articles.title: Ex-Ateneo coach Baldwin, others to file counter-affidavits at DOJ on Sept. 15
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Resigned Ateneo de Manila University basketball team head coach Tab Baldwin and 11 other respondents in the criminal charge filed by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI)…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Resigned Ateneo de Manila University men’s basketball team head coach Tab Baldwin and 11 other respondents in the reckless imprudence resulting in homicide complaints filed by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) are expected to submit their counter-affidavits on September 15, the Department on Justice (DOJ) said.

Justice Undersecretary Ian Norman Dato said this in a press conference on Thursday as the agency started its preliminary investigation into the drowning that killed Ateneo student-athletes Rene Baterbonia and Divine Adili during a training activity in Dipaculao, Aurora, on June 8.
Dato said the DOJ conducted its first hearing for its preliminary investigation last Monday.
“The second one (hearing) is on September 15, which is the submission of the counter-affidavits of the respondents,” Dato said.
“So it’s an ongoing preliminary investigation,” he added.

It was on July 13 when the NBI Homicide Division recommended that the DOJ file charges of reckless imprudence resulting in homicide against Baldwin, six assistant coaches, and the university’s physical therapist:
