articles.title: Senate to ‘add a little’ to Ombudsman’s proposed P51M secret funds
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Senate finance committee head JV Ejercito said on Thursday that it is worth adding “a little” to the P51 million confidential funds for the Office of the Ombudsman, as proposed…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Senate finance committee head JV Ejercito said on Thursday that it is worth adding “a little” to the P51 million confidential funds for the Office of the Ombudsman, as proposed in the National Expenditure Program for 2027.
Ejercito expressed the sentiment after the panel’s hearing on the Office of the Ombudsman’s budget.

During the proceeding, Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla told lawmakers what would be compromised after the Department of Budget and Management slashed his agency’s budget from its requested P147 million to P51 million.
“If there is any agency that is really worth helping or increasing confidential funds for, I think it is the Office of the Ombudsman,” Ejercito told the media.
“Because as I said, we will confine confidential funds to law enforcement, national security and investigative. And, of course, the Ombudsman is included in the end,” he explained.

Ejercito clarified, however, that the Senate might only be able to add a little more to the P51 million budget for the Ombudsman’s secret funds, and not restore the P147 million funding originally asked by the investigative body.
“We cannot promise that the P147M requested by the Ombudsman will be restored… But we might add a little,” the senator said.
In a separate interview, Remulla said that it will help the Ombudsman so much if its entire P147 million proposal will be granted.
Nevertheless, he said the agency will still be prepared for a different outcome.
The P51 million in confidential funds is only part of the P7.2 billion proposed budget of the Office of the Ombudsman for next year. /apl

articles.title: Indonesian haze blankets Bukidnon skies
articles.summary: VALENCIA CITY, Bukidnon — Residents across Bukidnon have observed a thin haze blanketing the skies since September 1, particularly during sunrise, with authorities confirming Thursday that it was due…

blocks.text: VALENCIA CITY, Bukidnon — Residents across Bukidnon have observed a thin haze blanketing the skies since September 1, particularly during sunrise, with authorities confirming Thursday that it was due to forest and land fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia.

Ejay Zuniga, weather specialist at the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) Mindanao Regional Services Division, confirmed on Thursday morning that cross-equatorial winds from the Southern Hemisphere brought the haze.Zuniga explained that winds originating from Indonesia—where massive forest and peatland fires have been burning for weeks—are drifting toward Visayas and Mindanao.

EMB is an agency under the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR).The DENR-10 station in Cagayan de Oro recorded an AQI of 133, which is classified as “Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups.”

EMB-10 officially attributed the deteriorating air quality to transboundary smoke from forest and land fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia.In response, the Department of Health (DOH) urged the public to take precautionary measures, including wearing masks and limiting strenuous outdoor activities.The DOH advised vulnerable groups—such as children, older adults, pregnant women, and individuals with pre-existing heart or lung conditions—to exercise heightened caution and keep their prescribed medications readily available.Outdoor workers were also advised to take regular indoor breaks.Residents are encouraged to continuously monitor official air quality updates from the DENR-EMB and their respective local government units./coa

articles.title: New musical to give intimate portrait of Marilyn Monroe and Arthur Miller’s marriage
articles.summary:
Misfits Together, by Bastille’s Dan Smith and To Kill a King’s Ralph Pelleymounter, is set amid the 1950s’ ‘red scare’

It was lampooned as the union of the “hourglass” and the “egghead” –…

blocks.text: It was lampooned as the union of the “hourglass” and the “egghead” – the marriage, in the summer of 1956, between Hollywood superstar Marilyn Monroe and Pulitzer-winning playwright Arthur Miller. Now, a new stage musical is to give a nuanced and intimate portrait of that famous relationship, treat each as trailblazers in their own way and reveal parallels between the volatile state of the US during the 50s “red scare” and now.

The production, which opens next autumn at Leicester’s Curve, is called Misfits Together, a reference to the film Miller wrote for Monroe that was released shortly after their divorce in 1961. It is a foray into musical theatre by two indie musicians, Dan Smith of the band Bastille and Ralph Pelleymounter from To Kill a King, who have recorded the score as a studio album. The first track, Oh America, is out on Thursday.

Smith and Pelleymounter had originally envisaged it as a musical about 50s America. They shared their songs with Charlotte Bogard Macleod, who has written the book, and had long been fascinated by the relationship that caught the public’s imagination.

blocks.caption: Arthur Miller, Laurence Olivier and Marilyn Monroe at the Savoy hotel, London, in 1956. Photograph: PA

blocks.text: “I’d always wanted to explore Arthur Miller and how he had this integrity that cut through everything,” she said. “He refused to name names [before the House Un-American Activities Committee] and he stood up at a huge personal cost. When we started doing research, we just couldn’t believe that Marilyn was so central to this. She was supporting him. She had her own production company. And we were thinking, why hasn’t this been talked about or celebrated?” Each empowered the other, she added – “fighting [the anti-communist senator Joe] McCarthy or fighting misogyny”.

Smith said that the musical would deal with how Monroe was pigeonholed. “Here’s a working-class woman who was in foster care and created the persona of Marilyn Monroe and became one of the most successful and known people ever in the world,” he said. “And still at the height of her success and fame, she was constantly questioned and denigrated and patronised.”
Despite her many achievements, Monroe had been “reduced and reduced and reduced” to the image of a bombshell, Pelleymounter said. The musical, he added, would look at how her fame eclipsed Miller’s.

Presented with Tila Arts, Misfits Together will be staged by Curve’s artistic director, Nikolai Foster, who said the company had been watching Monroe’s films for research. He praised her “innate understanding of the art of film-making” and “the craft of acting”. Foster said the musical showed the couple’s lives in such closeup that at times during the workshops they almost forgot that the main characters were two of the 20th century’s most famous cultural figures.

blocks.caption: From left, Curve chief executive Chris Stafford, librettist Charlotte Bogard Macleod, Dan Smith, Ralph Pelleymounter and Curve artistic director Nikolai Foster. Photograph: Phil Tragen

blocks.text: Pelleymounter said he had returned to the phrase “history doesn’t repeat, but it rhymes” throughout their work on the project. Seventy years after the red scare, othering was still being used to create “fear and anger in order to maintain the status quo” in the US, he said. One song written for the musical expresses Miller and film director Elia Kazan’s frustration at “seeing politicians say things on the news that are so blatantly not true, that are manipulative and scaremongering”.

Other famous figures in the musical include Laurence Olivier, Monroe’s co-star in The Prince and the Showgirl. “He says: ‘Stop trying to act, just be sexy,’” said Bogard Macleod. “His one note is: ‘Be sexy!’ He was frustrated with her wanting lots of takes, and she was just trying to get it right. But then when you see the film, she’s the one that shines.”

Smith and Pelleymounter wrote more than three dozen songs for the film and have been whittling them down to under half that number. The pair, longtime friends, “have always loved writing narrative songs and using songwriting to dive into character and story and history and culture”, said Smith. “I want the songs to be epic and instant and nuanced and move the story along, to sweep across history and then zoom into someone’s psychology.”

One song takes surprising inspiration from Eminem’s hit Stan, as it tells an “incredibly complex story via their correspondence”. Pelleymounter said they had also drawn inspiration from famous photos of the pair. “Bicycle rides have definitely made it into at least one song.”

Pelleymounter and Smith will be following in the footsteps of fellow indie musician Passenger (Michael David Rosenberg), who recently had a musical theatre success with the Olivier award-nominated The Unlikely Pilgrimage of Harold Fry. Smith has also written the music and lyrics for Young Romantics, a musical in development whose characters include Mary Shelley and Lord Byron.
Misfits Together will run at Curve’s Studio theatre from 4-25 September 2027.

articles.title: Marcoleta posts bail over alleged violations of law banning gifts to public officials
articles.summary: Senator Rodante Marcoleta posted P90,000 bail Thursday over alleged violations of Presidential Decree (PD) 46 stemming from his acceptance of a P75-million donation while he was an incumbent Sagip…

blocks.text: Published September 3, 2026 2:40pm

Senator Rodante Marcoleta posted P90,000 bail Thursday over alleged violations of Presidential Decree (PD) 46 stemming from his acceptance of a P75-million donation while he was an incumbent Sagip party-list representative.

Marcoleta posted bail before the Sandiganbayan’s Fourth, Sixth and First Divisions, where the three PD 46 cases are pending. The decree prohibits public officials from receiving, directly or indirectly, any gift, present or other form of benefit in the course of their official duties.

This came as the Sandiganbayan Third Division began hearings on Marcoleta’s petition for bail in the P75-million plunder case over alleged unjust enrichment stemming from an undeclared campaign donation.
The P75-million donation is also the subject of the PD 46 charges filed against Marcoleta and three others: former Anakalusugan party-list Rep. Michael Defensor, Joseph Espiritu, and Aristotle Viray.
However, since Marcoleta still has a pending plunder case, a non-bailable offense, he will remain detained at the New Quezon City Jail. — VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Indonesian haze blankets Bukidnon skies
articles.summary: VALENCIA CITY, Bukidnon — Residents across Bukidnon have observed a thin haze blanketing the skies since September 1, particularly during sunrise, with authorities confirming Thursday that it was due…

blocks.text: VALENCIA CITY, Bukidnon — Residents across Bukidnon have observed a thin haze blanketing the skies since September 1, particularly during sunrise, with authorities confirming Thursday that it was due to forest and land fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia.

Ejay Zuniga, weather specialist at the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) Mindanao Regional Services Division, confirmed on Thursday morning that cross-equatorial winds from the Southern Hemisphere brought the haze.Zuniga explained that winds originating from Indonesia—where massive forest and peatland fires have been burning for weeks—are drifting toward Visayas and Mindanao.

EMB is an agency under the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR).The DENR-10 station in Cagayan de Oro recorded an AQI of 133, which is classified as “Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups.”

EMB-10 officially attributed the deteriorating air quality to transboundary smoke from forest and land fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia.In response, the Department of Health (DOH) urged the public to take precautionary measures, including wearing masks and limiting strenuous outdoor activities.The DOH advised vulnerable groups—such as children, older adults, pregnant women, and individuals with pre-existing heart or lung conditions—to exercise heightened caution and keep their prescribed medications readily available.Outdoor workers were also advised to take regular indoor breaks.Residents are encouraged to continuously monitor official air quality updates from the DENR-EMB and their respective local government units./coa

articles.title: Nepal sent alert 38 minutes after glacier collapse. It wasn’t enough
articles.summary: KATHMANDU — Nima Dorje Tamang was in Hakubesi, a hamlet south of Syafrubesi in Rasuwa, when the flood struck. Before Tamang could prepare, he heard a thunderous roar and saw the flood gushing…

blocks.text: KATHMANDU — Nima Dorje Tamang was in Hakubesi, a hamlet south of Syafrubesi in Rasuwa, when the flood struck. Before Tamang could prepare, he heard a thunderous roar and saw the flood gushing toward him, its waves taller than him.

Tamang and his family ran uphill for their lives but the waves caught him and a rock struck his leg, fracturing it. Swept into the river, he managed to grab a tree near the bank and clung to it for what felt like two hours until his father and his brother came to rescue him. For the next 24 hours, he said he slipped in and out of consciousness before a helicopter brought him to Kathmandu.

At the orthopedic inpatient ward of Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital, Tamang told the doctors, “Even the air makes it hurt,” when they pressed his left foot. It was still swollen after the surgery. But from his hospital bed, Tamang worried about his family back home. “We lost our uncle, aunt, sister, and brother-in-law,” he said. “And everyone says there will be a massive flood again.”

Like Tamang, communities and authorities were caught off guard when the glacier collapsed at 8:37 AM on August 26. Scientists say the likelihood of predicting this particular type of disaster was minimal, and the resulting flash flood surged so rapidly through the steep mountain terrain that there was little time to warn communities downstream. But the disaster exposed a deeper problem: Nepal’s warning systems remain largely designed around individual hazards, while disasters in the Hindu Kush Himalaya are becoming increasingly complex, cascading and transboundary.

“There is no such thing as an early warning system in Nepal. Simply having sensors does not mean it’s a system; it has to be much more comprehensive,” said Anil Pokhrel, former chief executive of National Disaster Risk Reduction & Management Authority (NDRRMA), stressing the word “system.” For it to be a system, it needed to have a proper assessment of who and what is at risk, he said, then an observation system to anticipate hazards in real time, a comprehensive communications plan for timely alerts, and preparedness for emergencies.
“If the Chinese sensors detect something upstream, a series of sirens should automatically go off all at once. Text messages should go off with a loud buzzer even if it is on silent mode,” he added.

Over the last decade, Pokhrel said Nepal had invested a lot on the observation side, installing sensors. Without multiple sets of sensors monitoring different hazards across different locations, as we saw with Rasuwa floods, it is inadequate to save lives.

When the massive glacial collapse hit the Lhende valley, near the Nepal-Tibet border, Nepal’s Department of Mines and Geology recorded seismic activity. “Our records showed a 4.4 magnitude. But the frequency of the seismic activity did not match that of an earthquake, which is the department’s monitoring mandate, so we did not alert the public like we usually do,” said Lok Vijay Adhikari, chief of National Earthquake Monitoring and Research Center in the Department of Mines and Geology. The US Geological Survey also initially recorded the event at magnitude 4.4, but later revised its assessment, attributing the seismic activity to the glacial collapse.

In the minutes that followed, rising water levels in Bhotekoshi in Rasuwa could potentially have provided another opportunity to alert the public. It was the same Lhende Khola, a transboundary high-altitude river that originates in Gyirong County in Tibet and flows toward the Nepal border, feeding into Bhotekoshi as well as Trishuli downstream. But at 8:50 AM, the flash flood swept away the gauge in the Bhotekoshi river in Rasuwa, at the Syabrubesi hydrological station. Designed to detect gradual rises in the rivers, the gauges were ill-equipped to detect the high-speed flood.
Who knows what to do with the warnings

Twenty-three minutes later, the District Administrative Officer in Rasuwa informed the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology (DHM) about the flash flood. “We informed DHM at nine. We could not do much in Rasuwa because the flood had destroyed the [communications] towers, yet local authorities informed communities, and people went from door to door warning each other,” said Shanti Mahat, spokesperson of NDRRMA.
“But for people downstream we used every means to inform them—through text alerts, caller tune, media broadcasts, and police miking,” she added.

Within 15 minutes of receiving the information, at 9:15 AM — 38 minutes after the ice-rock avalanche — people in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, and Chitwan got text alerts that advised them to immediately move to safe, higher ground as water levels in the Bhotekoshi river in Rasuwa had crossed the danger threshold. It also listed hotlines for rescue assistance.

blocks.caption: Nima Dorje Tamang’s mobile phone showing the warning text message he received.

blocks.text: Such alerts are critical in a crisis. Over 95 percent of Nepali adults have mobile phones with data, and it is an effective method even if language and literacy levels may hinder access.
Early warning mechanisms can also be basic, where people are vigilant, spot a danger, inform on time, and those at risk know how to act.

Himanshu Thakkar, coordinator of the South Asia Network on Dams, Rivers & People recalled an incident from the 2021 glacier collapse in Chamoli of Uttarakhand in India, part of the Hindu Kush Himalayan region. “A woman who was on top of a hill saw the flood [in Rishi Ganga] ravaging from a distance and immediately informed her husband, who was working at the hydropower project downstream,” Thakkar said. Her husband initially did not believe her because he could not see the flood. When he finally caught sight of it, he alerted his colleagues, and a group of them ran uphill and survived.

He juxtaposed that with having information about a risk and not knowing how to act on it, referring to the tour guide Ziha Yitie and other mountaineers in Tibet who videographed the slab of glacier falling off of Langtang Lirung Peak. But they did not immediately understand what they were seeing and realized the magnitude of the disaster only after descending down.
Where does accountability lie?

Ultimately, the responsibility for timely warning lies with the state. Nepal already has a bilateral flood-forecasting mechanism with India where the two countries exchange rainfall and river level data. But Nepal is mainly the provider of information, as most of the monitoring stations are in Nepal’s upstream rivers. On the other hand, despite agreements between the two presidents—Xi Jinping and Bidya Devi Bhandari—in 2019, committing to promote cooperation in different fields, including addressing climate change and protecting the environment, seven years on, the countries still do not have even a rudimentary early warning plan.

“There is no protocol. The practice that we have right now is that we cooperate with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to share information,” said Prakash Pokhrel, Geologist at NDRRMA. “Whenever a foreign country is involved, we have to go through the ministry.”

The danger of not having a mandatory protocol, former NDRRMA chief executive Anil Pokhrel warned, is that, “It comes down to the subjective judgement of individuals in authority who may or may not choose to inform.”

After last year’s catastrophic supraglacial flood in the same Bhotekoshi river in Rasuwa, Nepal’s monitoring of that area remained limited. The northern side of Nepal’s mountain range, however, happened to be in a “blind spot” that no one, including Nepal, China, and international geologists, was monitoring.
Asked if the area was a low priority for Nepal, government officials suggested it was easier said than done.

“The terrain above the settlement in Timure is extremely remote and difficult to access,” said Mahat. “While we have monitoring stations at the Bhotekoshi river, setting up stations that provide real-time data farther out has been very challenging. Even now we’re struggling to get images using drones.”
Dinkar Kayastha, information officer at the DHM, says that looking at the resources at their disposal, it is impossible to monitor everything, especially when 20 to 25 percent of Nepal is mountains.
Pointing to the Thame flood of 2024 in the Everest region, Kayastha said, “We saw that even such small glacier lakes, that were not considered threatening, can become devastating.”
As of now, according to him, Nepal has monitored major “high-risk” glacial lakes including Imja Tsho in the Khumbu, Everest region, and Tsho Rolpa in Rolwaling valley of Dolakha.

After last year’s flood in Bhotekoshi, Pokhrel, the geologist at NDRRMA, said they were monitoring potentially dangerous glacial lakes every day using satellite images to identify the risk of glacial lake outburst floods. International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD) has identified 21 potentially dangerous glacier lakes in Nepal across Gandaki, Koshi, and Karnali river basins and mapped 2070 lakes. Their numbers and their size are not absolute; ICIMOD’s research found that as temperatures rise, both the number and size of the lakes are increasing in Nepal.

blocks.caption: Nepal sent its disaster alert 38 minutes after the glacier collapse. It wasn’t enough

blocks.text: Earlier this year in March 2026, ICIMOD also warned that glaciers in the Hindu Kush Himalaya were melting at double the rate since 2000. They warned that catastrophic floods and water uncertainty were testament to the fact that it was a critical decade for the cryosphere, where retreats in certain parts could be irreversible. Yet, out of the 38 glaciers ICIMOD monitored, only seven met the global benchmark, and many in the region remained largely unmonitored.

But Prakash Pokhrel said the same satellite images are far less useful for anticipating a glacier collapse. “Many places look stable. We can’t know from the images how fractures have developed or if weathering has occurred,” he said.
When “Clean & Green” development deepens risks

For Thakkar, the responsibility is also on the investors of the 13 hydropower plants in Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts that were damaged by the floods, disconnecting roughly 431MW, a tenth of its total power, from the national grid.

The Asian Development Bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, and International Finance Corporation were among the major financiers of the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project, while China’s state-owned Exim Bank funded the Upper Trishuli 3A project. The projects also included financing from British International Investment, Korea Development Bank, and Exim Bank of Korea, as well as the Netherlands FMO, OPEC Fund and Canadian Climate Fund.

The Asian Development Bank’s panel of independent experts overseeing the Upper Trishuli-1 project had recommended strengthening the warning system and emergency plan, coordinating alerts with hydropower projects upstream and downstream, and putting evacuation protocols in place for dangerous floods.

blocks.caption: Nima Dorje Tamang receiving treatment at Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital.

blocks.text: “But they don’t do it. It’s complete callousness. There is no accountability in South Asian countries,” said Thakkar. “They [funders] know nobody is going to be held accountable so they just get away with it.”

Thakkar said that hydropower projects can aggravate disaster risks by creating additional vulnerabilities in already fragile Himalayan landscapes through deforestation, tunnelling, blasting, excavation and muck dumping. Dams can also worsen downstream flooding, while reservoirs accumulate silt that can create additional risks. When multiple hydropower projects are built in a cascade, he said, these impacts accumulate and multiply.
Climate change is adding another layer of risk through more intense rainfall, warmer winters, melting glaciers and thawing permafrost.

“Our dishonest EIAs, lack of accountability in governance and non-implementation of basic monitoring, forecasting and implementable disaster management plans is worsening the disaster impacts in river valleys with multiple hydropower projects,” said Thakkar. “By not doing independent post-disaster impact assessments, we have shut the doors for learning any lessons for the future.”

Nepal’s Trishuli river basin alone, which originates in Rasuwa, has 36 hydropower projects in various stages of construction and planning. In Tamang’s village in Hakubesi, he said about eighty percent of the population worked at the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower plant, and the rest of them were children or the elderly.

“We have no choice but to go to Kathmandu or to the Dhunche [headquarters of Rasuwa] for work. But with the hydropower people stayed back. Now all of them are trapped in it, the hydropower is gone, we have nothing,” he said. The government’s latest data shows 639 people remained trapped in Upper Trishuli-1 and Trishuli 3A.
What next?

For Dr. Saswata Sanyal, who is a disaster risk reduction specialist at ICIMOD, people need to understand the changing realities of living in the Hindu Kush region, where the risks we were familiar with yesterday are no longer the same today.

The Rasuwa flood was a testament to the complex interactions of hazards. “Something triggered an ice avalanche that led to flash floods, debris, sediments and boulders,” he said. Relief efforts since the disaster have also been affected by monsoon rains and flood alerts.
“The risks can be further exacerbated by earthquakes or climate change, so we need to understand the complex nature of hazards in the mountains,” he added.

Flood sensors, even if some of them were washed away in the flash floods in the Trishuli river in Galchchi, continued to be critical in monitoring the drastic increase in water levels and warning people. Sanyal suggested that it’s imperative for Nepal to increase those sensors upstream, not just in its own territory, but other countries in the Hindu Kush region should collaborate to do the same.

Pokhrel, the former chief executive of NDRRMA, added that Nepal needs to set up multiple sensors in diverse locations. Even for floods, he suggested, it’s not enough to install sensors in the bridges, and recommended setting them up on top of hills that can detect seismic waves or the rumble of boulders and floods to alert people using sirens.
Sanyal says people need to comprehend the scale of the Hindu Kush region.

“It has around 54,000 glaciers and more than 2000 glacier lakes, and permafrost covering an even larger area,” he said. While it is not possible to track every inch of the region, he suggested prioritizing the monitoring of areas with settlements downstream, with the countries not only sharing data but also working closely with each other.

Similarly, to identify risks in remote mountain areas that are difficult for scientists and government officials to routinely access, Anoop Nautiyal, climate advocate based in Dehradun, Uttarakhand, recommended training local communities on basic glaciology and hazard monitoring. “They are on the frontline dealing with the climate crisis and need to play a central role in prevention and disaster risk reduction.”

But monitoring cannot stop at national borders when the hazards themselves do not. Many disasters across the Hindu Kush Himalaya are transboundary, making regional cooperation critical. Climate activists, scientists, as well as researchers emphasised the importance of tripartite agreements between Nepal, China, and India, as well as bilateral agreements that go beyond non-binding commitments and include mandatory protocols and action plans for timely communication and response. “Every sensor, siren, drill is ultimately to ensure next time more people get a chance to reach safety,” said Sanyal.

Meanwhile, Tamang is worried about his grandparents back at home in Hakubesi. He said they are staying on higher grounds right now, but is concerned that they will soon run out of the limited food they have.

“Rescue, relief, everything reaches very late in our village. I don’t know why. There are still 100 to 200 people waiting with no rescue,” he said, showing his mobile phone, which showed that he received the warning text message at 9:42 AM. “I wish they would take them to Dhunche, because I hear there will be another massive flood; perhaps the water won’t reach as high.” /dl

articles.title: El Niño to be ‘very strong,’ last until February, UN warns
articles.summary: GENEVA — El Niño is set to become “very strong” in the months ahead, with the weather phenomenon near certain to persist through to February, the United Nations’ climate agency warned Thursday.…

blocks.text: GENEVA — El Niño is set to become “very strong” in the months ahead, with the weather phenomenon near certain to persist through to February, the United Nations’ climate agency warned Thursday.
The World Meteorological Organization said El Niño would peak toward the end of this year, though its knock-on impacts on the climate will continue well into 2027.

“El Niño is firmly established and will intensify into a very strong event in the coming months, with big impacts on rainfall and temperature patterns and associated risks of floods, drought and extreme heat,” the WMO said.
El Niño is a natural climate phenomenon and is not caused by climate change.
But scientists expect it will exacerbate the heat of a planet already warming from burning fossil fuels, while amping up weather extremes.
“El Niño is being supersized before our eyes,” said UN chief Antonio Guterres.

“The science leaves no room for doubt: the planet is in uncharted waters, and those waters are heating up. Sea surface temperatures are rising, temperatures keep climbing, and the world is in the danger zone of extreme weather.
“The race now is between rising risks and our commitment to take climate action and protect people. We must win that race.”
‘Massive blow’ to economies
El Niño tends to peak late in the year, but heat in the oceans releases more slowly into the atmosphere, pushing up global temperatures the following year.
The hottest year on record is 2024, following the last El Niño.
“This exceptional El Niño… has the potential to deliver a massive blow to communities and economies across the world,” said WMO chief Celeste Saulo.
“We are already seeing disruption and devastation from droughts and floods, and we expect these impacts to increase as El Niño intensifies.”
She put disaster management authorities and climate-sensitive sectors like agriculture, health, energy and water on notice, saying there was “no time to lose” in getting ready.
El Niño warms surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean, bringing worldwide changes in winds, pressure and rainfall patterns.
It typically takes place every two to seven years and lasts around nine to 12 months.
Conditions oscillate between El Niño and its opposite, La Niña, with neutral conditions in between.
“Fuelled by exceptionally warm ocean conditions across the tropical Pacific, El Niño is expected to strengthen further during the coming months to a very strong intensity,” the WMO said.
The UN agency classifies El Niño events as weak, moderate, strong or very strong, meaning it is set to reach the highest level out of four.
The WMO said there was an “exceptionally high likelihood of nearly 100 percent” that El Niño will continue through to February.
Pacific Ocean heating up
El Niño can reshape weather and climate patterns thousands of kilometres away from the tropical Pacific.

Every El Niño is different, but major events often follow familiar patterns. This includes drought across parts of the Amazon, Indonesia and Australia, disrupted monsoons in India, and shifting rainfall throughout the tropics.

For September-November, WMO forecasts indicate an increased likelihood of above-normal temperatures “across almost all land areas,” alongside rainfall patterns showing a “pronounced and classic atmospheric response to the strong Pacific El Niño,” the UN’s weather and climate agency said.
The index which measures sea surface temperature anomalies in the central eastern equatorial Pacific has strengthened from an average 1.5C above normal between May and July.
Weekly values between late July and mid-August ranged from around 2.2C to 2.6C above average, indicating continued El Niño intensification.
In some areas, subsurface ocean temperatures were more than 8C above average during July and early August. /dl

articles.title: P162M in ‘high-grade marijuana’ seized from yacht at Subic Freeport
articles.summary: OLONGAPO CITY — High-grade marijuana, often called “kush,” worth P162.2 million was seized from a yacht docked at the Subic Bay Yacht Club (SBYC) inside the Subic Bay Freeport on…

blocks.text: OLONGAPO CITY — High-grade marijuana, often called “kush,” worth P162.2 million was seized from a yacht docked at the Subic Bay Yacht Club (SBYC) inside the Subic Bay Freeport on Wednesday night, the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) confirmed on Thursday.

The illegal drugs were discovered hidden aboard Sailing Yacht (SY) “Lindsy” during a boarding and dismantling operation conducted by a composite team of the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA), the Coast Guard, and the Bureau of Customs (BOC).

Authorities were tipped off about the contraband on Sept. 1 after mechanics repairing the yacht’s generator and engine reportedly discovered the hidden compartment containing suspected illegal substances, according to a report from the PCG Intelligence Unit (CGIU) in Zambales.

The yacht had arrived at SBYC on Aug. 28 from Thailand and was bound for Taiwan when it experienced engine trouble. Authorities have yet to disclose the identity and whereabouts of the yacht’s owner or any other persons linked to the vessel.
On Wednesday, CGIU Zambales and Coast Guard Sub-Station Olongapo personnel conducted covert verification of the vessel while BOC and PDEA personnel prepared for boarding and inspection at 7 p.m.
The operating team seized approximately 89 kilos or packs of suspected kush. The team brought the confiscated items to the SBYC boathouse for inventory.

The CGS Zambales also served as a blocking force aboard a Philippine Coast Guard Auxiliary rigid-hull inflatable boat during the seaborne operation. It later provided security escort during the transport of the seized items.
As of 1:06 a.m. on Thursday, BOC and PDEA personnel were continuing the inventory of the confiscated marijuana. BOC turned over the drugs to PDEA for proper disposition and disposal. /coa

articles.title: Korea sees surge in suicide-encouraging content, most posts not deleted
articles.summary: SEOUL — More than 600,000 reports of online content that could encourage or facilitate suicide were filed in South Korea last year, but 7 in 10 remained online at the end of the year,…

blocks.text: SEOUL — More than 600,000 reports of online content that could encourage or facilitate suicide were filed in South Korea last year, but 7 in 10 remained online at the end of the year, government data showed Wednesday.

The Health Ministry received 602,781 reports of what Korean law defines as “suicide-inducing information” in 2025, according to data provided to Rep. Seo Mi-hwa of the ruling Democratic Party of Korea and first reported by Seoul Shinmun.
The category includes posts seeking suicide partners, content encouraging suicide and information on obtaining or using potentially lethal materials.
The number of reports has more than quadrupled from 142,725 in 2021. In 2025, only 176,163 of the reported items, or 29.2 percent, had been removed by year-end.
Social media accounted for 525,643 reports, with X responsible for 99.9 percent of them.
Online communities had the lowest removal rate. Of the 73,036 reports involving community posts, only 4,132, or 5.7 percent, resulted in removal.

The government had only one official dedicated to monitoring such content through 2024. Staffing was increased to four in September 2025, while the annual budget rose from 30 million won ($21,900) in 2024 to 207 million won this year.
The removal rate improved to 45.1 percent in the first half of this year, but more than half of reported content remained online.

Beginning Nov. 12, online platforms will be required to immediately remove or block suicide-inducing information they identify and restrict its search and transmission. The government also plans to introduce round-the-clock monitoring using artificial intelligence. /dl

If you or someone you know is in need of assistance, please reach out to the National Center for Mental Health (NCMH). Their crisis hotlines are available at 1553 (Luzon-wide landline toll-free), 0917-899-USAP (8727), 0966-351-4518, and 0908-639-2672. For more information, visit their website: (https://doh.gov.ph/NCMH-Crisis-Hotline)

Alternatively, you can contact Hopeline PH at the following numbers: 0917-5584673, 0918-8734673, 88044673. Additional resources are available at ngf-mindstrong.org, or connect with them on Facebook at Hopeline PH.

articles.title: 5 arrested in Bataan drug bust
articles.summary: ORION, Bataan- Five people, including a jobless woman, were arrested by the Orion police after a buy-bust operation conducted at an undisclosed remote village here on Wednesday night. The arrest of…

blocks.text: ORION, Bataan- Five people, including a jobless woman, were arrested by the Orion police after a buy-bust operation conducted at an undisclosed remote village here on Wednesday night.
The arrest of the suspects was undertaken after a week-long surveillance of the barangay where the rampant sale of shabu (crystal methamphetamine) had been going on, police said.
Authorities are set to conduct more operations are set to be conducted in the adjacent barangay where the five suspects were arrested.
Seized during the operation were 19.38 grams of shabu with a street value of P131,784 and the marked money used by police agents belonging to the Orion police drug enforcement unit.
The suspects are now detained at the Orion police custodial facility and are facing charges for violation of the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002./coa

articles.title: Charles Perrottet repeatedly denies taking payments from developer for political outcomes in Icac hearing
articles.summary: Brother of the former premier says he lied to developer Jean Nassif about doing political work for him and rejects accusation he is fabricating evidence

blocks.text: Charles Perrottet has repeatedly denied taking payments from the property developer Jean Nassif to achieve political outcomes for him, telling a corruption inquiry he cannot explain a message sent after a Nassif development was refused, which said: “Charles fucked this whole thing.”

Charles, the brother of former New South Wales premier Dominic Perrottet, has previously told the Independent Commission Against Corruption he would lie to Nassif about doing political work for him. On Thursday, he said he may also have regularly lied to close friend Christian Ellis, who is named in Icac’s allegations. He rejected the accusation he was fabricating evidence to Icac.

As part of its inquiry into alleged corruption in the NSW Liberals, Icac is investigating the allegation that conservative factional figures Charles Perrottet, Jeremy Greenwood and Ellis received prohibited donations totalling $2m from Nassif or his company Toplace between 2020 and 2023 in exchange for political outcomes, as well as the recruitment or renewal of members to the Liberal party, a practice known as branch stacking. Branch stacking is not itself illegal.
Ellis is overseas and has not responded to Icac, while Greenwood will appear before the commission next week.

Charles Perrottet has previously said he would regularly mislead Nassif, adding a “political flavour” to advice in order to chase up payments for genuine lobbying work by Beckington, a company controlled by Ellis and Greenwood.

On Thursday, the commission heard an exchange sent by Greenwood to Ellis in April 2020, expressing concern about losing Toplace as a client when Nassif’s Cherrybrook development proposal was refused after the Hills shire council did not support it. Charles Perrottet said he did not know what the message – in which Greenwood wrote “Charles fucked this whole thing” – meant.

He was asked about a subsequent exchange between him and Ellis in which he detailed steps to assist with Toplace developments, including a call he wrote he would make to the NSW Liberal MP and former Hills shire councillor Robyn Preston.

On Thursday, Charles Perrottet said he could not recall calling Preston. The counsel assisting, Peggy Dwyer SC, asked if he would “regularly lie to Christian Ellis at that time to tell him you were doing some things and not others?”
“I may have,” said Charles Perrottet, suggesting it might have been “to sound supportive”.

Dwyer, noting he had also said he would lie to Nassif, suggested that “actually the fabrication is the evidence you’re giving to the commission because you want to make it sound like you didn’t take the active steps that are clearly set out in this text”.
“No,” said Charles Perrottet.

Later, he was asked about a message from Greenwood to the Toplace executive Sharangan Maheswaran, also named in Icac’s allegations, in 2021, asking for payment from Nassif, or “Charles is just going to cut the relationship”. After Maheswaran offered to pass on the message, Greenwood expressed concern that Nassif might see it as a threat.

“Most certainly, but sometimes JN [Jean Nassif] gives into threats,” Maheswaran wrote back. Greenwood wrote that he wanted Nassif to understand that “yes, sure, we’re all friends, but Charles can’t keep exhausting the capital he has, which he gets on the back of other people’s work in the faction … while then having to make excuses because our agreements weren’t honoured”.
Maheswaran, who is named in a separate allegation, has previously denied any wrongdoing. He will appear before Icac next week.

Under repeated questioning from Dwyer, Charles Perrottet rejected the suggestion it was “clear as day … that Mr Greenwood shared your view, as expressed to Jean Nassif, that he had to hand over the money in order to achieve the political outcomes”.
after newsletter promotion
‘Meeting of the minds’

On Thursday, Charles Perrottet was asked about a 2020 meeting to discuss the recruitment of conservative right members amid a factional fight with centre-right Liberals to take over branches in the Hills shire. He said he supported the plan “to have more balance” in branches, but repeatedly rejected that Nassif was financially supporting branch stacking efforts.

The inquiry has previously heard Charles Perrottet created a group chat called “Back to Basics” in August 2020, adding his brothers Dominic and Jean-Claude Perrottet, Damien Tudehope, Ellis and two other conservative faction members.

“Gents, I believe it’s time for a WPH [West Pennant Hills] meeting of the minds. Lots has been going on, and some concerning developments this week in both the left and right has accelerated the need for us to get together and discuss,” he wrote. “This group share the same values.”

Charles Perrottet was asked about an agenda he shared with the group before the meeting at Tudehope’s West Pennant Hills home, including the item “Staffing support or new models to ensure progress and open discussion”. The day after the September 2020 meeting, Ellis provided an update to the group saying the “short-term goals” moving forward included “private clients for retainers for staff”.

Charles Perrottet rejected the suggestion that his first message was setting the agenda for a potential plan for private individuals to pay retainers to support branch stacking efforts, saying it “may have been a point of discussion that Christian wanted to raise at the meeting”.

The commission heard that the day after Ellis’s message, $148,500 was deposited via cheque from Toplace to Beckington. Charles Perrottet said the timing of the payment was a “coincidence”, “unless you speak to Christian [Ellis] and ask him”.

After Dwyer said that Ellis was in the UK and had chosen not to participate in hearings, Charles Perrottet said: “I’m aware. I’m not sure he hasn’t chosen to participate. I’m aware he’s in the UK. If you can’t ask him, I would ask Jeremy.”

Tudehope, who gave evidence to the inquiry in its second week, told the commission he could not recall the meeting or what the reference to private clients meant. Dominic Perrottet is not named as a person of interest in Icac’s allegations and is not accused of any wrongdoing.

Nassif, who fled Australia for Lebanon in 2022, has withdrawn from an expected appearance via video link on Friday after providing Icac with a medical certificate. He has previously denied any wrongdoing.
Icac’s inquiry continues.

articles.title: US: New York City Mayor Mamdani announces ban on AI for younger students
articles.summary: New York City is barring elementary and middle school students from using generative AI tools this school year. Meanwhile AI literacy classes and supervised pilot programs will be rolled out for high…

image.caption: Mamdani said AI-powered early education is not inevitableImage: NDZ/STAR MAX/IPx/picture alliance

blocks.text: New York City public schools will temporarily bar elementary and middle school students from using generative artificial intelligence tools during the upcoming school year, Mayor Zohran Mamdani said on Wednesday.
Officials have described this as the most expansive such prohibition in the United States.
What do we know about the AI ban?

The one-year moratorium bars student-facing generative AI software for students through eighth grade, affecting roughly 600,000 public school students, while officials study how children use the technology.
The city said the policy will halt use of about 40 educational AI tools currently used in classrooms.. Companion chatbots will be banned across all grade levels.

However, high schoolers will be exempt from the full ban. The city will roll out twice-yearly AI literacy classes for all public high school students and launch pilot programs letting some use select AI platforms under teacher supervision.
Teachers, meanwhile, will still be permitted to use AI for lesson planning and administrative tasks such as scheduling.
What did Mayor Mamdani say about the restrictions?

Mamdani framed the decision around the value of human connection in education: "Children need teachers and human connection in order to learn and grow. They need to develop skills alongside their peers, build relationships with educators and wrestle with tough problems on their own."

He also tied the policy to the district's broader teaching ideals, saying, "Each day when our children come to school, we teach them to ask questions, to challenge assumptions, to interrogate the premise, to ask why. When it comes to AI in our schools, we hold an obligation to do the same."
New York's move comes as school districts across the country weigh the benefits and risks of generative AI in classrooms.
AI knows what you did last summer
Is New York alone in banning AI?

One of the largest examples is Los Angeles Unified, the US's second-largest school district, which is also temporarily blocking generative AI tools on student devices across all grades as it develops a formal policy this school year. LAUSD had already banned devices before second grade and set screen-time limits as part of a broader policy adopted in June.
Like Los Angeles, New York is pairing AI restrictions with broader limits on technology use.

New York's new plan also includes recommended screen time limits – a cap of 30 minutes daily for grades three to five and 45 minutes for grades six to eight. The plan also calls for a citywide review of education technology tools to eliminate those deemed nonessential to learning.
At least 37 states already have some form of official AI guidance for schools, according to the Associated Press, but no consistent national standard exists for AI literacy instruction.
What has the reaction been?

Reactions from education and advocacy groups were mixed. Michael Mulgrew, president of the United Federation of Teachers, welcomed the screen time limits but said the AI policy "leaves many questions unanswered," including how the Education Department will ensure the tools it purchases include adequate safeguards, AP reported.
Landmark lawsuit against Meta kicks off in the US

Josh Golin, executive director of the children's advocacy group Fairplay, told AP he wanted a longer moratorium and more lead time before the school year began, adding that AI platforms should have to "demonstrate that their products are effective at teaching kids, that they're safe, that they're not displacing face-to-face interaction and that they're not leading to rampant cheating."
"A year to evaluate is not nearly enough time," he said.
New York City's roughly 1 million public school students return to classrooms next week.

articles.title: Ombudsman to form special team vs 'basura kings' nationwide
articles.summary: The Office of the Ombudsman will create a special investigative team to look into alleged corruption in garbage collection and waste management contracts nationwide, Ombudsman Jesus Crispin “Boying”…

blocks.text: Published September 3, 2026 2:27pm

The Office of the Ombudsman will create a special investigative team to look into alleged corruption in garbage collection and waste management contracts nationwide, Ombudsman Jesus Crispin “Boying” Remulla said during the Senate Finance Committee’s deliberations on the agency’s proposed 2027 budget.
The move followed a discussion on alleged irregularities in local government waste management, with Remulla describing individuals who control garbage-hauling operations as “basura kings.”
“May mga character tayo sa society na basura king. The big haulers are basura kings, Your Honor, and they’re here in Manila, in Metro Manila, in Manila, City of Manila, everywhere.”
(There are characters in society who are ‘basura kings.’ The big haulers are ‘basura kings,’ Your Honor, and they are here in Manila, Metro Manila, Manila City, and everywhere.)
Remulla said the Ombudsman would examine how garbage collection and waste management contracts are handled by local governments, particularly where large amounts of public funds are involved.
‘Basura’ contracts under scrutiny
Remulla pointed to the structure of garbage collection as an area that could be vulnerable to corruption, saying waste management involves substantial local government budgets.
“Kasi ang budget for basura ay so big that it can blind a lot of people into just making money out of it.”
(The budget for garbage is so large that it can tempt many people to simply make money from it.)
He said the problem is not limited to Metro Manila and confirmed that the planned investigative effort would cover local governments nationwide.

Asked whether the Ombudsman would have personnel specifically tasked to identify how local officials and contractors allegedly profit from garbage operations, Remulla said: “We will create a special investigative team for this, Your Honor. We will do it.”
(We will create a special investigative team for this, Your Honor. We will do it.)
The Ombudsman did not provide details during the hearing on the team’s composition, timeline or the specific local government units that would initially be covered.
Garbage problem goes beyond collection
Remulla also raised concerns over the implementation of the country’s waste-management system, saying the Department of Environment and Natural Resources should have a greater role.
He said garbage collection begins at the local government level but that other steps, including waste segregation and proper sanitary landfills, are often not followed.

“The tragedy, Your Honor, is that the work of the DENR is never started or finished because the garbage hauling begins with local government and nothing is followed: segregation, proper sanitary landfills, everything becomes upside.”

(The tragedy, Your Honor, is that the work of the DENR is never started or finished because garbage hauling begins with local governments, but the succeeding requirements are not followed—segregation, proper sanitary landfills, everything.)
Remulla said garbage is instead brought to contracted disposal sites, creating opportunities for large sums of money to circulate through waste-management contracts.
He added that the issue was something he had encountered in politics and described the alleged network of large garbage haulers as existing not only in Metro Manila but across the country.
Ombudsman previously urged mayors to check waste contracts
Remulla had earlier called on mayors to scrutinize offices under their supervision for possible corruption involving garbage collection and waste management contracts.
He also urged the public to report irregularities involving local officials and government offices to the Ombudsman and the Anti-Red Tape Authority (ARTA).

The Ombudsman has emphasized that allegations must be investigated and supported by evidence before cases are filed. Its broader anti-corruption campaign has also included intensified field investigations into infrastructure and flood-control projects. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: Over 500,000 hectares of land handed out to tillers, DAR says
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – More than 500,000 hectares of farmlands has been distributed to beneficiaries ever since President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. took office in 2022, Agrarian Reform Secretary Conrado…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – More than 500,000 hectares of farmlands has been distributed to beneficiaries ever since President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. took office in 2022, Agrarian Reform Secretary Conrado Estrella III said on Thursday.

During the deliberations on the the proposed 2027 budget of the Department of Agrarian Reform (DAR), Estrella told members of the House of Representatives committee on appropriations that his agency had distributed 410,179 titles covering 556,088 hectares to 376,738 agrarian reform beneficiaries identified.
“The years 2022 to 2026 may aptly be described as banner years for the Department of Agrarian Reform,” Estrella told lawmakers.

From the January to August 2026 period, DAR distributed 16,032 titles covering 23,574 hectares to 14,032 beneficiaries. In 2025, the agency had apportioned 199,838 titles over 23,574 hectares to 176,202 farmers, according to its presentation.
In 2024, 88,310 farmers received 102,546 land titles over 120,772 hectares of land. The agency gave away 69,897 titles for 84,044 hectares to 73,399 beneficiaries in 2023.
In the first year of President Ferdinand Marcos, Jr.’s government, DAR released 21,876 titles over 25,159 hectares to 24,804 farmers, based on the presentation.
Land reform is a contentious issue in the Philippines, a traditionally agricultural nation where vestiges of Spanish colonial land ownership have been inherited and sustained across decades.
About 5.4 million hectares of land were earmarked for distribution to farmers under the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform law, which aimed to reduce inequality by diffusing farmlands to tillers. /mr

articles.title: Witness: Marcoleta told Comelec P75-M he got from donors was his 'personal fund'
articles.summary: Senator Rodante Marcoleta said the P75 million donation he got from three individuals in 2025, the subject of the plunder charge against him, is part of his personal funds, a Commission on Elections…

blocks.text: Published September 3, 2026 2:25pm

Senator Rodante Marcoleta said the P75 million donation he got from three individuals in 2025, the subject of the plunder charge against him, is part of his personal funds, a Commission on Elections (Comelec) official said.

Atty. Victoria Kadeja Besinio of the Commission on Elections (Comelec) Political Finance and Affairs Department, a witness for the prosecution, made the testimony during Day 1 of the hearing on the petition for bail filed by Marcoleta.

"With regard to his verified position paper, Senator Marcoleta said that those funds were received by him in his personal capacity, and so they became part of his personal funds, and that those funds were not earmarked or restricted for purposes of the campaign, and that they were received by him prior to the campaign," Besinio said during the questioning of Sandiganbayan Third Division Associate Justice Ronald Moreno.
"That is what he stated in his position paper," Besinio added.
Besinio also testified that the Comelec did not make a determination as to the nature of the P75 million donation received by Marcoleta from three donors.

Marcoleta and the three individuals who donated such an amount to him, namely former Anakalusugan party-list Rep. Michael Defensor, Joseph Espiritu, and Aristotle Viray, are all facing a P75 million plunder charge over Marcoleta's undeclared P75 million worth of campaign donations.
They are also facing separate charges of violation of Presidential Decree 46, which prohibits public officials from receiving gifts.
When Marcoleta received the donation, he was an incumbent Sagip party-list representative.
Prior to the start of the bail hearing, Moreno also said that the P75 million plunder charge filed by government prosecutors against Marcoleta is a valid criminal information.

Moreno made the clarification during the hearing on Marcoleta's motion asking the anti-graft court to defer its issuance of a 90-day suspension order on Marcoleta pending a P75 million plunder charge against him over undeclared campaign donations.

"If there is no valid information, how come the court found that probable cause exist, thus the issuance of warrant of arrest [against Marcoleta]? Otherwise, we would have dismissed the case outright," Moreno said after Marcoleta's defense team repeatedly said that their motion to withhold the issuance of suspension order was filed since there is no valid criminal information against Marcoleta.
"If there is no probable cause, then then we have the obligation to dismiss the case outright," Moreno added.

Marcoleta's counsels then said that their contention that there is no valid information is due to the Sandiganbayan's lack of jurisdiction, saying that the matter is within the purview of the Commission on Elections.

Moreno then pointed out that Marcoleta's camp has argued in its motion to withhold suspension order and dismiss the case that he should not be suspended because the Ombudsman's allegations do not constitute the offense of plunder. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: El Niño to be ‘very strong,’ last until February, UN warns
articles.summary: GENEVA — El Niño is set to become “very strong” in the months ahead, with the weather phenomenon near certain to persist through to February, the United Nations’ climate agency warned Thursday.…

blocks.text: GENEVA — El Niño is set to become “very strong” in the months ahead, with the weather phenomenon near certain to persist through to February, the United Nations’ climate agency warned Thursday.
The World Meteorological Organization said El Niño would peak toward the end of this year, though its knock-on impacts on the climate will continue well into 2027.

“El Niño is firmly established and will intensify into a very strong event in the coming months, with big impacts on rainfall and temperature patterns and associated risks of floods, drought and extreme heat,” the WMO said.
El Niño is a natural climate phenomenon and is not caused by climate change.
But scientists expect it will exacerbate the heat of a planet already warming from burning fossil fuels, while amping up weather extremes.
“El Niño is being supersized before our eyes,” said UN chief Antonio Guterres.

“The science leaves no room for doubt: the planet is in uncharted waters, and those waters are heating up. Sea surface temperatures are rising, temperatures keep climbing, and the world is in the danger zone of extreme weather.
“The race now is between rising risks and our commitment to take climate action and protect people. We must win that race.”
‘Massive blow’ to economies
El Niño tends to peak late in the year, but heat in the oceans releases more slowly into the atmosphere, pushing up global temperatures the following year.
The hottest year on record is 2024, following the last El Niño.
“This exceptional El Niño… has the potential to deliver a massive blow to communities and economies across the world,” said WMO chief Celeste Saulo.
“We are already seeing disruption and devastation from droughts and floods, and we expect these impacts to increase as El Niño intensifies.”
She put disaster management authorities and climate-sensitive sectors like agriculture, health, energy and water on notice, saying there was “no time to lose” in getting ready.
El Niño warms surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean, bringing worldwide changes in winds, pressure and rainfall patterns.
It typically takes place every two to seven years and lasts around nine to 12 months.
Conditions oscillate between El Niño and its opposite, La Niña, with neutral conditions in between.
“Fuelled by exceptionally warm ocean conditions across the tropical Pacific, El Niño is expected to strengthen further during the coming months to a very strong intensity,” the WMO said.
The UN agency classifies El Niño events as weak, moderate, strong or very strong, meaning it is set to reach the highest level out of four.
The WMO said there was an “exceptionally high likelihood of nearly 100 percent” that El Niño will continue through to February.
Pacific Ocean heating up
El Niño can reshape weather and climate patterns thousands of kilometres away from the tropical Pacific.

Every El Niño is different, but major events often follow familiar patterns. This includes drought across parts of the Amazon, Indonesia and Australia, disrupted monsoons in India, and shifting rainfall throughout the tropics.

For September-November, WMO forecasts indicate an increased likelihood of above-normal temperatures “across almost all land areas,” alongside rainfall patterns showing a “pronounced and classic atmospheric response to the strong Pacific El Niño,” the UN’s weather and climate agency said.
The index which measures sea surface temperature anomalies in the central eastern equatorial Pacific has strengthened from an average 1.5C above normal between May and July.
Weekly values between late July and mid-August ranged from around 2.2C to 2.6C above average, indicating continued El Niño intensification.
In some areas, subsurface ocean temperatures were more than 8C above average during July and early August. /dl

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Resigned Ateneo de Manila University basketball team head coach Tab Baldwin and 11 other respondents in the criminal charge filed by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) are expected to submit their counter-affidavits on September 15.
The information comes from Justice Undersecretary Ian Norman Dato in a press conference at the Department of Justice (DOJ) on Thursday.
The NBI previously filed reckless imprudence resulting in homicide complaints at the DOJ against the dozen accused.

Dato told reporters in the press forum that the DOJ started its preliminary investigation on the drowning that killed Ateneo student-athletes Rene Baterbonia and Divine Adili during a training in Dipaculao, Aurora on June 8.
Dato said the department conducted its first hearing last Monday as part of its preliminary investigation.
“The second one (hearing) is on September 15, which is the submission of the counter-affidavits of the respondents,” the justice official said.
“So, it’s an ongoing preliminary investigation,” he added.

It was on July 13 when the NBI Homicide Division recommended that the DOJ file in court charges of reckless imprudence resulting in homicide against Baldwin, six assistant coaches, and the university’s physical therapist:

articles.title: Elderly American, wife shot dead in Dumaguete home invasion
articles.summary: Cebu City, Philippines — A 72-year-old American citizen and his 71-year-old Filipino wife were found dead after an apparent home invasion in Barangay Bajumpandan, Dumaguete City, early Wednesday…

blocks.text: Cebu City, Philippines — A 72-year-old American citizen and his 71-year-old Filipino wife were found dead after an apparent home invasion in Barangay Bajumpandan, Dumaguete City, early Wednesday morning, September 2, 2026.
Negros Oriental police identified the victims as Mark Duell and Elsie Duell and activated Special Investigation Task Group (SITG) “DUELL” following the fatal robbery.
Dumaguete home invasion

The couple, who had been married for 10 years and split their time traveling in and out of the country, were discovered inside their residence after local emergency services received a distress call around 6:08 a.m.

Police Captain Stephen Polinar, public information officer of the Negros Oriental Police Provincial Office (NOrPPO), stated that the Dumaguete City Police Station responded immediately after receiving the report via a 911 call placed by relatives of the victims.
According to initial statements from the couple’s 53-year-old house helper, two armed men wearing bonnets broke into the residential compound around 4:00 a.m.
The intruders reportedly entered the helper’s quarters first, holding her at gunpoint and tying her up before proceeding into the main living quarters.
Upon entering the main house, responding officers found the body of Elsie Duell in the kitchen area while Mark Duell’s body was found in the living room.
Both victims suffered multiple gunshot wounds.
Authorities are awaiting final post-mortem and autopsy results to confirm the exact number and caliber of rounds fired.
Robbery as motive

Investigators are treating robbery as a key motive after discovering that approximately ₱60,000 ($1,000) in cash, electronic devices, personal belongings, and identification documents were missing from the home.

Because the property lacked CCTV cameras, police units are currently executing a video backtracking operation, reviewing security footage from adjacent properties and surrounding roadways to trace the suspects’ entry and getaway routes.
Two persons of interest
Dumaguete City Police Chief Lt. Col. Don Richmond Conag confirmed that law enforcement has already identified two persons of interest in connection with the crime.
Meanwhile, the house helper remains in police custody as the sole primary witness and has undergone medico-legal examination to document her injuries and corroborate her statements.
SITG “DUELL” continues follow-up operations to establish the full sequence of events, verify all leads, and identify the perpetrators responsible for the double homicide.

articles.summary: More than one in five children aged 12 to 17 across Africa, Asia, Latin America, and Eastern Europe experienced at least one form of sexual abuse or exploitation on online platforms in the year…

items: Approximately 20 million internet-using children across 21 countries experienced sexual exploitation or abuse online in a year, primarily on social media platforms.
